modules.title: Planck's Law
modules.doc:
In this module we define Planck's law for blackbody radiation: The spectral density of
electromagnetic radiation emitted by a black body in thermal equilibrium at a given
temperature T, when there is no net flow of matter or energy between the body and
its environment.

## i. Overview

According to Planck's distribution law, the spectral energy radiance
(per unit frequency) for a black body at given temperature `T` as a function of frequency `ν`
is given by

    `B(ν, T) = 2 h ν³ / c² · 1 / (e^{h ν / (k_B T)} - 1)`

where `h` is Planck's constant, `c` the speed of light, and `k_B` the Boltzmann constant.

and per unit wavelength `λ`, given by

    `B(λ, T) = 2 h c² / λ⁵ · 1 / (e^{h c / (λ k_B T)} - 1)`

The two forms are related by `B(λ, T) = (c / λ²) B(ν = c/λ, T)`
(see `spectralRadianceWave_eq_spectralRadiance`), where the frequency `c / λ`
is given by `Frequency.ofWavelength`. The frequency and wavelength are taken to be
of the types `Frequency` and `Wavelength` from `Physlib.Optics`, i.e. nonnegative
quantities carrying the dimensions of inverse time and of length respectively.

## ii. Key results

- `BlackBody` : Structure representing an idealized black body in thermal equilibrium.
- `spectralRadiance` : The spectral radiance per unit frequency of blackbody radiation,
  as a function of a `Frequency`.
- `spectralRadiance_pos` : The spectral radiance is positive for positive frequency and temperature.
- `spectralRadiance_absZero` : The spectral radiance is 0 at absolute zero.
- `spectralRadianceWave` : Spectral radiance per unit wavelength, as a function of a `Wavelength`.
- `spectralRadianceWave_eq_spectralRadiance` : Correspondence between the two forms,
  via `Frequency.ofWavelength`.
- `firstRadiationConstant` / `secondRadiationConstant` : Radiation constants `c₁L` and `c₂`.
- `spectralRadianceWave_eq_constants` : Planck's law in terms of radiation constants.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The BlackBody structure
- B. Spectral radiance per unit frequency
- C. Spectral radiance per unit wavelength
- D. Correspondence between the two forms
- E. First and second radiation constants

## iv. References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planck%27s_law
* M. Planck, "Ueber das Gesetz der Energieverteilung im Normalspectrum",
  Ann. Phys. 309 (3), 553–563 (1901).

sections.text: ## B. Spectral radiance per unit frequency
## C. Spectral radiance per unit wavelength

## D. Correspondence between the two forms

Since `B(λ, T) dλ = -B(ν(λ), T) dν` with `ν = c / λ` and `|dν / dλ| = c / λ²`,
the wavelength form equals `c / λ²` times the frequency form evaluated at
`ν = c / λ`.

## E. First and second radiation constants

The wavelength variant uses only the combinations `2 h c²` and `h c / kB`,
called the first and second radiation constants.

declarations.name: BlackBody
declarations.doc: An idealized black body in thermal equilibrium at temperature `T`.
declarations.statement:
structure BlackBody where
  /-- The temperature of the black body. -/
  T : Temperature

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance
declarations.doc:
The spectral radiance per unit frequency of blackbody radiation at frequency `ν`
for a black body `B`, speed of light `c` and Boltzmann constant `kB`:

`B(ν, T) = 2 h ν³ / c² · 1 / (e^{h ν / (k_B T)} - 1)`

By the homogeneity and isotropy of blackbody radiation, the spectral radiance
is independent of position and direction, so it depends only on frequency
and temperature.

Extended by zero outside the physical domain `0 < ν`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spectralRadiance (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (ν : Frequency) : ℝ

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance_pos
declarations.doc:
The spectral radiance of blackbody radiation is positive for positive frequency
and positive temperature.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadiance_pos (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) : 0 < B.spectralRadiance c kB ν

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance_nonneg
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance per unit frequency is non-negative on the physical domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadiance_nonneg (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (ν : Frequency) (hν : 0 < ν.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) : 0 ≤ B.spectralRadiance c kB ν

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance_absZero
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance vanishes at absolute zero temperature.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadiance_absZero (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) (ν : Frequency) :
    spectralRadiance ⟨0⟩ c kB ν = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance_zeroFreq
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance vanishes at zero frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadiance_zeroFreq (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) :
    B.spectralRadiance c kB 0 = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadiance_eq_zero_of_nonpos_freq
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance vanishes when frequency is non-positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadiance_eq_zero_of_nonpos_freq (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (kB : BoltzmannConstant) (ν : Frequency) (hν : ν.val ≤ 0) :
    B.spectralRadiance c kB ν = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave
declarations.doc:
Spectral radiance per unit wavelength of blackbody radiation at wavelength
`λ` for a black body `B`, speed of light `c` and Boltzmann constant `kB`:

  `B(λ, T) = 2 h c² / λ⁵ · 1 / (e ^ (h c / (λ kB T)) - 1)`,

extended by zero outside the physical domain `0 < λ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spectralRadianceWave (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (lam : Wavelength) : ℝ

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_pos
declarations.doc:
The spectral radiance per unit wavelength is positive for positive wavelength
and positive temperature.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_pos (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (lam : Wavelength) (hlam : 0 < lam.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) :
    0 < B.spectralRadianceWave c kB lam

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_nonneg
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance per unit wavelength is non-negative on the physical domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_nonneg (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (lam : Wavelength) (hlam : 0 < lam.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) :
    0 ≤ B.spectralRadianceWave c kB lam

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_absZero
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance per unit wavelength vanishes at absolute zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_absZero (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant)
    (lam : Wavelength) : spectralRadianceWave ⟨0⟩ c kB lam = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_zeroWave
declarations.doc: The spectral radiance per unit wavelength vanishes at zero wavelength.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_zeroWave (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) :
    B.spectralRadianceWave c kB 0 = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_eq_zero_of_nonpos_wave
declarations.doc:
The spectral radiance per unit wavelength vanishes when wavelength is
non-positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_eq_zero_of_nonpos_wave (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (kB : BoltzmannConstant) (lam : Wavelength) (hlam : lam.val ≤ 0) :
    B.spectralRadianceWave c kB lam = 0

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_eq_spectralRadiance
declarations.doc:
Correspondence between the wavelength and frequency forms of Planck's law:
`B(λ, T) = (c / λ²) B(ν = c / λ, T)`, where the frequency `c / λ` is given by
`Frequency.ofWavelength`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_eq_spectralRadiance (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (kB : BoltzmannConstant) (lam : Wavelength) (hlam : 0 < lam.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) :
    B.spectralRadianceWave c kB lam
      = ((c : ℝ) / (lam.val : ℝ) ^ 2) * B.spectralRadiance c kB
          (Frequency.ofWavelength c.toWithDim lam hlam)

declarations.name: BlackBody.firstRadiationConstant
declarations.doc: The first radiation constant `c₁L = 2 h c²`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def firstRadiationConstant (c : SpeedOfLight) : ℝ

declarations.name: BlackBody.firstRadiationConstant_pos
declarations.doc: The first radiation constant is positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma firstRadiationConstant_pos (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    0 < firstRadiationConstant c

declarations.name: BlackBody.firstRadiationConstant_eq
declarations.doc: The first radiation constant equals `2 * h * c ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma firstRadiationConstant_eq (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    firstRadiationConstant c = 2 * h * (c : ℝ) ^ 2

declarations.name: BlackBody.secondRadiationConstant
declarations.doc: The second radiation constant `c₂ = h c / kB`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def secondRadiationConstant (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) : ℝ

declarations.name: BlackBody.secondRadiationConstant_pos
declarations.doc: The second radiation constant is positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma secondRadiationConstant_pos (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) :
    0 < secondRadiationConstant c kB

declarations.name: BlackBody.secondRadiationConstant_eq
declarations.doc: The second radiation constant equals `h * c / kB`.
declarations.statement:
lemma secondRadiationConstant_eq (c : SpeedOfLight) (kB : BoltzmannConstant) :
    secondRadiationConstant c kB = (h : ℝ) * (c : ℝ) / (kB : ℝ)

declarations.name: BlackBody.spectralRadianceWave_eq_constants
declarations.doc:
Planck's law per unit wavelength in terms of the radiation constants:
`B(λ, T) = (c₁L / λ⁵) / (e ^ (c₂ / (λ T)) - 1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma spectralRadianceWave_eq_constants (B : BlackBody) (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (kB : BoltzmannConstant) (lam : Wavelength) (hlam : 0 < lam.val) (hT : 0 < (B.T : ℝ)) :
    B.spectralRadianceWave c kB lam
      = firstRadiationConstant c / (lam.val : ℝ) ^ 5
        / (Real.exp (secondRadiationConstant c kB / ((lam.val : ℝ) * (B.T : ℝ))) - 1)

modules.title: Finite-dimensional quantum systems
modules.doc:
A `FiniteTarget` consists of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space together with a self-adjoint
Hamiltonian. Its Hamiltonian determines a unitary time evolution through Stone's correspondence.

Physical examples of such systems include:
- Spin systems.
- Tight binding chains.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget
declarations.doc: A finite-dimensional quantum system with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian.
declarations.statement:
structure FiniteTarget (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
  [CompleteSpace H] [FiniteDimensional ℂ H] (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The Hilbert space has dimension `n`. -/
  hdim: Module.finrank ℂ H = n
  /-- The Hamiltonian. -/
  Ham : H →L[ℂ] H
  /-- The Hamiltonian is self-adjoint. -/
  Ham_selfAdjoint: IsSelfAdjoint Ham

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.unitaryTimeEvolution
declarations.doc: The unitary time evolution generated by the Hamiltonian of `A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unitaryTimeEvolution : UnitaryOneParameterGroup H

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.unitaryTimeEvolution_generator
declarations.doc: The generator of time evolution is the Hamiltonian divided by `ℏ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryTimeEvolution_generator :
    A.unitaryTimeEvolution.generator = ((ℏ : ℂ)⁻¹) • A.Ham

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.timeEvolution
declarations.doc: The operator implementing the time evolution of `A` at time `t`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def timeEvolution (t : ℝ) : H →L[ℂ] H

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.timeEvolution_eq_exp
declarations.statement:
lemma timeEvolution_eq_exp (t : ℝ) :
    A.timeEvolution t = NormedSpace.exp ((-(t : ℂ) * Complex.I / ℏ) • A.Ham)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.timeEvolutionMatrix
declarations.doc: The matrix of the time-evolution operator at time `t` in the basis `b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def timeEvolutionMatrix (t : ℝ) (b : Basis (Fin n) ℂ H) :
  Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteTarget.timeEvolutionMatrixStandard
declarations.doc: The matrix of the time-evolution operator in a chosen basis indexed by `Fin n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def timeEvolutionMatrixStandard (t : ℝ) :
  Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ

modules.title: The free particle on `Space d`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The free quantum particle is one of the simplest quantum systems.
States for a particle of mass `m` are elements of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d` and evolve according
to the Hamiltonian `p²/2m` with no potential.

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic properties
- B. Hilbert space
- C. Hamiltonian
- D. As a quantum system

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The quantum harmonic oscillator
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The harmonic oscillator is one of the most important examples in non-relativistic quantum mechanics.
It describes a particle of mass `m` subject to a positive-definite quadratic potential
in `d` dimensions.

- `Basic.lean` : Properties of the potential, definition of isotropic oscillators,
    kinetic, potential and Hamiltonian operators.
- `LadderOperators.lean` : Definitions of the raising/lowering/number operators
    and their algebraic properties.
- `NumberOperator.lean` : The number operators as unbounded operators, symmetry.

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic properties
  - A.1. Positive mass
  - A.2. Positive natural frequencies
- B. Characteristic lengths
  - B.1. Coordinate rescaling
- C. The quadratic potential function
  - C.1. Positive-definite matrix
  - C.2. Quadratic form
  - C.3. Potential function
- D. Isotropic oscillators
- E. Hilbert space
- F. Operators
  - E.1. Kinetic energy
  - E.2. Potential energy
  - E.3. Hamiltonian
- G. As a quantum system

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator
declarations.doc: The `d`-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator.
declarations.statement:
structure HarmonicOscillator (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The mass (positive). -/
  m : ℝ
  hm : 0 < m
  /-- The natural frequencies (positive). -/
  ω : Fin d → ℝ
  hω : ∀ i, 0 < ω i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.m_pos
declarations.statement: lemma m_pos : 0 < Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.m_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma m_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.m_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma m_ne_zero : Q.m ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ω_pos
declarations.statement: lemma ω_pos : 0 < Q.ω i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ω_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma ω_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.ω i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ω_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ω_ne_zero : Q.ω i ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ
declarations.doc: The characteristic length `ξ i ≔ √ℏ / (√Q.m * √(Q.ω i))`.
declarations.statement: def ξ : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_eq
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_eq : Q.ξ i = √ℏ / (√Q.m * √(Q.ω i))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_pos
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_pos : 0 < Q.ξ i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.ξ i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_ne_zero : Q.ξ i ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_ofReal_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The characteristic length is nonzero as a complex number.
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_ofReal_ne_zero : ((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ) ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_sq
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_sq : (Q.ξ i) ^ 2 = ℏ / (Q.m * Q.ω i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_inv
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_inv : (Q.ξ i)⁻¹ = √Q.m * √(Q.ω i) / √ℏ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_inv'
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_inv' : (Q.ξ i)⁻¹ = Q.m * Q.ω i * Q.ξ i / ℏ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_sq_mul_ofReal
declarations.doc: `ξᵢ² m ωᵢ = ℏ`, as complex numbers.
declarations.statement:
lemma ξ_sq_mul_ofReal :
    ((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ 2 * ((Q.m : ℝ) : ℂ) * ((Q.ω i : ℝ) : ℂ) = (ℏ : ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξEquiv
declarations.doc: The continuous linear equivalence which rescales `xᵢ` to `ξᵢxᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def ξEquiv : Space d ≃L[ℝ] Space d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξEquiv_apply
declarations.statement: lemma ξEquiv_apply (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) : Q.ξEquiv x i = Q.ξ i * x i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.ξEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.statement: lemma ξEquiv_symm_apply (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) : Q.ξEquiv.symm x i = (Q.ξ i)⁻¹ * x i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialMatrix
declarations.doc: The positive-definite matrix defining the quadratic potential function.
declarations.statement: def potentialMatrix : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialMatrix_eq
declarations.statement: lemma potentialMatrix_eq : Q.potentialMatrix = diagonal ((2⁻¹ * Q.m) • Q.ω ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialMatrix_isHermitian
declarations.statement: lemma potentialMatrix_isHermitian : Q.potentialMatrix.IsHermitian

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialMatrix_mulVec
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialMatrix_mulVec (v : Fin d → ℝ) :
    Q.potentialMatrix *ᵥ v = (2⁻¹ * Q.m) • (Q.ω ^ 2 * v)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialQuadraticForm
declarations.doc: The positive-definite quadratic form associated to the potential matrix.
declarations.statement: def potentialQuadraticForm : QuadraticForm ℝ (Fin d → ℝ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction
declarations.doc: The quadratic potential function, `½m · ∑ i, ωᵢ²·xᵢ²`.
declarations.statement: def potentialFunction : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction_eq
declarations.statement: lemma potentialFunction_eq : Q.potentialFunction = Q.potentialQuadraticForm ∘ Space.val

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction_apply
declarations.doc: `V(x) = ∑ᵢ ½ m ωᵢ² xᵢ²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialFunction_apply (x : Space d) :
    Q.potentialFunction x = ∑ i, 2⁻¹ * Q.m * Q.ω i ^ 2 * x i ^ 2

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction_hasTemperateGrowth
declarations.doc: The potential function, as a complex-valued function, has temperate growth.
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialFunction_hasTemperateGrowth :
    Function.HasTemperateGrowth (fun x : Space d => (Q.potentialFunction x : ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction_continuous
declarations.doc: The potential function for the harmonic oscillator is continuous.
declarations.statement: lemma potentialFunction_continuous : Continuous Q.potentialFunction

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialFunction_aestronglyMeasurable
declarations.doc: The potential function for the harmonic oscillator is a.e. strongly measurable.
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialFunction_aestronglyMeasurable :
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable Q.potentialFunction MeasureTheory.volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.IsIsotropic
declarations.doc: A Harmonic oscillator is isotropic if all natural frequencies are equal.
declarations.statement: def IsIsotropic : Prop

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.isIsotropic_def
declarations.statement: lemma isIsotropic_def : Q.IsIsotropic ↔ ∀ i j, Q.ω i = Q.ω j

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.isIsotropic_of_one
declarations.statement: lemma isIsotropic_of_one (Q : HarmonicOscillator 1) : Q.IsIsotropic

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.HS
declarations.doc: The Hilbert space for the quantum harmonic oscillator.
declarations.statement: abbrev HS (_ : HarmonicOscillator d) : Type _

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.kineticOperator
declarations.doc: The kinetic energy operator, `p²/2m`.
declarations.statement: def kineticOperator : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.kineticOperator_apply_schwartz
declarations.doc: The kinetic operator on a Schwartz map, `(1/2m) ∑ᵢ pᵢ (pᵢ f)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma kineticOperator_apply_schwartz (f : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    (h : (schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS) ∈ Q.kineticOperator.domain) :
    Q.kineticOperator ⟨schwartzEquiv volume f, h⟩
      = schwartzEquiv volume (((2 * Q.m)⁻¹ : ℝ) • ∑ i, 𝐩 i (𝐩 i f))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialOperator
declarations.doc: The potential operator which maps `ψ` to `Q.potentialFunction • ψ`.
declarations.statement: def potentialOperator : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialOperator_apply_schwartz
declarations.doc: The potential operator on a Schwartz map, almost everywhere `V f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialOperator_apply_schwartz (f : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    (h : (schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS) ∈ Q.potentialOperator.domain) :
    ⇑(Q.potentialOperator ⟨schwartzEquiv volume f, h⟩) =ᵐ[volume]
      fun x => (Q.potentialFunction x : ℂ) * f x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.potentialOperator_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc: The potential operator for the harmonic oscillator is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement: lemma potentialOperator_isSelfAdjoint : IsSelfAdjoint Q.potentialOperator

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.hamiltonian
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian for the harmonic oscillator.
declarations.statement: def hamiltonian : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.hamiltonain_eq
declarations.statement: lemma hamiltonain_eq : Q.hamiltonian = Q.kineticOperator + Q.potentialOperator

modules.title: Energy eigenstates of the quantum harmonic oscillator
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The quantum harmonic oscillator in `d` dimensions is exactly solvable - the energy eigenvalues
and eigenfunction can be computed analytically.

The ground-state wavefunction is a normalized Gaussian with covariance controlled
by the harmonic oscillator's characteristic lengths. A general state is then obtained by acting
on the ground state with the raising operators and is labelled by `d` integer quantum numbers.
Their wavefunctions are given by products of (physicist's) Hermite polynomials multiplying
the ground-state Gaussian. The ladder operators of `LadderOperators.lean` act on them by shifting
one quantum number, `aᵢ† ψₙ = √(nᵢ + 1) ψₙ₊ₑᵢ` and `aᵢ ψₙ = √nᵢ ψₙ₋ₑᵢ`, so that `Nᵢ ψₙ = nᵢ ψₙ` and
`H ψₙ = Eₙ ψₙ` with `Eₙ = ∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (nᵢ + ½)` for the Hamiltonian of `Basic.lean`, which acts on
Schwartz maps as `∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (Nᵢ + ½)` (`hamiltonian_apply_schwartz`).

When the potential is isotropic another description of the energy eigenstates is possible;
energy eigenspaces carry SO(d) representations and eigenfunctions can be written in terms of
hyperspherical harmonics. In such cases the energies only depend on the radial quantum number.

## ii. Key results

- `raising_eigenfunction`, `lowering_eigenfunction`: `aᵢ† ψₙ = √(nᵢ + 1) ψₙ₊ₑᵢ`,
  `aᵢ ψₙ = √nᵢ ψₙ₋ₑᵢ`; `lowering_eigenfunction_zero`: `aᵢ ψ₀ = 0`.
- `number_eigenfunction`: `Nᵢ ψₙ = nᵢ ψₙ`.
- `sum_number_eigenfunction`, `hamiltonian_eigenstate`: `H ψₙ = Eₙ ψₙ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cartesian basis
  - A.1. Energy eigenvalues
  - A.2. Eigenfunctions
  - A.3. Eigenstates
- B. The ladder operators on the eigenfunctions
- C. The eigenvalue equation

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy
declarations.doc: The energy eigenvalues, `∑ i, ℏ ωᵢ (nᵢ + ½)`.
declarations.statement: def eigenEnergy : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy_eq
declarations.statement: lemma eigenEnergy_eq : Q.eigenEnergy n = ∑ i, ℏ * Q.ω i * (n i + 1 / 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenEnergy_strictMono
declarations.statement: lemma eigenEnergy_strictMono : StrictMono Q.eigenEnergy

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff
declarations.doc: The `i`th normalization constant for `Q.eigenfunction n`, `1 / √(2 ^ nᵢ * nᵢ! * √π * ξᵢ)`.
declarations.statement: def eigenCoeff (i : Fin d) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff_eq
declarations.statement: lemma eigenCoeff_eq (i : Fin d) : Q.eigenCoeff n i = 1 / √(2 ^ n i * (n i)! * √π * Q.ξ i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff_update_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenCoeff_update_succ (i : Fin d) (n : Fin d → ℕ) :
    √((n i : ℝ) + 1) * Q.eigenCoeff (Function.update n i (n i + 1)) i
      = (√2)⁻¹ * Q.eigenCoeff n i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenCoeff_update_pred
declarations.doc: `√nᵢ c(n - eᵢ)ᵢ = 2 nᵢ c(n)ᵢ / √2` (both sides vanish when `nᵢ = 0`).
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenCoeff_update_pred (i : Fin d) (n : Fin d → ℕ) :
    √(n i : ℝ) * Q.eigenCoeff (Function.update n i (n i - 1)) i
      = (√2)⁻¹ * (2 * n i) * Q.eigenCoeff n i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
The eigenfunction labelled by the integer quantum numbers `n : Fin d → ℕ`, defined as a product
of (physicist's) Hermite polynomials multiplying a Gaussian with covariance controlled
by the characteristic lengths, `Q.ξ`.
declarations.statement: def eigenfunction : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_eq :
    Q.eigenfunction n = compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℂ Q.ξEquiv.symm (smulLeftCLM ℂ
      (fun x ↦ ∏ i, Q.eigenCoeff n i * physHermite (n i) (x i)) (stdGaussian (Space d) ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_apply :
    Q.eigenfunction n x =
      ∏ i, Q.eigenCoeff n i *
        physHermite (n i) (x i / Q.ξ i) * cexp (-2⁻¹ * (x i / Q.ξ i) ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.oneDim
declarations.doc:
The one-dimensional harmonic oscillator of mass `m` and angular frequency `ωⱼ`, along the
`j`th axis. `Q.eigenfunction n` is the product over `j` of the `nⱼ`th eigenfunctions of these
oscillators (`eigenfunction_eq_prod_oneDim`).
declarations.statement: def oneDim (j : Fin d) : OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.oneDim_ξ
declarations.doc: The length scale of `Q.oneDim j` is `ξⱼ`.
declarations.statement: lemma oneDim_ξ (j : Fin d) : (Q.oneDim j).ξ = Q.ξ j

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.oneDim_eigenfunction_apply
declarations.doc: The `nⱼ`th eigenfunction of `Q.oneDim j` is `y ↦ c(n)ⱼ Hₙⱼ(y / ξⱼ) exp(-½ (y / ξⱼ)²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma oneDim_eigenfunction_apply (j : Fin d) (y : ℝ) :
    (Q.oneDim j).eigenfunction (n j) y =
      (Q.eigenCoeff n j : ℂ) * (physHermite (n j) (y / Q.ξ j) : ℂ) *
        cexp (-2⁻¹ * ((y : ℂ) / (Q.ξ j : ℂ)) ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_eq_prod_oneDim
declarations.doc: The eigenfunction is the product of the eigenfunctions of the one-dimensional oscillators.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_eq_prod_oneDim :
    Q.eigenfunction n x = ∏ j, (Q.oneDim j).eigenfunction (n j) (x j)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_oneDim_eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the `nⱼ`th eigenfunction of `Q.oneDim j`,
`c(n)ⱼ ((2 nⱼ/ξⱼ) Hₙⱼ₋₁(y/ξⱼ) - (y/ξⱼ²) Hₙⱼ(y/ξⱼ)) exp(-½ (y/ξⱼ)²)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_oneDim_eigenfunction (j : Fin d) (y : ℝ) :
    _root_.deriv ((Q.oneDim j).eigenfunction (n j)) y
      = (Q.eigenCoeff n j : ℂ) *
        (((2 * n j / Q.ξ j : ℝ) : ℂ) * (physHermite (n j - 1) (y / Q.ξ j) : ℂ)
          - ((y / Q.ξ j ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) * (physHermite (n j) (y / Q.ξ j) : ℂ)) *
        cexp (-2⁻¹ * ((y : ℂ) / (Q.ξ j : ℂ)) ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_update_apply
declarations.doc: The eigenfunction with the `i`th quantum number changed to `k`, factor `i` set apart.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_update_apply (i : Fin d) (k : ℕ) :
    Q.eigenfunction (Function.update n i k) x =
      (Q.oneDim i).eigenfunction (Function.update n i k i) (x i) *
        ∏ j ∈ univ.erase i, (Q.oneDim j).eigenfunction (n j) (x j)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_eigenfunction_apply
declarations.doc: The `i`th spatial derivative of the eigenfunction, factor `i` differentiated.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eigenfunction_apply (i : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (Q.eigenfunction n) x =
      _root_.deriv ((Q.oneDim i).eigenfunction (n i)) (x i) *
        ∏ j ∈ univ.erase i, (Q.oneDim j).eigenfunction (n j) (x j)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstate
declarations.doc: `Q.eigenfunction n` as an element of the Schwartz submodule of the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def eigenstate : SchwartzSubmodule d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstate_eq
declarations.statement: lemma eigenstate_eq : Q.eigenstate n = schwartzEquiv _ (Q.eigenfunction n)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstates_orthonormal
declarations.doc: The energy eigenstates are orthonormal.
declarations.statement: lemma eigenstates_orthonormal : ⟪(Q.eigenstate n : Q.HS), Q.eigenstate n'⟫_ℂ = δ[n,n']

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raising_eigenfunction
declarations.doc: `aᵢ† ψₙ = √(nᵢ + 1) ψₙ₊ₑᵢ`: the raising operator raises the `i`th quantum number by one.
declarations.statement:
lemma raising_eigenfunction (i : Fin d) (n : Fin d → ℕ) :
    Q.raisingCLM i (Q.eigenfunction n) =
      ((Real.sqrt (n i + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) • Q.eigenfunction (Function.update n i (n i + 1))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.lowering_eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
`aᵢ ψₙ = √nᵢ ψₙ₋ₑᵢ`: the lowering operator lowers the `i`th quantum number by one (and
annihilates the eigenfunction when `nᵢ = 0`, since `√0 = 0`).
declarations.statement:
lemma lowering_eigenfunction (i : Fin d) (n : Fin d → ℕ) :
    Q.loweringCLM i (Q.eigenfunction n) =
      ((Real.sqrt (n i) : ℝ) : ℂ) • Q.eigenfunction (Function.update n i (n i - 1))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.lowering_eigenfunction_zero
declarations.doc: The ground state is annihilated by every lowering operator.
declarations.statement: lemma lowering_eigenfunction_zero (i : Fin d) : Q.loweringCLM i (Q.eigenfunction 0) = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.number_eigenfunction
declarations.doc: `Nᵢ ψₙ = nᵢ ψₙ`: the eigenfunctions are eigenfunctions of the number operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma number_eigenfunction (i : Fin d) (n : Fin d → ℕ) :
    Q.numberCLM i (Q.eigenfunction n) = ((n i : ℕ) : ℂ) • Q.eigenfunction n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sum_number_eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
`∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (Nᵢ + ½) ψₙ = Eₙ ψₙ`: the eigenvalue equation for the Hamiltonian written with the
number operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_number_eigenfunction :
    (∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
      (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))) (Q.eigenfunction n) =
      (Q.eigenEnergy n : ℂ) • Q.eigenfunction n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.eigenstate_mem_hamiltonian_domain
declarations.doc: The eigenstates lie in the domain of the Hamiltonian.
declarations.statement: lemma eigenstate_mem_hamiltonian_domain : (Q.eigenstate n : Q.HS) ∈ Q.hamiltonian.domain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.hamiltonian_eigenstate
declarations.doc:
`H ψₙ = Eₙ ψₙ`: the time-independent Schrodinger equation for the eigenstates, with the
Hamiltonian `kineticOperator + potentialOperator` of `Basic.lean`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_eigenstate (h : (Q.eigenstate n : Q.HS) ∈ Q.hamiltonian.domain) :
    Q.hamiltonian ⟨Q.eigenstate n, h⟩ = (Q.eigenEnergy n : ℂ) • (Q.eigenstate n : Q.HS)

modules.title: Ladder operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The ladder operators of the `d`-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator, acting on Schwartz maps:
the lowering (annihilation) operators `aᵢ = (xᵢ/ξᵢ + i ξᵢ pᵢ/ℏ)/√2` and the raising (creation)
operators `aᵢ† = (xᵢ/ξᵢ - i ξᵢ pᵢ/ℏ)/√2`, together with
their commutation relations, which all follow from the canonical commutation relations
`position_commutation_momentum`. The ladder operators are then lifted to unbounded operators on the
Hilbert space with the Schwartz submodule as domain (like `momentumOperator`), `aᵢ†` being the
formal adjoint of `aᵢ`. The number operators `Nᵢ = aᵢ† aᵢ` and the Hamiltonian written through them
are in `NumberOperator.lean`.

## ii. Key results

- `lowering_commutation_raising`: `[aᵢ, aⱼ†] = δᵢⱼ 𝟙`; `lowering_commutation_lowering`,
  `raising_commutation_raising`: `[aᵢ, aⱼ] = 0`, `[aᵢ†, aⱼ†] = 0`.
- `position_eq_lowering_add_raising`, `momentum_eq_raising_sub_lowering`: the position and
  momentum operators in terms of the ladder operators.
- `loweringOperator_isFormalAdjoint_raisingOperator`: `aᵢ†` is the formal adjoint of `aᵢ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Ladder operators
  - A.1. Definitions
  - A.2. Commutation relations
  - A.3. Position and momentum in terms of the ladder operators
  - A.4. The ladder operators as unbounded operators, adjointness

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringCLM
declarations.doc:
The lowering (annihilation) operator `aᵢ = (xᵢ/ξᵢ + i ξᵢ pᵢ/ℏ)/√2`, as a continuous linear
map on Schwartz maps.
declarations.statement: def loweringCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raisingCLM
declarations.doc:
The raising (creation) operator `aᵢ† = (xᵢ/ξᵢ - i ξᵢ pᵢ/ℏ)/√2`, as a continuous linear
map on Schwartz maps.
declarations.statement: def raisingCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringCLM_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma loweringCLM_eq : Q.loweringCLM i =
    (Real.sqrt 2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ • 𝐱 i + (I * ((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ) / (ℏ : ℂ)) • 𝐩 i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raisingCLM_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma raisingCLM_eq : Q.raisingCLM i =
    (Real.sqrt 2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ • 𝐱 i - (I * ((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ) / (ℏ : ℂ)) • 𝐩 i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sqrt_two_sq_ofReal
declarations.doc: `(√2)² = 2` as complex numbers.
declarations.statement: lemma sqrt_two_sq_ofReal : ((Real.sqrt 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ 2 = 2

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.lowering_commutation_raising
declarations.doc: `[aᵢ, aⱼ†] = δᵢⱼ 𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lowering_commutation_raising :
    ⁅Q.loweringCLM i, Q.raisingCLM j⁆ = δ[i,j] • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.lowering_commutation_lowering
declarations.statement: lemma lowering_commutation_lowering : ⁅Q.loweringCLM i, Q.loweringCLM j⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raising_commutation_raising
declarations.statement: lemma raising_commutation_raising : ⁅Q.raisingCLM i, Q.raisingCLM j⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raising_commutation_lowering
declarations.doc: `[aᵢ†, aⱼ] = -δᵢⱼ 𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
lemma raising_commutation_lowering :
    ⁅Q.raisingCLM i, Q.loweringCLM j⁆ = -(δ[i,j] • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.position_eq_lowering_add_raising
declarations.statement:
lemma position_eq_lowering_add_raising :
    𝐱 i = (((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ) / (Real.sqrt 2 : ℂ)) • (Q.loweringCLM i + Q.raisingCLM i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.momentum_eq_raising_sub_lowering
declarations.doc: `pᵢ = (i ℏ/(√2 ξᵢ)) (aᵢ† - aᵢ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma momentum_eq_raising_sub_lowering :
    𝐩 i = (I * (ℏ : ℂ) / ((Real.sqrt 2 : ℂ) * ((Q.ξ i : ℝ) : ℂ))) •
      (Q.raisingCLM i - Q.loweringCLM i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringOperator
declarations.doc: The lowering operator as an unbounded operator with domain the Schwartz submodule.
declarations.statement: def loweringOperator : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raisingOperator
declarations.doc: The raising operator as an unbounded operator with domain the Schwartz submodule.
declarations.statement: def raisingOperator : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma loweringOperator_apply (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    Q.loweringOperator i ψ =
      schwartzEquiv volume (Q.loweringCLM i ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raisingOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma raisingOperator_apply (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    Q.raisingOperator i ψ =
      schwartzEquiv volume (Q.raisingCLM i ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringCLM_inner
declarations.doc: `⟪aᵢ f, g⟫ = ⟪f, aᵢ† g⟫` for Schwartz maps `f`, `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma loweringCLM_inner (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume (Q.loweringCLM i f) : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume g⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume (Q.raisingCLM i g)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.raisingCLM_inner
declarations.doc: `⟪aᵢ† f, g⟫ = ⟪f, aᵢ g⟫` for Schwartz maps `f`, `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma raisingCLM_inner (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume (Q.raisingCLM i f) : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume g⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume (Q.loweringCLM i g)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.loweringOperator_isFormalAdjoint_raisingOperator
declarations.doc: The raising operator is the formal adjoint of the lowering operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma loweringOperator_isFormalAdjoint_raisingOperator :
    (Q.loweringOperator i).IsFormalAdjoint (Q.raisingOperator i)

modules.title: Number operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The number operators `Nᵢ = aᵢ† aᵢ` of the `d`-dimensional quantum harmonic oscillator, built from
the ladder operators of `LadderOperators.lean` and acting on Schwartz maps: their commutation
relations with the ladder operators and with each other, and the Hamiltonian of `Basic.lean`, which
on Schwartz maps acts as `H_N = ∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (Nᵢ + ½)`, commutes with the number operators and lowers
and raises energies by `ℏ ωᵢ`. The number operators are then lifted to unbounded operators on the
Hilbert space with the Schwartz submodule as domain (like `momentumOperator`), where they are
symmetric, as is the Hamiltonian.

## ii. Key results

- `number_commutation_number`: `[Nᵢ, Nⱼ] = 0`; `number_commutation_lowering`,
  `number_commutation_raising`: `[Nᵢ, aⱼ] = -δᵢⱼ aⱼ`, `[Nᵢ, aⱼ†] = δᵢⱼ aⱼ†`.
- `lowering_comp_raising`: `aᵢ aᵢ† = Nᵢ + 𝟙`; `numberCLM_inner`:
  `⟪ Nᵢ f, g⟫ = ⟪ f, Nᵢ g⟫` for Schwartz maps.
- `sum_number_commutation_lowering`, `sum_number_commutation_raising`,
  `sum_number_commutation_number`: with `H_N = ∑ⱼ ℏ ωⱼ (Nⱼ + ½)`, `[H_N, aᵢ] = -ℏ ωᵢ aᵢ`,
  `[H_N, aᵢ†] = ℏ ωᵢ aᵢ†`, `[H_N, Nᵢ] = 0`.
- `sum_number_apply`: `H_N ψ = (1/2m) ∑ᵢ pᵢ (pᵢ ψ) + V ψ` on Schwartz maps;
  `hamiltonian_apply_schwartz`: the Hamiltonian of `Basic.lean` acts on Schwartz maps as `H_N`;
  `hamiltonian_inner_schwartz`: it is symmetric on the Schwartz submodule.
- `numberOperator_isSymmetric`: the number operators are symmetric.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Number operators
  - A.1. Definition
  - A.2. Commutation relations
  - A.3. Inner products
- B. Hamiltonian
  - B.1. Commutation relations with the ladder and number operators
  - B.2. The Hamiltonian on Schwartz maps
- C. The number operators as unbounded operators
- D. Symmetry

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Hamiltonian

On Schwartz maps the Hamiltonian of `Basic.lean` acts as `H_N = ∑ⱼ ℏ ωⱼ (Nⱼ + ½)`
(`hamiltonian_apply_schwartz`); the lemmas below are stated for this sum.

### B.2. The Hamiltonian on Schwartz maps
## C. The number operators as unbounded operators

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberCLM
declarations.doc: The number operator `Nᵢ = aᵢ† aᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def numberCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberCLM_eq
declarations.statement: lemma numberCLM_eq : Q.numberCLM i = Q.raisingCLM i ∘L Q.loweringCLM i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.number_commutation_lowering
declarations.doc: `[Nᵢ, aⱼ] = -δᵢⱼ aⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma number_commutation_lowering :
    ⁅Q.numberCLM i, Q.loweringCLM j⁆ = -(δ[i,j] • Q.loweringCLM j)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.number_commutation_raising
declarations.doc: `[Nᵢ, aⱼ†] = δᵢⱼ aⱼ†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma number_commutation_raising :
    ⁅Q.numberCLM i, Q.raisingCLM j⁆ = δ[i,j] • Q.raisingCLM j

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.number_commutation_number
declarations.statement: lemma number_commutation_number : ⁅Q.numberCLM i, Q.numberCLM j⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.lowering_comp_raising
declarations.doc: `aᵢ aᵢ† = Nᵢ + 𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lowering_comp_raising :
    Q.loweringCLM i ∘L Q.raisingCLM i =
      Q.numberCLM i + ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberCLM_inner
declarations.doc: `⟪Nᵢ f, g⟫ = ⟪f, Nᵢ g⟫` for Schwartz maps `f`, `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma numberCLM_inner (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume (Q.numberCLM i f) : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume g⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS), schwartzEquiv volume (Q.numberCLM i g)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sum_number_commutation_lowering
declarations.doc: `[∑ⱼ ℏ ωⱼ (Nⱼ + ½), aᵢ] = -ℏ ωᵢ aᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_number_commutation_lowering :
    ⁅∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)),
      Q.loweringCLM i⁆ = -(((ℏ * Q.ω i : ℝ) : ℂ) • Q.loweringCLM i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sum_number_commutation_raising
declarations.doc: `[∑ⱼ ℏ ωⱼ (Nⱼ + ½), aᵢ†] = ℏ ωᵢ aᵢ†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_number_commutation_raising :
    ⁅∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)),
      Q.raisingCLM i⁆ = ((ℏ * Q.ω i : ℝ) : ℂ) • Q.raisingCLM i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sum_number_commutation_number
declarations.doc: `[∑ⱼ ℏ ωⱼ (Nⱼ + ½), Nᵢ] = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_number_commutation_number :
    ⁅∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)),
      Q.numberCLM i⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.sum_number_apply
declarations.doc: On Schwartz maps, `∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (Nᵢ + ½) ψ = (1/2m) ∑ᵢ pᵢ (pᵢ ψ) + V ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_number_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    (∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
      (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))) ψ x =
      ((2 * Q.m : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, 𝐩 i (𝐩 i ψ) x + (Q.potentialFunction x : ℂ) * ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.schwartzSubmodule_le_hamiltonian_domain
declarations.doc: The Schwartz submodule is contained in the domain of the Hamiltonian.
declarations.statement: lemma schwartzSubmodule_le_hamiltonian_domain : SchwartzSubmodule d ≤ Q.hamiltonian.domain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.hamiltonian_apply_schwartz
declarations.doc:
On a Schwartz map, the Hamiltonian `kineticOperator + potentialOperator` of `Basic.lean` acts as
`∑ᵢ ℏ ωᵢ (Nᵢ + ½)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_apply_schwartz (f : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    (h : (schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS) ∈ Q.hamiltonian.domain) :
    Q.hamiltonian ⟨schwartzEquiv volume f, h⟩ = schwartzEquiv volume
      ((∑ j, ((ℏ * Q.ω j : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (Q.numberCLM j + (2⁻¹ : ℂ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))) f)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.hamiltonian_inner_schwartz
declarations.doc:
`⟪H f, g⟫ = ⟪f, H g⟫` for Schwartz maps `f`, `g`: the Hamiltonian is symmetric on the Schwartz
submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_inner_schwartz (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    (hf : (schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS) ∈ Q.hamiltonian.domain)
    (hg : (schwartzEquiv volume g : Q.HS) ∈ Q.hamiltonian.domain) :
    ⟪Q.hamiltonian ⟨schwartzEquiv volume f, hf⟩, (schwartzEquiv volume g : Q.HS)⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume f : Q.HS), Q.hamiltonian ⟨schwartzEquiv volume g, hg⟩⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberOperator
declarations.doc: The number operator as an unbounded operator with domain the Schwartz submodule.
declarations.statement: def numberOperator : Q.HS →ₗ.[ℂ] Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma numberOperator_apply (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    Q.numberOperator i ψ =
      schwartzEquiv volume (Q.numberCLM i ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HarmonicOscillator.numberOperator_isSymmetric
declarations.doc: The number operator is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma numberOperator_isSymmetric : (Q.numberOperator i).IsSymmetric

modules.title: 1d Harmonic Oscillator
modules.doc:
The quantum harmonic oscillator in 1d.
This file contains
- the definition of the Schrodinger operator
- the definition of eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the Schrodinger operator in terms
  of Hermite polynomials
- proof that eigenfunctions and eigenvalues are indeed eigenfunctions and eigenvalues.

declarations.name: Complex.ofReal_hasDerivAt
declarations.statement: lemma Complex.ofReal_hasDerivAt : HasDerivAt Complex.ofReal 1 x

declarations.name: Complex.deriv_ofReal

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator
declarations.doc:
A quantum harmonic oscillator specified by a three
real parameters: the mass of the particle `m`, a value of Planck's constant `ℏ`, and
an angular frequency `ω`. All three of these parameters are assumed to be positive.
declarations.statement:
structure HarmonicOscillator where
  /-- The mass of the particle. -/
  m : ℝ
  /-- The angular frequency of the harmonic oscillator. -/
  ω : ℝ
  hω : 0 < ω
  hm : 0 < m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.m_pos
declarations.statement: lemma m_pos : 0 < Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.m_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma m_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.m_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma m_ne_zero : Q.m ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ω_pos
declarations.statement: lemma ω_pos : 0 < Q.ω

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ω_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma ω_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.ω

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ω_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ω_ne_zero : Q.ω ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ
declarations.doc:
The characteristic length `ξ` of the harmonic oscillator is defined
as `√(ℏ /(m ω))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ξ : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.ξ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_pos
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_pos : 0 < Q.ξ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_ne_zero : Q.ξ ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_sq
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_sq : Q.ξ^2 = ℏ / (Q.m * Q.ω)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_abs
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_abs : abs Q.ξ = Q.ξ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.one_over_ξ
declarations.statement: lemma one_over_ξ : 1/Q.ξ = √(Q.m * Q.ω / ℏ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.ξ_inverse
declarations.statement: lemma ξ_inverse : Q.ξ⁻¹ = √(Q.m * Q.ω / ℏ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.one_over_ξ_sq
declarations.statement: lemma one_over_ξ_sq : (1/Q.ξ)^2 = Q.m * Q.ω / ℏ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator
declarations.doc:
For a harmonic oscillator, the Schrodinger Operator corresponding to it
is defined as the function from `ℝ → ℂ` to `ℝ → ℂ` taking

`ψ ↦ - ℏ^2 / (2 * m) * ψ'' + 1/2 * m * ω^2 * x^2 * ψ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def schrodingerOperator (ψ : ℝ → ℂ) : ℝ → ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_eq (ψ : ℝ → ℂ) :
    Q.schrodingerOperator ψ = (- ℏ ^ 2 / (2 * Q.m)) •
    (deriv (deriv ψ)) + (1/2 * Q.m * Q.ω^2) • ((fun x => Complex.ofReal x ^2) * ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_eq_ξ
declarations.doc: The schrodinger operator written in terms of `ξ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_eq_ξ (ψ : ℝ → ℂ) : Q.schrodingerOperator ψ =
    fun x => (ℏ ^2 / (2 * Q.m)) * (- (deriv (deriv ψ) x) + (1/Q.ξ^2)^2 * x^2 * ψ x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_parity
declarations.doc: The Schrodinger operator commutes with the parity operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_parity (ψ : ℝ → ℂ) :
    Q.schrodingerOperator (parityOperator ψ) = parityOperator (Q.schrodingerOperator ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_add
declarations.doc: The Schrodinger operator is additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_add (ψ φ : ℝ → ℂ)
    (hψ : Differentiable ℝ ψ) (hψ' : Differentiable ℝ (deriv ψ))
    (hφ : Differentiable ℝ φ) (hφ' : Differentiable ℝ (deriv φ)) :
    Q.schrodingerOperator (ψ + φ) = Q.schrodingerOperator ψ + Q.schrodingerOperator φ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_smul
declarations.doc: The Schrodinger operator is homogeneous.
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_smul (c : ℂ) (ψ : ℝ → ℂ)
    (hψ : Differentiable ℝ ψ) (hψ' : Differentiable ℝ (deriv ψ)) :
    Q.schrodingerOperator (c • ψ) = c • Q.schrodingerOperator ψ

modules.title: Completeness of the eigenfunctions of the Harmonic Oscillator
modules.doc:
Completeness of the eigenfunctions follows from Plancherel's theorem.

The steps of this proof are:

1. Prove that if `f` is orthogonal to all eigenvectors then the Fourier transform of
  it multiplied by `exp(-c x^2)` for a `0<c` is zero.
  Part of this is using the concept of `dominated_convergence`.
2. Use 'Plancherel's theorem' to show that `f` is zero.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.mul_eigenfunction_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_eigenfunction_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Q.eigenfunction n x * f x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.mul_physHermite_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_physHermite_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (n : ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => physHermite n (x/Q.ξ) *
      (f x * ↑(Real.exp (- x ^ 2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2)))))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.mul_polynomial_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_polynomial_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (P : Polynomial ℤ) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => (P (x /Q.ξ)) *
      (f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2)))) volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.mul_power_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_power_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (r : ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => x ^ r * (f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2)))) volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.orthogonal_eigenfunction_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_eigenfunction_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (n : ℕ) : ∫ (x : ℝ), Q.eigenfunction n x * f x = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.orthogonal_physHermite_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_physHermite_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (n : ℕ) : ∫ (x : ℝ), (physHermite n (x / Q.ξ)) * (f x * ↑(Real.exp (- x ^ 2 / (2 * Q.ξ ^ 2))))
    = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.orthogonal_polynomial_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_polynomial_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (P : Polynomial ℤ) :
    ∫ x : ℝ, (P (x /Q.ξ)) * (f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2))) = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.orthogonal_power_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
If `f` is a function `ℝ → ℂ` satisfying `MemHS f` such that it is orthogonal
to all `eigenfunction n` then it is orthogonal to

`x ^ r * e ^ (- x ^ 2 / (2 ξ^2))`

the proof of this result relies on the fact that Hermite polynomials span polynomials.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_power_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (r : ℕ) : ∫ x : ℝ, (x ^ r * (f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2)))) = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.orthogonal_exp_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
If `f` is a function `ℝ → ℂ` satisfying `MemHS f` such that it is orthogonal
to all `eigenfunction n` then it is orthogonal to

`e ^ (I c x) * e ^ (- x ^ 2 / (2 ξ^2))`

for any real `c`.
The proof of this result relies on the expansion of `e ^ (I c x)`
in terms of `x^r/r!` and using `orthogonal_power_of_mem_orthogonal`
along with integrability conditions.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_exp_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (c : ℝ) : ∫ x : ℝ, Complex.exp (Complex.I * c * x) *
    (f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2))) = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.fourierIntegral_zero_of_mem_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
If `f` is a function `ℝ → ℂ` satisfying `MemHS f` such that it is orthogonal
to all `eigenfunction n` then the fourier transform of

`f (x) * e ^ (- x ^ 2 / (2 ξ^2))`

is zero.

The proof of this result relies on `orthogonal_exp_of_mem_orthogonal`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fourierIntegral_zero_of_mem_orthogonal (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0) :
    𝓕 (fun x => f x * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2))) = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.zero_of_orthogonal_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma zero_of_orthogonal_mk (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), HilbertSpace.mk hf⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (plancherel_theorem: ∀ {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Integrable f volume) (_ : MemLp f 2),
      eLpNorm (𝓕 f) 2 volume = eLpNorm f 2 volume) :
    HilbertSpace.mk hf = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.zero_of_orthogonal_eigenVector
declarations.statement:
lemma zero_of_orthogonal_eigenVector (f : HilbertSpace)
    (hOrth : ∀ n : ℕ, ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n), f⟫_ℂ = 0)
    (plancherel_theorem: ∀ {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Integrable f volume) (_ : MemLp f 2),
      eLpNorm (𝓕 f) 2 volume = eLpNorm f 2 volume) : f = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_completeness
declarations.doc:
Assuming Plancherel's theorem (which is not yet in Mathlib),
the topological closure of the span of the eigenfunctions of the harmonic oscillator
is the whole Hilbert space.

The proof of this result relies on `fourierIntegral_zero_of_mem_orthogonal`
and Plancherel's theorem which together give us that the norm of

`f x * e ^ (- x^2 / (2 * ξ^2))`

is zero for `f` orthogonal to all eigenfunctions, and hence the norm of `f` is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem eigenfunction_completeness
    (plancherel_theorem : ∀ {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Integrable f volume) (_ : MemLp f 2),
      eLpNorm (𝓕 f) 2 volume = eLpNorm f 2 volume) :
    (Submodule.span ℂ
    (Set.range (fun n => HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n)))).topologicalClosure = ⊤

modules.title: Eigenfunction of the Harmonic Oscillator
modules.doc:
Note: These eigenfunctions have been generalized to `d` dimensions in
`QuantumMechanics/HarmonicOscillator/Eigenstates.lean`.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
The `n`th eigenfunction of the Harmonic oscillator is defined as the function `ℝ → ℂ`
taking `x : ℝ` to

`1/√(2^n n!) 1/√(√π ξ) * physHermite n (x / ξ) * e ^ (- x²/ (2 ξ²))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eigenfunction (n : ℕ) : ℝ → ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_eq (n : ℕ) :
    Q.eigenfunction n = fun (x : ℝ) => (1/√(2 ^ n * n !) * (1/ √(√Real.pi * Q.ξ))) *
    Complex.ofReal (physHermite n (x / Q.ξ) * Real.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2)))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_zero : Q.eigenfunction 0 = fun (x : ℝ) =>
    (1/ √(√Real.pi * Q.ξ)) * Complex.exp (- x^2 / (2 * Q.ξ^2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_eq_mul_eigenfunction_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_eq_mul_eigenfunction_zero (n : ℕ) :
    Q.eigenfunction n = fun x => Complex.ofReal (1/√(2 ^ n * n !))
    * Complex.ofReal (physHermite n (x / Q.ξ)) * Q.eigenfunction 0 x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_integrable
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are integrable.
declarations.statement: lemma eigenfunction_integrable (n : ℕ) : Integrable (Q.eigenfunction n)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_conj
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are real.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_conj (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) (Q.eigenfunction n x) = Q.eigenfunction n x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_point_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_point_norm (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    ‖Q.eigenfunction n x‖ = (1/√(2 ^ n * n !) * (1/ √(√Real.pi * Q.ξ))) *
    (|physHermite n (x / Q.ξ)| * Real.exp (- x ^ 2 / (2 * Q.ξ ^ 2)))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_point_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_point_norm_sq (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    ‖Q.eigenfunction n x‖ ^ 2 = (1/√(2 ^ n * n !) * (1/ √(√Real.pi * Q.ξ))) ^ 2 *
    ((physHermite n (x / Q.ξ)) ^ 2 * Real.exp (- x^2 / Q.ξ ^ 2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_square_integrable
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are square integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_square_integrable (n : ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ‖Q.eigenfunction n x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_aeStronglyMeasurable
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are almost everywhere strongly measurable.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_aeStronglyMeasurable (n : ℕ) :
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (Q.eigenfunction n)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_memHS
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are members of the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: lemma eigenfunction_memHS (n : ℕ) : MemHS (Q.eigenfunction n)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_differentiableAt
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are differentiable.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_differentiableAt (x : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (Q.eigenfunction n) x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_continuous
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are continuous.
declarations.statement: lemma eigenfunction_continuous (n : ℕ) : Continuous (Q.eigenfunction n)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_parity
declarations.doc:
The `n`th eigenfunction is an eigenfunction of the parity operator with
the eigenvalue `(-1) ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_parity (n : ℕ) :
    parityOperator (Q.eigenfunction n) = (-1) ^ n * Q.eigenfunction n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_mul
declarations.doc: A simplification of the product of two eigenfunctions.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_mul (n p : ℕ) :
    (Q.eigenfunction n x) * (Q.eigenfunction p x) =
    1/√(2 ^ n * n !) * 1/√(2 ^ p * p !) * (1/ (√Real.pi * Q.ξ)) * Complex.ofReal
    (physHermite n (x / Q.ξ) * physHermite p (x / Q.ξ) * Real.exp (- x^2 / Q.ξ^2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_mul_self
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_mul_self (n : ℕ) : (Q.eigenfunction n x) * (Q.eigenfunction n x) =
    (1/ (2 ^ n * n !) * (1/ (√Real.pi * Q.ξ))) *
    Complex.ofReal ((physHermite n (x / Q.ξ))^2 * Real.exp (- x^2 / Q.ξ^2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_normalized
declarations.doc: The eigenfunction are normalized.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_normalized (n : ℕ) : ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n),
    HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n)⟫_ℂ = 1

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_orthogonal
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions of the quantum harmonic oscillator are orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_orthogonal {n p : ℕ} (hnp : n ≠ p) :
    ⟪HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n),
      HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS p)⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_orthonormal
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are orthonormal within the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_orthonormal :
    Orthonormal ℂ (fun n => HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenfunction_linearIndependent
declarations.doc: The eigenfunctions are linearly independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma eigenfunction_linearIndependent :
    LinearIndependent ℂ (fun n => HilbertSpace.mk (Q.eigenfunction_memHS n))

modules.title: Examples: 1d Quantum Harmonic Oscillator
modules.doc:
This module gives simple examples of how to use the
`QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator` API.

It is intended for experimentation and pedagogical use, and should
not be imported into other modules.

To run it from the command line:
```
lake env lean Physlib/QuantumMechanics/OneDimension/HarmonicOscillator/Examples.lean
```

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.Examples.Q
declarations.doc: A concrete harmonic oscillator with `m = 1`, `ω = 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def Q : HarmonicOscillator

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.eigenValue
declarations.doc: The `n`th eigenvalues for a Harmonic oscillator is defined as `(n + 1/2) * ℏ * ω`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eigenValue (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_eigenfunction_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eigenfunction_zero : deriv (Q.eigenfunction 0) =
    Complex.ofReal (- 1 / Q.ξ ^2) • Complex.ofReal * Q.eigenfunction 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_eigenfunction_zero'
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eigenfunction_zero' : deriv (Q.eigenfunction 0) =
    (- √2 / (2 * Q.ξ) : ℂ) • Q.eigenfunction 1

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_physHermite_characteristic_length
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_physHermite_characteristic_length (n : ℕ) :
    deriv (fun x => Complex.ofReal (physHermite n (x/Q.ξ))) = fun x =>
    Complex.ofReal (1/Q.ξ) * 2 * n * physHermite (n-1) (x/Q.ξ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_eigenfunction_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eigenfunction_succ (n : ℕ) :
    deriv (Q.eigenfunction (n + 1)) = fun x =>
    Complex.ofReal (1/√(2 ^ (n + 1) * (n + 1)!) * (1/Q.ξ)) •
    ((2 * (n + 1) * physHermite n (x/Q.ξ)
      - (x/Q.ξ) * physHermite (n + 1) (x/Q.ξ)) * Q.eigenfunction 0 x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_deriv_eigenfunction_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_eigenfunction_zero (x : ℝ) : deriv (deriv (Q.eigenfunction 0)) x =
    (- 1 / Q.ξ^2) * (1 + ((- 1/ Q.ξ^2) * x ^ 2)) * Q.eigenfunction 0 x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_deriv_eigenfunction_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_eigenfunction_succ (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun x => deriv (Q.eigenfunction (n + 1)) x) x =
    Complex.ofReal (1/√(2 ^ (n + 1) * (n + 1) !) * (1/Q.ξ)) *
      ((2 * (↑n + 1) * deriv (fun x => ↑(physHermite n (x/Q.ξ))) x +
      (-(1/Q.ξ^2)) * (4 * (↑n + 1) * x) *
      (physHermite n (x/Q.ξ)) + (- (1/Q.ξ)) * (1 + (- (1/Q.ξ^2)) * x ^ 2) *
      (physHermite (n + 1) (x/Q.ξ))) * Q.eigenfunction 0 x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.deriv_deriv_eigenfunction
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_eigenfunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun x => deriv (Q.eigenfunction n) x) x = (- 1 / Q.ξ^2) * ((2 * n + 1)
    + ((- 1/ Q.ξ^2) * x ^ 2)) * Q.eigenfunction n x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HarmonicOscillator.schrodingerOperator_eigenfunction
declarations.doc:
The `n`th eigenfunction satisfies the time-independent Schrodinger equation with
respect to the `n`th eigenvalue. That is to say for `Q` a harmonic oscillator,

`Q.schrodingerOperator (Q.eigenfunction n) x = Q.eigenValue n * Q.eigenfunction n x`.

The proof of this result is done by explicit calculation of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma schrodingerOperator_eigenfunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    Q.schrodingerOperator (Q.eigenfunction n) x = Q.eigenValue n * Q.eigenfunction n x

modules.title: The Hilbert space of a finite target quantum mechanical system
modules.doc:
A finite target quantum mechanical system is one whose states live in a finite
dimensional Hilbert space, with the basis states labelled by a finite type `d`
(for example the sites of a finite lattice, or the levels of a qudit).

This file contains
- the definition of `FiniteHilbertSpace d`, the Hilbert space of such a system,
  as a structure wrapping `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`, together with the notation `𝓗[d]`;
- its vector space structure (`AddCommGroup` and `Module ℂ`), transferred from
  `EuclideanSpace ℂ d` along the equivalence `equivEuclidean`;
- its Hilbert space structure (`NormedAddCommGroup`, `InnerProductSpace ℂ`,
  `FiniteDimensional ℂ` and `CompleteSpace`), induced along `linearEquivEuclidean`;
- the standard orthonormal basis `basisFun`, whose elements are the states
  localized at the points of `d`.

sections.text:
## The vector space structure on `FiniteHilbertSpace d`

The vector space structure is transferred from `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`
along the equivalence `equivEuclidean`.

## The Hilbert space structure on `FiniteHilbertSpace d`

The norm and inner product are induced from `EuclideanSpace ℂ d` along
`linearEquivEuclidean`, making `FiniteHilbertSpace d` a finite dimensional
(and hence complete) inner product space, that is, a Hilbert space.
## The standard orthonormal basis of `FiniteHilbertSpace d`

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert space of a finite target quantum mechanical system whose target is
a finite type `d` with decidable equality.

It is defined as a structure with a single field `val`, wrapping an element of
`EuclideanSpace ℂ d` — the space of functions `d → ℂ` carrying the `L²` inner
product `⟪ψ, φ⟫ = ∑ i, conj (ψ i) * φ i`. Using a structure in preference to
`EuclideanSpace ℂ d` itself makes the Hilbert space of states a type of its own,
with its own API and the notation `𝓗[d]`.

Being finite dimensional, it is automatically a complete inner product space,
that is, a genuine Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
structure FiniteHilbertSpace (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
  /-- The underlying element of `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`. -/
  val : EuclideanSpace ℂ d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.equivEuclidean
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `FiniteHilbertSpace d` and `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`
given by `val`.
declarations.statement: def equivEuclidean : FiniteHilbertSpace d ≃ EuclideanSpace ℂ d
noncomputable instance : AddCommGroup (FiniteHilbertSpace d)
noncomputable instance : Module ℂ (FiniteHilbertSpace d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.val_add
declarations.statement: lemma val_add (ψ φ : FiniteHilbertSpace d) : (ψ + φ).val = ψ.val + φ.val

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.val_smul
declarations.statement: lemma val_smul (c : ℂ) (ψ : FiniteHilbertSpace d) : (c • ψ).val = c • ψ.val

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.val_zero
declarations.statement: lemma val_zero : (0 : FiniteHilbertSpace d).val = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.linearEquivEuclidean
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `FiniteHilbertSpace d` and `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`
as a `ℂ`-linear equivalence, upgrading `equivEuclidean`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def linearEquivEuclidean : FiniteHilbertSpace d ≃ₗ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ d
noncomputable instance : NormedAddCommGroup (FiniteHilbertSpace d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.norm_eq_val
declarations.statement: lemma norm_eq_val (ψ : FiniteHilbertSpace d) : ‖ψ‖ = ‖ψ.val‖
noncomputable instance : InnerProductSpace ℂ (FiniteHilbertSpace d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.inner_eq_val
declarations.statement: lemma inner_eq_val (ψ φ : FiniteHilbertSpace d) : inner ℂ ψ φ = inner ℂ ψ.val φ.val
instance : FiniteDimensional ℂ (FiniteHilbertSpace d)
instance : CompleteSpace (FiniteHilbertSpace d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.isometryEquivEuclidean
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `FiniteHilbertSpace d` and `EuclideanSpace ℂ d`
as a linear isometry equivalence, upgrading `linearEquivEuclidean`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isometryEquivEuclidean : FiniteHilbertSpace d ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.basisFun
declarations.doc: The standard orthonormal basis of `FiniteHilbertSpace d`, indexed by `d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def basisFun (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] :
    OrthonormalBasis d ℂ (FiniteHilbertSpace d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.FiniteHilbertSpace.basisFun_apply
declarations.statement: lemma basisFun_apply (i : d) : basisFun d i = ⟨EuclideanSpace.single i 1⟩
