sections.text: ## Member of the Hilbert space as a property
# Construction of elements of the Hilbert space

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert space for a one dimensional quantum system is defined as
the space of almost-everywhere equal equivalence classes of square integrable functions
from `ℝ` to `ℂ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev HilbertSpace

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.toBra
declarations.doc: The anti-linear map from the Hilbert space to it's dual.
declarations.statement: def toBra : HilbertSpace →ₛₗ[starRingEnd ℂ] StrongDual ℂ HilbertSpace

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.toBra_apply
declarations.statement: lemma toBra_apply (f g : HilbertSpace) : toBra f g = ⟪f, g⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.toBra_surjective
declarations.doc:
The anti-linear map, `toBra`, taking a ket to it's corresponding
bra is surjective.
declarations.statement: lemma toBra_surjective : Function.Surjective toBra

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.toBra_injective
declarations.doc:
The anti-linear map, `toBra`, taking a ket to it's corresponding
bra is injective.
declarations.statement: lemma toBra_injective : Function.Injective toBra

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.MemHS
declarations.doc:
The proposition `MemHS f` for a function `f : ℝ → ℂ` is defined
to be true if the function `f` can be lifted to the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def MemHS (f : ℝ → ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.aeStronglyMeasurable_of_memHS
declarations.statement: lemma aeStronglyMeasurable_of_memHS {f : ℝ → ℂ} (h : MemHS f) : AEStronglyMeasurable f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.memHS_iff
declarations.doc:
A function `f` satisfies `MemHS f` if and only if it is almost everywhere
strongly measurable, and square integrable.
declarations.statement:
lemma memHS_iff {f : ℝ → ℂ} : MemHS f ↔
    AEStronglyMeasurable f ∧ Integrable (fun x => ‖f x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.zero_memHS
declarations.statement: lemma zero_memHS : MemHS 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.zero_fun_memHS
declarations.statement: lemma zero_fun_memHS : MemHS (fun _ : ℝ => (0 : ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.memHS_add
declarations.statement:
lemma memHS_add {f g : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : MemHS f) (hg : MemHS g) :
    MemHS (f + g)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.memHS_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma memHS_smul {f : ℝ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} (hf : MemHS f) :
    MemHS (c • f)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.memHS_of_ae
declarations.statement:
lemma memHS_of_ae {g : ℝ → ℂ} (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (hfg : f =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume] g) :
    MemHS g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.aeEqFun_mk_mem_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma aeEqFun_mk_mem_iff (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f volume) :
    AEEqFun.mk f hf ∈ HilbertSpace ↔ MemHS f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mk
declarations.doc:
Given a function `f : ℝ → ℂ` such that `MemHS f` is true via `hf`, then `HilbertSpace.mk hf`
is the element of the `HilbertSpace` defined by `f`.
declarations.statement: def mk {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : MemHS f) : HilbertSpace

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.coe_hilbertSpace_memHS
declarations.statement: lemma coe_hilbertSpace_memHS (f : HilbertSpace) : MemHS (f : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mk_surjective
declarations.statement: lemma mk_surjective (f : HilbertSpace) : ∃ (g : ℝ → ℂ), ∃ (hg : MemHS g), mk hg = f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.coe_mk_ae
declarations.statement: lemma coe_mk_ae {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : MemHS f) : (mk hf : ℝ → ℂ) =ᵐ[MeasureTheory.volume] f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.inner_mk_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_mk_mk {f g : ℝ → ℂ} {hf : MemHS f} {hg : MemHS g} :
    inner ℂ (mk hf) (mk hg) = ∫ x : ℝ, starRingEnd ℂ (f x) * g x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.eLpNorm_mk
declarations.statement: lemma eLpNorm_mk {f : ℝ → ℂ} {hf : MemHS f} : eLpNorm (mk hf) 2 volume = eLpNorm f 2 volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mem_iff'
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iff' {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f MeasureTheory.volume) :
    MeasureTheory.AEEqFun.mk f hf ∈ HilbertSpace
    ↔ MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ‖f x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mk_add
declarations.statement:
lemma mk_add {f g : ℝ → ℂ} {hf : MemHS f} {hg : MemHS g} :
    mk (memHS_add hf hg) = mk hf + mk hg

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mk_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma mk_smul {f : ℝ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} {hf : MemHS f} :
    mk (memHS_smul (c := c) hf) = c • mk hf

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mk_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mk_eq_iff {f g : ℝ → ℂ} {hf : MemHS f} {hg : MemHS g} :
    mk hf = mk hg ↔ f =ᵐ[volume] g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.ext_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_iff {f g : HilbertSpace} :
    f = g ↔ (f : ℝ → ℂ) =ᶠ[ae volume] (g : ℝ → ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussian_integrable {b : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => (Real.exp (- b * (x - c)^ 2) : ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.gaussian_aestronglyMeasurable
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussian_aestronglyMeasurable {b : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Real.exp (- b * (x - c) ^2) : ℂ)) volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.gaussian_memHS
declarations.statement:
lemma gaussian_memHS {b : ℝ} (c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MemHS (fun x => (Real.exp (- b * (x - c) ^2) : ℂ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.exp_mul_gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_mul_gaussian_integrable (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (c * x) * Real.exp (- b * x ^ 2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.exp_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (|c * x|) * Real.exp (- b * x ^ 2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mul_gaussian_mem_Lp_one
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_gaussian_mem_Lp_one (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => f x * Real.exp (- b * (x - c) ^ 2)) 1 volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.mul_gaussian_mem_Lp_two
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_gaussian_mem_Lp_two (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.MemLp (fun x => f x * Real.exp (- b * (x - c) ^ 2)) 2 volume

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.abs_mul_gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_mul_gaussian_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => norm (f x) * Real.exp (- b * (x - c)^2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.exp_mul_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_mul_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f)
    (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) : MeasureTheory.Integrable
    (fun x => Real.exp (c * x) * norm (f x) * Real.exp (- b * x ^ 2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.exp_abs_mul_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma exp_abs_mul_abs_mul_gaussian_integrable (f : ℝ → ℂ) (hf : MemHS f) (b c : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable
    (fun x => Real.exp (|c * x|) * norm (f x) * Real.exp (- b * x ^ 2))

modules.title: Plane waves
modules.doc:
We define plane waves as a member of the dual of the Schwartz submodule of the 1d Hilbert space.

This module has been generalized to d-dimensions in
`QuantumMechanics/HilbertSpaces/SpaceD/MomentumStates.lean` and will be removed in the near future.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.planewaveFunctional
declarations.doc:
Plane waves as a member of the dual of the
Schwartz submodule of the Hilbert space.

For a given `k` this corresponds to the plane wave
`exp (2π I k x)`.
declarations.statement: def planewaveFunctional (k : ℝ) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ) →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.planewaveFunctional_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma planewaveFunctional_apply (k : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) :
    planewaveFunctional k ψ = 𝓕 ψ k

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.eq_of_eq_planewaveFunctional
declarations.doc:
Two elements of the Schwartz submodule are equal if and only if they are equal on
all applications of `planewaveFunctional`.

modules.title: Position states
modules.doc:
We define position state as a member of the dual of the Schwartz submodule of the 1d Hilbert space.

This module has been generalized to d-dimensions in
`QuantumMechanics/HilbertSpaces/SpaceD/PositionStates.lean` and will be removed in the near future.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.positionState
declarations.doc:
Position state as a member of the dual of the
Schwartz submodule of the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def positionState (x : ℝ) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ) →L[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.positionState_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma positionState_apply (x : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) :
    positionState x ψ = ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.eq_of_eq_positionState
declarations.doc:
Two elements of the `𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)` are equal if they
are equal on all position states.

modules.title: Schwartz submodule of the Hilbert space
modules.doc:
This can be used to define e.g.
the rigged Hilbert space.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.schwartzIncl
declarations.doc: The continuous linear map including Schwartz functions into the hilbert space.
declarations.statement: def schwartzIncl : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ) →L[ℂ] HilbertSpace

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.schwartzIncl_injective
declarations.statement: lemma schwartzIncl_injective : Function.Injective schwartzIncl

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.HilbertSpace.schwartzIncl_coe_ae
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzIncl_coe_ae (ψ : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) :
    ψ.1 =ᶠ[ae volume] (schwartzIncl ψ)

modules.title: Hilbert spaces for quantum mechanics on `Space d`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Hilbert spaces appropriate for doing quantum mechanics on `Space d` are the $L^2$-spaces
`SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ := Lp ℂ 2 μ`, where `μ` is some measure on `Space d`.
Elements of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` are _equivalence classes_ of functions `Space d → ℂ` which are
square-integrable with respect to `μ`, i.e. `∫ x, ‖f x‖ ^ 2 ∂μ` is finite, and where `f` and `g` are
in the same equivalence class if they are `μ`-a.e. equal.

The ability of a function to be interpreted as an element of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` is captured
by the property `MemHS`. If one has `hf : MemHS f μ` for a function `f : Space d → ℂ` this means
that `f` is `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable and square-integrable; `mk hf` constructs the corresponding
equivalence class of `f` in `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ`.

Given `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` and `Ω : Set (Space d)`, the Hilbert space
`SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ ≔ SpaceDHilbertSpace d (μ.restrict Ω)` may be interpreted as the
sub-Hilbert space consisting of those vectors with domain contained in `Ω`.
The reason is that for each `ψ` in `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ` we have
`ψ =ᵐ[μ.restrict Ω] Ω.indicator ψ`, namely the equivalence class of `ψ` always
contains a representative which vanishes on the complement of `Ω`.
The linear isometry `restrictIncl Ω μ` describes this sub-Hilbert space relationship
by mapping each `ψ` to this special representative in its equivalence class.
Similarly, we may project `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` onto `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ` by enlarging the
equivalence classes, essentially dropping information about the functions on the complement of `Ω`.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` : The $L^2$-space on `Space d` with respect to the measure `μ`.
- `toBra` : The linear equivalence between the Hilbert space and its dual. This is the map which
    sends each ket to its corresponding bra and _vice versa_.
- `MemHS f μ` : The proposition capturing exactly when a function `f : Space d → ℂ` can be lifted
    to an element of the Hilbert space.
- `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ` : An abbreviation for the Hilbert space
    `SpaceDHilbertSpace d (μ.restrict Ω)` appropriate for describing the $L^2$-space of complex
    functions on a subset of `Space d`.
- `subspaceProjection` : The continuous linear projection of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` onto
    `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ`.
- `subspaceIncl` : The linear isometry including `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ`
    as a sub-Hilbert space of `SpaceDHilbertspace d μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. SpaceDHilbertSpace
  - A.1. Dual space
  - A.2. Membership
  - A.3. Construction of elements
  - A.4. Coersions
  - A.5. Misc.
- B. SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Dirichlet submodule
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the Dirichlet submodule of `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ` consisting of
equivalence classes of Schwartz maps which vanish on `frontier Ω`. The frontier (or boundary)
of a set `Ω` contains all points whose neighborhoods always intersect with both `Ω` and `Ωᶜ`.

These serve as a convenient dense domain for operators acting on wavefunctions satisfying
homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on `Ω`.

## ii. Key results

- `DirichletSubmoduleOn Ω μ`: The subspace of `SchwartzSubmodule d μ` consisting of Schwartz maps
  which vanish on the frontier of `Ω`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definitions
- B. Contained in SchwartzSubmoduleOn
- C. Density

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn.DirichletSchwartzMap

declarations.statement: def DirichletSchwartzMap : Submodule ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn.DirichletSubmoduleOn
declarations.doc:
The submodule of the Hilbert space on `Ω` consisting of the equivalence classes
of Schwartz maps which vanish on `frontier Ω`.
declarations.statement: abbrev DirichletSubmoduleOn : Submodule ℂ (SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn.DirichletSubmoduleOn.mem_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iff {ψ : SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ} :
    ψ ∈ DirichletSubmoduleOn Ω μ ↔
      ∃ f : DirichletSchwartzMap Ω, subspaceProjection Ω μ (schwartzIncl μ f) = ψ

declarations.statement: lemma le_schwartzSubmoduleOn : DirichletSubmoduleOn Ω μ ≤ SchwartzSubmoduleOn Ω μ

modules.title: The Fourier transform on `SpaceDHilbertSpace`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the Fourier transform on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d` as a unitary operator.
Mathlib's L² Fourier transform `MeasureTheory.Lp.fourierTransformₗᵢ` is a linear isometry
equivalence of `Lp ℂ 2 volume`, hence of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`, onto itself; packaged as
`fourierUnitary d`.

## ii. Key results

- `fourierUnitary d` : the L² Fourier transform as a unitary
  `SpaceDHilbertSpace d ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d`, acting as `𝓕`/`𝓕⁻`
  (`fourierUnitary_apply`, `fourierUnitary_symm_apply`).
- `schwartzIncl_fourier_eq` : `𝓕 (schwartzIncl f) = schwartzIncl (𝓕 f)`.
- `schwartzIncl_fourierInv_eq` : the inverse acts by the inverse Schwartz Fourier transform.
- `fourierUnitary_map_schwartzSubmodule` : `fourierUnitary d` maps the Schwartz submodule onto
  itself.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Fourier unitary
- B. Action on the Schwartz submodule

## iv. References

* None.

Applying `fourierUnitary d` to the L² class of a Schwartz map `f` gives the L² class of the

lemma schwartzIncl_fourier_eq (f : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :

    (SchwartzSubmodule d).map (fourierUnitary d).toLinearMap = SchwartzSubmodule d

modules.title: Momentum states
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Informally, the momentum "state" corresponding to the wave vector `p`, of momentum `ℏ p`, is the
non-normalizable plane wave `exp (I p ⬝ᵥ x)`. More precisely, the momentum "state" lives in the
_rigged_ Hilbert space `𝓢(Space d, ℂ) < SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ < StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)`
as the bra `⟨p|`. This is the linear functional `ψ ↦ ⟨exp (I p ⬝ᵥ x), ψ⟩ = 𝓕 ψ ((2π)⁻¹ • p)`.

An operator `A` acts on `momentumState p` by precomposition, `⟨p| A = momentumState p ∘L A`.

## ii. Key results

- `momentumState` : the momentum state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.
- `momentumState_comp_momentumCLM` : the momentum state `momentumState p` is a generalized
  eigenvector of `𝐩 i` with eigenvalue `ℏ pᵢ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Momentum states
- B. Momentum states as generalized eigenvectors

## iv. References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigged_Hilbert_space. [ref: wiki_rigged_hilbert_space]

sections.text: ## B. Momentum states as generalized eigenvectors

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.momentumState
declarations.doc:
Momentum state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.

For a given wave vector `p` this is the bra `⟨p|` of the non-normalizable plane wave
`exp (I p ⬝ᵥ x)`, that is `ψ ↦ ⟨exp (I p ⬝ᵥ x), ψ⟩`.
declarations.statement: def momentumState (p : Space d) : StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.momentumState_apply
declarations.doc: The defining property of momentum states.
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumState_apply (p : Space d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    momentumState p ψ = 𝓕 ψ ((2 * π)⁻¹ • p)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.eq_of_eq_momentumState
declarations.doc: Two Schwartz maps are equal if they are equal on all momentum states.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_eq_momentumState {ψ φ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)}
    (h : ∀ p, momentumState p ψ = momentumState p φ) : ψ = φ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.momentumState_comp_momentumCLM
declarations.doc:
The momentum state `momentumState p` is a generalized eigenvector of `𝐩 i` with eigenvalue
`ℏ pᵢ`, in the bra form `⟨p| 𝐩ᵢ = ℏ pᵢ ⟨p|` as functionals on Schwartz space. Since `𝐩 i` is
symmetric and `ℏ pᵢ` is real, this is equivalent to the ket form `𝐩ᵢ |p⟩ = ℏ pᵢ |p⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumState_comp_momentumCLM (p : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    momentumState p ∘L 𝐩 i = (ℏ * p i : ℂ) • momentumState p

modules.title: Polynomially-bounded Schwartz submodules
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define polynomially-bounded Schwartz submodules of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ`.

For each `a : ℕ∞`, `PolyBddSchwartzSubmodule d a μ` is the submodule corresponding to Schwartz
maps `f` satisfying the polynomial growth bounds `‖x‖ ^ (-k) * ‖f x‖ ≤ Cₖ` for all `(k : ℕ) ≤ a`.
In particular, for `a = ⊤` such a bound holds for all natural numbers.

These serve as a natural domain for singular unbounded operators. For example, the `1/r` Coulomb
potential operator maps `PolyBddSchwartzSubmodule d ⊤ μ` to itself. In the same way that multiplying
a Schwartz map by any polynomial in the coordinates results in a square-integrable function,
polynomially-bounded Schwartz maps may be multiplied by Laurent polynomials and remain
square-integrable (the precise condition depends on `d`, `a` and the negative degree of
the Laurent polynomial).

Note: the condition defining polynomially-bounded Schwartz maps is phrased as
`‖x‖ ^ (-k) * ‖f x‖ ≤ Cₖ` rather than as `‖f x‖ ≤ Cₖ * ‖x‖ ^ k` to mirror `SchwartzMap.decay`.
These two conditions only differ at `x = 0` and are therefore equivalent for `d > 0` since
then `f 0` may be determined by continuity. For `d = 0` the former does not constrain `f 0 = 0`
(since `x = 0` is the only point and `0⁻¹ = 0`) while the latter does (and would therefore spoil
their being dense in `SpaceDHilbertSpace 0 ≅ ℂ`).

## ii. Key results

- `PolyBddSchwartzSubmodule d (a : ℕ∞) μ`: Restriction of `SchwartzSubmodule d μ` to those
  Schwartz maps which are bounded by powers of `‖x‖`.
- `PolyBddSchwartzSubmodule.dense`: These submodules are dense in `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definitions
- B. Coercions
- C. (In)equalities
- D. Density

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Position states
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Informally, the position "state" at `x : Space d` has a non-normalizable wavefunction which is
a Dirac-delta function centered at `x`. More precisely, the position "state" lives in the _rigged_
Hilbert space `𝓢(Space d, ℂ) < SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ < StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` as the element
of the dual of `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` defined by evaluation at `x`.

## ii. Key results

- `positionState` : the position state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.
- `positionState_comp_positionCLM` : the position state `positionState x` is a generalized
  eigenvector of `𝐱 i` with eigenvalue `xᵢ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Position states
- B. Position states as generalized eigenvectors

## iv. References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rigged_Hilbert_space. [ref: wiki_rigged_hilbert_space]

sections.text: ## B. Position states as generalized eigenvectors

declarations.doc:
Position state as a member of the strong dual of the Schwartz space.

For a given `x` this corresponds to the non-normalizable wavefunction `ψ(y) = δᵈ(y - x)
declarations.statement: def positionState (x : Space d) : StrongDual ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.doc: The defining property of position states.

    (h : ∀ x, positionState x f = positionState x g) : f = g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.positionState_comp_positionCLM
declarations.doc:
The position state `positionState x` is a generalized eigenvector of `𝐱 i` with eigenvalue
`xᵢ`, in the bra form `⟨x| 𝐱ᵢ = xᵢ ⟨x|` as functionals on Schwartz space. Since `𝐱 i` is
symmetric and `xᵢ` is real, this is equivalent to the ket form `𝐱ᵢ |x⟩ = xᵢ |x⟩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma positionState_comp_positionCLM (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    positionState x ∘L 𝐱 i = (x i : ℂ) • positionState x

modules.title: Schwartz submodule
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the Schwartz submodule of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ`.
`SchwartzSubmodule d μ` consists of the `μ`-a.e. equal equivalence classes of Schwartz maps
on `Space d`.

This is an import subspace of the Hilbert space. For one, the Fourier transform maps the Schwartz
submodule into itself. It also is a convenient dense domain on which to define derivative operators.

## ii. Key results

- `SchwartzSubmodule d μ`: Submodule of `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` consisting of the L² equivalence
  classes of Schwartz maps `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)`.
- `SchwartzSubmoduleOn Ω μ`: The projection of `SchwartzSubmodule d μ`
  onto `SpaceDHilbertSpaceOn Ω μ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. SchwartzSubmodule
  - A.1. Coercions
  - A.2. Misc.
- B. SchwartzSubmoduleOn

## iv. References

* None.

## i. Overview

In this module we define the Sobolev submodules of `SpaceDHilbertSpace`.

## ii. Key results

modules.title: Complete tensor product
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Given two inner product spaces `E` and `F` over `𝕜`, their tensor product `E ⊗[𝕜] F` consists
of finite sums of simple (a.k.a. pure) tensors `m ⊗ₜ[𝕜] n`. This tensor product is again an inner
product space with inner product defined by `⟪m ⊗ₜ n, m' ⊗ₜ n'⟫_𝕜 = ⟪m, m'⟫_𝕜 * ⟪n, n'⟫_𝕜`
on simple tensors and then extended by linearity (c.f. `TensorProduct.instInnerProductSpace`).

However, in general this procedure does not result in a Hilbert space: Cauchy sequences need not
converge because the tensor product does not contain any _infinite_ sums of simple tensors.
In order to obtain a Hilbert space for use in quantum mechanics, we must _add in_ the limits
of Cauchy sequences by taking the completion.

In this module we define the complete tensor product,
`CompleteTensorProduct 𝕜 E F := Completion (E ⊗[𝕜] F)` with notation `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F` and `E ⊗ₕ F`,
provide some basic properties for the maps which embed `E ⊗[𝕜] F` into `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F`
and prove that `⊗ₕ` is commutative and associative (up to linear isometric equivalence).

## ii. Key results

- `CompleteTensorProduct 𝕜 E F` (notation `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F` and `E ⊗ₕ F`) :
    The _completion_ of the tensor product of a pair of inner product spaces `E` and `F` over `𝕜`.
- `CompleteTensorProduct.comm 𝕜 E F` : The linear isometric equivalence between
    `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F` and `F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] E`.
- `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc 𝕜 E F G` : The linear isometric equivalence between
    `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G` and `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)`.
- `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc_tIncl₃ₗᵢ` : On the algebraic threefold tensor product,
    `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc` reduces to `TensorProduct.assoc`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition
- B. Nontrivial
- C. Coercions
- D. Induction principle
- E. Commutative
- F. Associative
  - F.1. Associativity on the algebraic tensor product

## iv. References

* None.

lemma _root_.TensorProduct.denseRange_map
    {R 𝕜 : Type*} [CommSemiring R] [RCLike 𝕜] {σ : R →+* 𝕜} [RingHomSurjective σ]
    {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
    {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 F]
    {f : M →ₛₗ[σ] E} (hf : DenseRange f) {g : N →ₛₗ[σ] F} (hg : DenseRange g) :
    DenseRange (TensorProduct.map f g)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc
declarations.doc:
The compete tensor product of inner product spaces is associative,
up to linear isometric equivalence.
declarations.statement: def assoc : E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.tIncl₃ₗᵢ
declarations.doc:
The embedding of the algebraic threefold tensor product `E ⊗[𝕜] F ⊗[𝕜] G` into the complete
tensor product `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G` as a linear isometry: `E ⊗[𝕜] F` is first embedded into
`E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F`, then `(E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F) ⊗[𝕜] G` is embedded into its completion.
declarations.statement: def tIncl₃ₗᵢ : E ⊗[𝕜] F ⊗[𝕜] G →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.tIncl₃'ₗᵢ
declarations.doc:
The embedding of the algebraic threefold tensor product `E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗[𝕜] G)` into the
complete tensor product `E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)` as a linear isometry: `F ⊗[𝕜] G` is first
embedded into `F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G`, then `E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)` is embedded into its completion.
declarations.statement: def tIncl₃'ₗᵢ : E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗[𝕜] G) →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.tIncl₃ₗᵢ_tmul
declarations.doc: On a simple tensor `x ⊗ₜ y ⊗ₜ z`, the embedding `tIncl₃ₗᵢ` is the nested coercion.
declarations.statement:
lemma tIncl₃ₗᵢ_tmul (x : E) (y : F) (z : G) :
    tIncl₃ₗᵢ (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z) = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z : (E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F) ⊗[𝕜] G)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.tIncl₃'ₗᵢ_tmul
declarations.doc: On a simple tensor `x ⊗ₜ (y ⊗ₜ z)`, the embedding `tIncl₃'ₗᵢ` is the nested coercion.
declarations.statement:
lemma tIncl₃'ₗᵢ_tmul (x : E) (y : F) (z : G) :
    tIncl₃'ₗᵢ (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z)) = (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z) : E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G))

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc_tIncl₃ₗᵢ
declarations.doc:
`CompleteTensorProduct.assoc` acting on an element of the algebraic threefold tensor product
reduces to `TensorProduct.assoc`.
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_tIncl₃ₗᵢ (x : E ⊗[𝕜] F ⊗[𝕜] G) :
    assoc 𝕜 E F G (tIncl₃ₗᵢ x) = tIncl₃'ₗᵢ (TensorProduct.assoc 𝕜 E F G x)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc_symm_tIncl₃'ₗᵢ
declarations.doc:
The inverse of `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc` acting on an element of the algebraic threefold
tensor product reduces to the inverse of `TensorProduct.assoc`.
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_symm_tIncl₃'ₗᵢ (x : E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗[𝕜] G)) :
    (assoc 𝕜 E F G).symm (tIncl₃'ₗᵢ x) = tIncl₃ₗᵢ ((TensorProduct.assoc 𝕜 E F G).symm x)

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc_tmul
declarations.doc: `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc` on simple tensors (c.f. `TensorProduct.assoc_tmul`).
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_tmul (x : E) (y : F) (z : G) :
    assoc 𝕜 E F G (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z : (E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F) ⊗[𝕜] G) =
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z) : E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G))

declarations.name: CompleteTensorProduct.assoc_symm_tmul
declarations.doc:
The inverse of `CompleteTensorProduct.assoc` on simple tensors
(c.f. `TensorProduct.assoc_symm_tmul`).
declarations.statement:
lemma assoc_symm_tmul (x : E) (y : F) (z : G) :
    (assoc 𝕜 E F G).symm (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] (y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z) : E ⊗[𝕜] (F ⊗ₕ[𝕜] G)) =
      (x ⊗ₜ[𝕜] y ⊗ₜ[𝕜] z : (E ⊗ₕ[𝕜] F) ⊗[𝕜] G)

modules.title: Hydrogen atom
modules.doc:
This module introduces the `d`-dimensional hydrogen atom with `1/r` potential.

In addition to the dimension `d`, the quantum mechanical system is characterized by
a mass `m > 0` and constant `k` appearing in the potential `V = -k/r`.
The standard hydrogen atom has `d=3`, `m = mₑmₚ/(mₑ + mₚ) ≈ mₑ` and `k = e²/4πε₀`.

The potential `V = -k/r` is singular at the origin. To address this we define a regularized
Hamiltonian in which the potential is replaced by `-k·r(ε)⁻¹`, where `r(ε)² = ‖x‖² + ε²`.
This goes by several names including "soft-core" and "truncated" Coulomb potential.

The (unregularized) Hamiltonian is densely defined in any dimension: its domain contains the
dense submodule of polynomially-bounded Schwartz maps (`hamiltonianOperator_hasDenseDomain`).

## References

* https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.80.032507. [ref: doi_physreva_80_032507]
* https://doi.org/10.1063/1.3290740. [ref: doi_1063_1_3290740]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom
declarations.doc:
A hydrogen atom is characterized by the number of spatial dimensions `d`,
the mass `m` and the coefficient `k` for the `1/r` potential.
declarations.statement:
structure HydrogenAtom (d : ℕ) extends SpaceDQuantumSystem d where
  /-- Coefficient in the Coulomb potential (positive for attractive) -/
  k : ℝ
  coulomb_potential : potential = fun x ↦ -k * ‖x‖⁻¹

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.potential_eq
declarations.statement: lemma potential_eq : H.potential = fun x ↦ -H.k * ‖x‖⁻¹

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.potential_AESM
declarations.statement: lemma potential_AESM : AEStronglyMeasurable H.potential

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.potential_AEM
declarations.statement: lemma potential_AEM : AEMeasurable H.potential

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.hamiltonianRegCLM
declarations.doc:
The hydrogen atom Hamiltonian regularized by `ε ≠ 0` is defined to be
`𝐇(ε) ≔ (2m)⁻¹𝐩² - k·𝐫(ε)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: def hamiltonianRegCLM (ε : ℝˣ) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.hamiltonianRegCLM_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianRegCLM_eq (ε : ℝˣ) :
    H.hamiltonianRegCLM ε = (2 * H.m)⁻¹ • (𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩) - H.k • 𝐫₀ ε (-1)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.polyBddSchwartzSubmodule_le_hamiltonianOperator_domain
declarations.doc:
Polynomially-bounded Schwartz maps `f` with `‖x‖ ^ (-k) * ‖f x‖ ≤ Cₖ` for all `k ≤ ⌊2 - d/2⌋`
lie in the domain of the Hamiltonian. For `d ≥ 3` these are all Schwartz maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyBddSchwartzSubmodule_le_hamiltonianOperator_domain :
    PolyBddSchwartzSubmodule d ⌊1 - d / 2 - (-1 : ℝ)⌋.toNat ≤
      H.hamiltonianOperator.domain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.hamiltonianOperator_hasDenseDomain
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian of the hydrogen atom is densely defined, in any dimension.
declarations.statement: lemma hamiltonianOperator_hasDenseDomain : H.hamiltonianOperator.HasDenseDomain

modules.title: Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector
modules.doc:
In this file we define
- The (regularized) LRL vector operator for the quantum mechanical hydrogen atom,
  `𝐀(ε)ᵢ ≔ ½(𝐩ⱼ𝐋ᵢⱼ + 𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐩ⱼ) - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`.

The main results are
- The commutators `⁅𝐋ᵢⱼ, 𝐀(ε)ₖ⁆ = iℏ(δᵢₖ𝐀(ε)ⱼ - δⱼₖ𝐀(ε)ᵢ)` in `angularMomentum_commutation_lrl`
- The cyclic relation `𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐀(ε)ₖ + 𝐋ⱼₖ𝐀(ε)ᵢ + 𝐋ₖᵢ𝐀(ε)ⱼ = 0` (in `d = 3`: `𝐋 · 𝐀(ε) = 0`) in
  `angularMomentum_cyclic_lrl`, and with `𝐀(ε)` on the left in `lrl_cyclic_angularMomentum`
- The commutators `⁅𝐀(ε)ᵢ, 𝐀(ε)ⱼ⁆ = (-2iℏm·𝐇(ε) + iℏmkε²·𝐫(ε)⁻³))𝐋ᵢⱼ` in `lrl_commutation_lrl`
- The commutators `⁅𝐇(ε), 𝐀(ε)ᵢ⁆ = iℏε²(⋯)` in `hamiltonianReg_commutation_lrl`
- The relation `𝐀(ε)² = 2m 𝐇(ε)(𝐋² + ¼ℏ²(d-1)²) + m²k² + ε²(⋯)` in `lrlOperatorSqr_eq`

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperator
declarations.doc:
The (regularized) Laplace-Runge-Lenz vector operator for the `d`-dimensional hydrogen atom,
`𝐀(ε)ᵢ ≔ ½(𝐩ⱼ𝐋ᵢⱼ + 𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐩ⱼ) - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def lrlOperator (ε : ℝˣ) (i : Fin d) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperator_eq
declarations.doc: `𝐀(ε)ᵢ = 𝐱ᵢ𝐩² - (𝐱ⱼ𝐩ⱼ)𝐩ᵢ + ½iℏ(d-1)𝐩ᵢ - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`
declarations.statement:
lemma lrlOperator_eq (ε : ℝˣ) (i : Fin d) : H.lrlOperator ε i = 𝐱 i ∘L (𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩)
    - (𝐱 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩) ∘L 𝐩 i + (2⁻¹ * I * ℏ * (d - 1)) • 𝐩 i - (H.m * H.k) • 𝐫₀ ε (-1) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperator_eq'
declarations.doc: `𝐀(ε)ᵢ = 𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐩ⱼ + ½iℏ(d-1)𝐩ᵢ - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`
declarations.statement:
lemma lrlOperator_eq' (ε : ℝˣ) (i : Fin d) : H.lrlOperator ε i =
    𝐋 i ⬝ᵥ 𝐩 + (2⁻¹ * I * ℏ * (d - 1)) • 𝐩 i - (H.m * H.k) • 𝐫₀ ε (-1) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperator_eq''
declarations.doc: `𝐀(ε)ᵢ = 𝐩ⱼ𝐋ᵢⱼ - ½iℏ(d-1)𝐩ᵢ - mk·𝐫(ε)⁻¹𝐱ᵢ`
declarations.statement:
lemma lrlOperator_eq'' (ε : ℝˣ) (i : Fin d) : H.lrlOperator ε i =
    𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐋 i - (2⁻¹ * I * ℏ * (d - 1)) • 𝐩 i - (H.m * H.k) • 𝐫₀ ε (-1) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentum_commutation_Ldot_p
declarations.doc:
A supporting piece of `angularMomentum_commutation_lrl`: how `𝐋ᵢⱼ` commutes with the
dot-product term `𝐋ₖ⬝ᵥ𝐩` appearing in `H.lrlOperator`'s expanded form (`lrlOperator_eq'`).
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_commutation_Ldot_p (i j k : Fin d) :
    ⁅𝐋[d] i j, 𝐋 k ⬝ᵥ 𝐩⁆ =
      (I * ℏ) • (δ[i,k] • (𝐋 j ⬝ᵥ 𝐩) - δ[j,k] • (𝐋 i ⬝ᵥ 𝐩))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentum_commutation_lrl
declarations.doc: `⁅𝐋ᵢⱼ, 𝐀(ε)ₖ⁆ = iℏ(δᵢₖ𝐀(ε)ⱼ - δⱼₖ𝐀(ε)ᵢ)`
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_commutation_lrl (ε : ℝˣ) (i j k : Fin d) : ⁅𝐋 i j, H.lrlOperator ε k⁆ =
    (I * ℏ) • (δ[i,k] • H.lrlOperator ε j - δ[j,k] • H.lrlOperator ε i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentum_commutation_lrlSqr
declarations.doc: `⁅𝐋ᵢⱼ, 𝐀(ε)²⁆ = 0`
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_commutation_lrlSqr (ε : ℝˣ) (i j : Fin d) :
    ⁅𝐋 i j, H.lrlOperator ε ⬝ᵥ H.lrlOperator ε⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentumSqr_commutation_lrlSqr
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumSqr_commutation_lrlSqr (ε : ℝˣ) :
    ⁅𝐋²[d], H.lrlOperator ε ⬝ᵥ H.lrlOperator ε⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.angularMomentum_cyclic_lrl
declarations.doc:
`𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐀(ε)ₖ + 𝐋ⱼₖ𝐀(ε)ᵢ + 𝐋ₖᵢ𝐀(ε)ⱼ = 0`; in three dimensions this is `𝐋 · 𝐀(ε) = 0`.
The identity is trivial unless `i`, `j`, `k` are pairwise distinct, so it has no content in
fewer than three dimensions.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_cyclic_lrl (ε : ℝˣ) (i j k : Fin d) :
    𝐋 i j ∘L H.lrlOperator ε k + 𝐋 j k ∘L H.lrlOperator ε i + 𝐋 k i ∘L H.lrlOperator ε j = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrl_cyclic_angularMomentum
declarations.doc:
`𝐀(ε)ₖ𝐋ᵢⱼ + 𝐀(ε)ᵢ𝐋ⱼₖ + 𝐀(ε)ⱼ𝐋ₖᵢ = 0`; in three dimensions this is `𝐀(ε) · 𝐋 = 0`.
The identity is trivial unless `i`, `j`, `k` are pairwise distinct, so it has no content in
fewer than three dimensions.
declarations.statement:
lemma lrl_cyclic_angularMomentum (ε : ℝˣ) (i j k : Fin d) :
    H.lrlOperator ε k ∘L 𝐋 i j + H.lrlOperator ε i ∘L 𝐋 j k + H.lrlOperator ε j ∘L 𝐋 k i = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrl_commutation_lrl
declarations.doc: `⁅𝐀(ε)ᵢ, 𝐀(ε)ⱼ⁆ = (-2iℏm·𝐇(ε) + iℏmkε²·𝐫(ε)⁻³)𝐋ᵢⱼ`
declarations.statement:
lemma lrl_commutation_lrl (ε : ℝˣ) (i j : Fin d) :
    ⁅H.lrlOperator ε i, H.lrlOperator ε j⁆ = ((-2 * I * ℏ * H.m) • H.hamiltonianRegCLM ε
    + (I * ℏ * H.m * H.k * ε.1 ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (-3)) ∘L 𝐋 i j

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.hamiltonianReg_commutation_lrl
declarations.doc: `⁅𝐇(ε), 𝐀(ε)ᵢ⁆ = iℏk·ε²𝐫(ε)⁻³𝐩ᵢ - 3ℏ²k/2·ε²𝐫(ε)⁻⁵𝐱ᵢ`
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonianReg_commutation_lrl (ε : ℝˣ) (i : Fin d) :
    ⁅H.hamiltonianRegCLM ε, H.lrlOperator ε i⁆ = (I * ℏ * H.k * ε.1 ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (-3) ∘L 𝐩 i
    - (3 / 2 * ℏ ^ 2 * H.k * ε.1 ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (-5) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lrlOperatorSqr_eq
declarations.doc:
The square of the (regularized) LRL vector operator is related to the (regularized) Hamiltonian
`𝐇(ε)` of the hydrogen atom, square of the angular momentum `𝐋²` and powers of `𝐫(ε)` as
`𝐀(ε)² = 2m·𝐇(ε)(𝐋² + ¼ℏ²(d-1)²) + m²k²(𝟙 - ε²·𝐫(ε)⁻²) - ½(d-1)mkℏ²ε²𝐫(ε)⁻³`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lrlOperatorSqr_eq (ε : ℝˣ) : H.lrlOperator ε ⬝ᵥ H.lrlOperator ε =
    (2 * H.m) • (H.hamiltonianRegCLM ε) ∘L
      (𝐋² + (4⁻¹ * ℏ ^ 2 * (d - 1) ^ 2 : ℝ) • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ))
    + (H.m ^ 2 * H.k ^ 2) • (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) - ε.1 ^ 2 • 𝐫₀ ε (-2))
    - (2⁻¹ * ℏ^2 * H.m * H.k * (d - 1) * ε.1 ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (-3)

modules.title: The Rydberg formula and the spectral series of the hydrogen atom
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The bound-state energies expected for the `d`-dimensional hydrogen atom with potential `-k / r`
are `E_n = -Ry / (n + (d - 1) / 2) ^ 2` for `n : ℕ`, with the Rydberg energy
`Ry = m k ^ 2 / (2 ℏ ^ 2)`. This module defines these Bohr levels and derives from them, by
algebra alone, the Rydberg formula for the energy, the frequency and the wavelength of the
photon emitted in a transition between two levels, together with the Lyman, Balmer and Paschen
series and their series limits.

The statement that these values are the point spectrum of the hydrogen Hamiltonian is not
proved here; it is a separate TODO of the `Basic` module. Nothing in this module depends on
the Hamiltonian.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `rydbergEnergy` : the Rydberg energy `Ry = m k ^ 2 / (2 ℏ ^ 2)`.
- `levelIndex` : the effective principal quantum number `L n = n + (d - 1) / 2`.
- `energyLevel` : the Bohr levels `E_n = -Ry / L n ^ 2`.
- `transitionFrequency` : the frequency `ν = (E_{n₂} - E_{n₁}) / h` of the photon emitted in
    the transition from `n₂` to `n₁`, and `wavelength` its wavelength `c / ν`.
- `rydbergFrequency` : the Rydberg frequency `R_ν = Ry / h`.
- `lymanFrequency`, `balmerFrequency`, `paschenFrequency` : the three classical series.

Lemmas:
- `energyLevel_strictMono` : the Bohr levels increase strictly with `n` when `2 ≤ d`
    and `k ≠ 0`.
- `transitionFrequency_eq` : the Rydberg formula `ν = R_ν (1 / L n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / L n₂ ^ 2)`.
- `wavelength_inv` : its wavenumber form `1 / λ = (R_ν / c) (1 / L n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / L n₂ ^ 2)`.
- `tendsto_transitionFrequency` : the series limit `ν → R_ν / L n₁ ^ 2` as `n₂ → ∞`.
- `balmerFrequency_lt_lymanFrequency` : for `2 ≤ d ≤ 5`, every Balmer line lies below every
    Lyman line.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The level index
- B. The Bohr levels
- C. Transitions and the Rydberg formula
- D. The spectral series

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## B. The Bohr levels

The Rydberg energy `Ry = m k ^ 2 / (2 ℏ ^ 2)` sets the scale of the spectrum, and the level
index `L n = n + (d - 1) / 2` is the effective principal quantum number in dimension `d`; for
`d = 3` it is `n + 1`, the usual principal quantum number, with `n = 0` the ground state.

## C. Transitions and the Rydberg formula

A transition from the level `n₂` down to the level `n₁` emits a photon of energy
`E_{n₂} - E_{n₁}`, frequency `ν = (E_{n₂} - E_{n₁}) / h` and wavelength `λ = c / ν`, with `c` the
speed of light. The Rydberg formula expresses these through the Rydberg frequency `R_ν = Ry / h`,
the frequency of a photon carrying the Rydberg energy.

The same definitions are used for any pair of levels. When `2 ≤ d` and `k ≠ 0` and `n₂ < n₁`,
the level `n₂` lies below `n₁`: the transition from `n₂` to `n₁` goes up and absorbs a photon, and
the frequency and the wavelength defined here are then negative, their absolute values being
those of the absorbed photon. For `n₁ = n₂` there is no photon and the frequency is `0`.

## D. The spectral series

The Lyman, Balmer and Paschen series collect the transitions down to the levels of index `0`,
`1` and `2`; for `d = 3` these are the levels `n = 1`, `2` and `3` of the usual numbering.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex
declarations.doc:
The level index `n + (d - 1) / 2` of the `n`-th Bohr level; for `d = 3` it is the principal
quantum number `n + 1`.
declarations.statement: def levelIndex (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex_eq
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the level index.
declarations.statement: lemma levelIndex_eq (n : ℕ) : levelIndex d n = n + ((d : ℝ) - 1) / 2

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex_pos
declarations.doc: The level index is positive when `2 ≤ d`.
declarations.statement: lemma levelIndex_pos (hd : 2 ≤ d) (n : ℕ) : 0 < levelIndex d n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex_nonneg
declarations.doc: The level index is non-negative when `d ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma levelIndex_nonneg [NeZero d] (n : ℕ) : 0 ≤ levelIndex d n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex_strictMono
declarations.doc: The level index is strictly increasing.
declarations.statement: lemma levelIndex_strictMono : StrictMono (levelIndex d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.levelIndex_monotone
declarations.doc: The level index is monotone.
declarations.statement: lemma levelIndex_monotone : Monotone (levelIndex d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergEnergy
declarations.doc: The Rydberg energy of the atom, `Ry = m k ^ 2 / (2 ℏ ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement: def rydbergEnergy : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergEnergy_eq
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the Rydberg energy.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergEnergy_eq : H.rydbergEnergy = H.m * H.k ^ 2 / (2 * (ℏ : ℝ) ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th Bohr level `E_n = -Ry / (n + (d - 1) / 2) ^ 2`.

These are the bound-state energies expected for the hydrogen Hamiltonian; that they form its
point spectrum is not proved here. For `d = 1` and `n = 0` the level index vanishes and the value
is `0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.
declarations.statement: def energyLevel (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_eq
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the Bohr levels.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_eq (n : ℕ) : H.energyLevel n = -H.rydbergEnergy / levelIndex d n ^ 2

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergEnergy_nonneg
declarations.doc: The Rydberg energy is non-negative.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergEnergy_nonneg : 0 ≤ H.rydbergEnergy

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergEnergy_pos
declarations.doc: The Rydberg energy is positive when `k ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergEnergy_pos (hk : H.k ≠ 0) : 0 < H.rydbergEnergy

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergEnergy_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The Rydberg energy vanishes when `k = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergEnergy_eq_zero (hk : H.k = 0) : H.rydbergEnergy = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_nonpos
declarations.doc: The Bohr levels are non-positive.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_nonpos (n : ℕ) : H.energyLevel n ≤ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_neg
declarations.doc: The Bohr levels are negative when `2 ≤ d` and `k ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_neg (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hk : H.k ≠ 0) (n : ℕ) : H.energyLevel n < 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The Bohr levels vanish when `k = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_eq_zero (hk : H.k = 0) (n : ℕ) : H.energyLevel n = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_strictMono
declarations.doc: The Bohr levels are strictly increasing when `2 ≤ d` and `k ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_strictMono (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hk : H.k ≠ 0) : StrictMono H.energyLevel

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.energyLevel_monotone
declarations.doc:
The Bohr levels are monotone when `2 ≤ d`. The hypothesis on `d` cannot be dropped:
for `d = 1` the level index of `n = 0` vanishes, so that `E_0 = 0` by the convention
`x / 0 = 0` while every other level is negative.
declarations.statement: lemma energyLevel_monotone (hd : 2 ≤ d) : Monotone H.energyLevel

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionEnergy
declarations.doc: The energy `E_{n₂} - E_{n₁}` of the transition from the level `n₂` to the level `n₁`.
declarations.statement: def transitionEnergy (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionEnergy_eq_sub
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the transition energy.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionEnergy_eq_sub (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.transitionEnergy n₁ n₂ = H.energyLevel n₂ - H.energyLevel n₁

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency
declarations.doc:
The frequency `(E_{n₂} - E_{n₁}) / h` of the transition from `n₂` to `n₁`. When `2 ≤ d` and
`k ≠ 0`, it is positive for `n₁ < n₂` (`transitionFrequency_pos`): the transition emits a photon
of this frequency. For `n₂ < n₁` it is negative (`transitionFrequency_neg`): the transition goes
up in energy and absorbs a photon, whose frequency is the absolute value `(E_{n₁} - E_{n₂}) / h`
(`transitionFrequency_swap`). For `n₁ = n₂` it is `0` (`transitionFrequency_self`).
declarations.statement: def transitionFrequency (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_eq_div
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the transition frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_eq_div (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂ = H.transitionEnergy n₁ n₂ / (h : ℝ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_swap
declarations.doc: Exchanging the two levels changes the sign of the transition frequency.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_swap (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.transitionFrequency n₂ n₁ = -H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_self
declarations.doc: The transition frequency between a level and itself is `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma transitionFrequency_self (n : ℕ) : H.transitionFrequency n n = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergFrequency
declarations.doc:
The Rydberg frequency `R_ν = Ry / h`, the frequency of a photon whose energy is the Rydberg
energy.
declarations.statement: abbrev rydbergFrequency : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.wavelength
declarations.doc:
The wavelength `c / ν` of the photon emitted in the transition from `n₂` to `n₁`, with `c` the
speed of light. When `2 ≤ d` and `k ≠ 0` and `n₂ < n₁`, the frequency is negative and so is this
wavelength; its absolute value is the wavelength of the photon absorbed in the transition from
`n₂` up to `n₁`. For `n₁ = n₂` there is no photon: the frequency is `0` and the value `c / 0 = 0`
is a junk value, not a wavelength.
declarations.statement: def wavelength (c : SpeedOfLight) (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.wavelength_eq_div
declarations.doc: The defining formula of the wavelength.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavelength_eq_div (c : SpeedOfLight) (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.wavelength c n₁ n₂ = c / H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionEnergy_eq
declarations.doc:
The Rydberg formula for the transition energy,
`E_{n₂} - E_{n₁} = Ry (1 / L n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / L n₂ ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionEnergy_eq (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.transitionEnergy n₁ n₂ =
      H.rydbergEnergy * (1 / levelIndex d n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / levelIndex d n₂ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergFrequency_eq
declarations.doc:
The Rydberg frequency in terms of the mass, the coupling constant and `ℏ`,
`R_ν = m k ^ 2 / (4 π ℏ ^ 3)`, using `h = 2 π ℏ`.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergFrequency_eq : H.rydbergFrequency = H.m * H.k ^ 2 / (4 * π * (ℏ : ℝ) ^ 3)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergFrequency_nonneg
declarations.doc: The Rydberg frequency is non-negative.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergFrequency_nonneg : 0 ≤ H.rydbergFrequency

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergFrequency_pos
declarations.doc:
The Rydberg frequency is positive when `k ≠ 0`. Not `@[simp]`: since `rydbergFrequency` is an
abbreviation, `simp` already gets this from `rydbergEnergy_pos` and `h_pos`.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergFrequency_pos (hk : H.k ≠ 0) : 0 < H.rydbergFrequency

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.rydbergFrequency_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The Rydberg frequency vanishes when `k = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma rydbergFrequency_eq_zero (hk : H.k = 0) : H.rydbergFrequency = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_eq
declarations.doc: The Rydberg formula for the frequency, `ν = R_ν (1 / L n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / L n₂ ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_eq (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂ =
      H.rydbergFrequency * (1 / levelIndex d n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / levelIndex d n₂ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_pos
declarations.doc:
The frequency of a transition from `n₂` down to `n₁ < n₂` is positive when `2 ≤ d` and
`k ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_pos (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hk : H.k ≠ 0) {n₁ n₂ : ℕ} (hn : n₁ < n₂) :
    0 < H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_neg
declarations.doc:
The frequency of a transition from `n₂` up to `n₁`, with `n₂ < n₁`, is negative when `2 ≤ d`
and `k ≠ 0`: the transition absorbs a photon.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_neg (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hk : H.k ≠ 0) {n₁ n₂ : ℕ} (hn : n₂ < n₁) :
    H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂ < 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.wavelength_inv
declarations.doc:
The Rydberg formula for the wavenumber,
`1 / λ = (R_ν / c) (1 / L n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / L n₂ ^ 2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma wavelength_inv (c : SpeedOfLight) (n₁ n₂ : ℕ) :
    (H.wavelength c n₁ n₂)⁻¹ =
      H.rydbergFrequency / c * (1 / levelIndex d n₁ ^ 2 - 1 / levelIndex d n₂ ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_strictMono
declarations.doc:
For a fixed lower level, the transition frequency is strictly increasing in the upper level
when `2 ≤ d` and `k ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_strictMono (hd : 2 ≤ d) (hk : H.k ≠ 0) (n₁ : ℕ) :
    StrictMono (H.transitionFrequency n₁)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.transitionFrequency_monotone
declarations.doc:
For a fixed lower level, the transition frequency is monotone in the upper level when
`2 ≤ d`. The hypothesis on `k` can be dropped, but not the one on `d`: for `d = 1` the level
index of `n = 0` vanishes and `1 / L 0 ^ 2 = 0` by the convention `x / 0 = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transitionFrequency_monotone (hd : 2 ≤ d) (n₁ : ℕ) :
    Monotone (H.transitionFrequency n₁)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.tendsto_transitionFrequency
declarations.doc:
The series limit: as the upper level goes to infinity, the transition frequency to the
level `n₁` tends to `R_ν / L n₁ ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tendsto_transitionFrequency (n₁ : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun n₂ : ℕ => H.transitionFrequency n₁ n₂) atTop
      (𝓝 (H.rydbergFrequency / levelIndex d n₁ ^ 2))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.lymanFrequency
declarations.doc: The Lyman series: the transitions down to the level of index `0`.
declarations.statement: abbrev lymanFrequency (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.balmerFrequency
declarations.doc: The Balmer series: the transitions down to the level of index `1`.
declarations.statement: abbrev balmerFrequency (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.paschenFrequency
declarations.doc: The Paschen series: the transitions down to the level of index `2`.
declarations.statement: abbrev paschenFrequency (n : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.HydrogenAtom.balmerFrequency_lt_lymanFrequency
declarations.doc:
For `2 ≤ d ≤ 5`, every Balmer line has a lower frequency than every Lyman line: the Balmer
series limit `R_ν / L 1 ^ 2` is at most the first Lyman line `R_ν (1 / L 0 ^ 2 - 1 / L 1 ^ 2)`,
which holds exactly when `2 L 0 ^ 2 ≤ L 1 ^ 2`, that is `d ^ 2 - 6 d + 1 ≤ 0`. This fails for
`6 ≤ d`: in dimension `6` the Balmer line `n₂ = 15` has exactly the frequency
`96 R_ν / 1225` of the first Lyman line, and the Balmer lines above it are faster still.

The Balmer lines are the transitions with `1 < n₂`, but that hypothesis is not needed here: for
`n₂ ≤ 1` the left-hand side is non-positive while the right-hand side is positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma balmerFrequency_lt_lymanFrequency (hd₂ : 2 ≤ d) (hd₅ : d ≤ 5) (hk : H.k ≠ 0)
    {n₂ n₃ : ℕ} (h₃ : 0 < n₃) : H.balmerFrequency n₂ < H.lymanFrequency n₃

modules.title: The infinite square well
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The particle in an infinite square well is one of the simplest quantum systems.
The domain is an axis-aligned cuboid (the well) and energy eigenstates are (products of)
trigonometric functions satisfying appropriate boundary conditions.

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic properties
- B. Domain
- C. Hilbert space
- D. Hamiltonian
- E. As a quantum system

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell
declarations.doc:
A spinless quantum particle with mass `m > 0` confined to a cuboid in `Space d`.

The bounds of the well are specified by two functions `lower upper : Fin d → ℝ`
satisfying `∀ i, lower i < upper i`.
declarations.statement:
structure InfiniteSquareWell (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The mass (positive). -/
  m : ℝ
  hm : 0 < m
  /-- The lower bounds of the well. -/
  lower : Fin d → ℝ
  /-- The upper bounds of the well. -/
  upper : Fin d → ℝ
  /-- The well is a non-empty set. -/
  h_bounds : ∀ i, lower i < upper i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.m_pos
declarations.statement: lemma m_pos : 0 < Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.m_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma m_nonneg : 0 ≤ Q.m

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.m_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma m_ne_zero : Q.m ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.well
declarations.doc: The domain of the infinite square well as a Cartesian product of closed intervals.
declarations.statement: def well : Set (Space d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.measure
declarations.doc: The measure associated with the domain of the infinite square well.
declarations.statement: def measure : Measure (Space d)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.InfiniteSquareWell.HS
declarations.doc: The Hilbert space for the infinite square well.
declarations.statement: abbrev HS : Type _

modules.title: Angular momentum operator
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we introduce several angular momentum operators for quantum mechanics on `Space d`.
Each component also acts symmetrically on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d` with domain `SchwartzSubmodule d`.
We prove its symmetry and commutation relations.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `angularMomentumCLM` : (components of) the angular momentum operator acting on Schwartz maps
    `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` as `𝐱ᵢ∘𝐩ⱼ - 𝐱ⱼ∘𝐩ᵢ`.
- `angularMomentumOperatorSqr` : the operator acting on Schwartz maps `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)`
    as `½ ∑ᵢⱼ 𝐋ᵢⱼ∘𝐋ᵢⱼ`.
- `angularMomentumOperator2D` : the (pseudo)scalar angular momentum operator for `d = 2`.
- `angularMomentumOperator3D` : the (pseudo)vector angular momentum operator for `d = 3`.
- `angularMomentumOperator` : each component as a partially defined operator on
    `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`, preserving the dense Schwartz submodule.
- `angularMomentumSqOperator` : angular momentum squared on the same Schwartz domain.

Lemmas:
- `angularMomentumOperator_isSymmetric` : angular momentum is symmetric on the Schwartz domain.
- `angularMomentumSqOperator_isSymmetric` : its sum of component squares is also symmetric.
- `angularMomentum_commutation_angularMomentum` : angular momenta generate an `𝔰𝔬(d)` algebra.

Notation:
- `𝐋` for `angularMomentumCLM`
- `𝐋²` for `angularMomentumOperatorSqr`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Angular momentum operator
  - A.1 Antisymmetry
- B. Angular momentum squared operator
- C. Special cases in low dimensions
- D. Hilbert-space angular momentum operator
  - D.1. Angular momentum squared on the Hilbert space
- E. Algebraic relations
  - E.1. Angular momentum / position
  - E.2. Angular momentum / momentum
  - E.3. Angular momentum / angular momentum
  - E.4. Angular momentum / dilation operator

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## C. Special cases in low dimensions

  • d = 1 : The angular momentum operator is trivial.

  • d = 2 : The angular momentum operator has only one independent component, 𝐋₀₁, which may
            be thought of as a (pseudo)scalar operator.

  • d = 3 : The angular momentum operator has three independent components, 𝐋₀₁, 𝐋₁₂ and 𝐋₂₀.
            Dualizing using the Levi-Civita symbol produces the familiar (pseudo)vector angular
            momentum operator with components 𝐋₀ = 𝐋₁₂, 𝐋₁ = 𝐋₂₀ and 𝐋₂ = 𝐋₀₁.
### D.1. Angular momentum squared on the Hilbert space

### E.4. Angular momentum / dilation operator

Angular momentum commutes with the dilation operator `𝐱 · 𝐩`.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM
declarations.doc:
Component `i j` of the angular momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself defined by `𝐋ᵢⱼ ≔ 𝐱ᵢ∘𝐩ⱼ - 𝐱ⱼ∘𝐩ᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def angularMomentumCLM {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM_apply_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumCLM_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐋 i j ψ = 𝐱 i (𝐩 j ψ) - 𝐱 j (𝐩 i ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumCLM_apply {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐋 i j ψ x = 𝐱 i (𝐩 j ψ) x - 𝐱 j (𝐩 i ψ) x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM_antisymm
declarations.doc: The angular momentum operator is antisymmetric, `𝐋ᵢⱼ = -𝐋ⱼᵢ`
declarations.statement: lemma angularMomentumCLM_antisymm {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) : 𝐋 i j = -𝐋 j i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Angular momentum operator components with repeated index vanish, `𝐋ᵢᵢ = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma angularMomentumCLM_eq_zero {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d) : 𝐋 i i = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr
declarations.doc: The square of the angular momentum operator, `𝐋² ≔ ½ ∑ᵢⱼ 𝐋ᵢⱼ∘𝐋ᵢⱼ`.
declarations.statement: def angularMomentumOperatorSqr {d : ℕ} : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐋² ψ = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • ∑ i, ∑ j, 𝐋 i j (𝐋 i j ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperatorSqr_apply {d : ℕ} (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐋² ψ x = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, ∑ j, 𝐋 i j (𝐋 i j ψ) x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator1D_trivial
declarations.doc: In one dimension the angular momentum operator is trivial.
declarations.statement: lemma angularMomentumOperator1D_trivial : 𝐋[1] = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator2D
declarations.doc: The angular momentum (pseudo)scalar operator in two dimensions, `𝐋 ≔ 𝐋₀₁`.
declarations.statement: def angularMomentumOperator2D : 𝓢(Space 2, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space 2, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator3D
declarations.doc:
The angular momentum (pseudo)vector operator in three dimensions, `𝐋ᵢ ≔ ½ ∑ⱼₖ εᵢⱼₖ 𝐋ⱼₖ`.
The transpose matches the convention of `Matrix.crossProductVee`, giving `(𝐋₁₂, 𝐋₂₀, 𝐋₀₁)`.
declarations.statement: def angularMomentumOperator3D (i : Fin 3) : 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space 3, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator
declarations.doc:
Component `i j` of angular momentum on the Hilbert space, with Schwartz domain.
This transports the existing Schwartz-space operator `𝐋 i j`.
declarations.statement: def angularMomentumOperator : SpaceDHilbertSpace d →ₗ.[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_domain_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_domain_eq :
    (angularMomentumOperator i j).domain = SchwartzSubmodule d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_apply (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    angularMomentumOperator i j ψ =
      schwartzEquiv volume (𝐋 i j ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_apply_ae
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_apply_ae (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    angularMomentumOperator i j ψ =ᵐ[volume] 𝐋 i j ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_range
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_range (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    angularMomentumOperator i j ψ ∈ SchwartzSubmodule d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_hasDenseDomain
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_hasDenseDomain :
    (angularMomentumOperator i j).HasDenseDomain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumCLM_eq_momentum_position
declarations.doc: Reversing the order of position and momentum leaves angular momentum unchanged.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumCLM_eq_momentum_position :
    𝐋 i j = 𝐩 j ∘L 𝐱 i - 𝐩 i ∘L 𝐱 j

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_isSymmetric
declarations.doc: Each angular momentum component is symmetric on the Schwartz domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_isSymmetric :
    (angularMomentumOperator i j).IsSymmetric

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentumOperator_isUnbounded
declarations.doc: Angular momentum on the Schwartz domain is densely defined and closable.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumOperator_isUnbounded :
    (angularMomentumOperator i j).IsUnbounded

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentum_cyclic_position
declarations.doc:
`𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐱ₖ + 𝐋ⱼₖ𝐱ᵢ + 𝐋ₖᵢ𝐱ⱼ = 0`; in three dimensions this is `𝐋 · 𝐱 = 0`.
The identity is trivial unless `i`, `j`, `k` are pairwise distinct, so it has no content in
fewer than three dimensions.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_cyclic_position :
    𝐋 i j ∘L 𝐱 k + 𝐋 j k ∘L 𝐱 i + 𝐋 k i ∘L 𝐱 j = 0

declarations.statement:

declarations.statement: lemma angularMomentumSqr_commutation_momentumSqr : ⁅𝐋²[d], 𝐩[d] ⬝ᵥ 𝐩⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.angularMomentum_cyclic_momentum
declarations.doc:
`𝐋ᵢⱼ𝐩ₖ + 𝐋ⱼₖ𝐩ᵢ + 𝐋ₖᵢ𝐩ⱼ = 0`; in three dimensions this is `𝐋 · 𝐩 = 0`.
The identity is trivial unless `i`, `j`, `k` are pairwise distinct, so it has no content in
fewer than three dimensions.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_cyclic_momentum :
    𝐋 i j ∘L 𝐩 k + 𝐋 j k ∘L 𝐩 i + 𝐋 k i ∘L 𝐩 j = 0

declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_commutation_angularMomentum : ⁅𝐋 i j, 𝐋 k l⁆ =

declarations.statement: lemma angularMomentumSqr_commutation_angularMomentum : ⁅𝐋²[d], 𝐋 i j⁆ = 0

modules.title: Three-dimensional angular momentum
modules.doc:
Cartesian components, commutation relations, and ladder operators on the Schwartz domain.

## i. Overview

The Cartesian components use the right-handed convention
`Lx = L₁₂`, `Ly = L₂₀`, `Lz = L₀₁`, with coordinate indices `0, 1, 2`.
The Schwartz operators are the existing `angularMomentumOperator3D`; the Hilbert-space
operators have the common invariant domain `SchwartzSubmodule 3`.
Their commutation algebra and the raising/lowering operators are proved first on Schwartz maps
and then transported to this Hilbert-space domain. In particular, a zero commutator means zero
on that domain; it is not an equality with the everywhere-defined zero `LinearPMap`.

## ii. Key results

- `angularMomentumDimThreeOperator`: the Hilbert-space Cartesian components.
- `angularMomentumOperatorSqr_eq_sum_dimThree`: `L² = Lx² + Ly² + Lz²` on Schwartz maps.
- `angularMomentumDimThreeOperator_isSymmetric`: symmetry of each Cartesian component.
- `angularMomentumDimThree_commutation`: `[Li, Lj] = iℏ ∑k εijk Lk`.
- `angularMomentumRaisingCLM`, `angularMomentumLoweringCLM`: `Lx ± i Ly` on Schwartz maps.
- `angularMomentumRaisingOperator`, `angularMomentumLoweringOperator`: their Hilbert-space lifts.
- `angularMomentumZOperator_commutation_raising`, `angularMomentumZOperator_commutation_lowering`:
  `[Lz, L±] = ±ℏ L±` on the Schwartz domain.
- `angularMomentumSqOperator_commutation_raising`, `angularMomentumSqOperator_commutation_lowering`:
  `[L², L±] = 0` on that domain.

Open the `AngularMomentum` scope for `𝐋₃ i` on Schwartz maps and `𝓛₃ i` on the Hilbert space,
where `i : Fin 3` and indices `0`, `1`, `2` correspond to `x`, `y`, `z`.
The notation `𝓛²` denotes the Hilbert-space square.
The same scope provides `𝐋⁺`, `𝐋⁻` and `𝓛⁺`, `𝓛⁻` for the ladder operators.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cartesian components
  - A.1. Hilbert-space transport
  - A.2. Sum of the three squares
- B. Commutation algebra
- C. Ladder operators
  - C.1. Hilbert-space ladder operators
  - C.2. Hilbert-space commutation relations on the invariant domain

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ### A.2. Sum of the three squares

## B. Commutation algebra

The bracket below is the existing commutator of continuous linear maps on Schwartz space.
Hilbert-space statements are evaluated on `SchwartzSubmodule 3`, with explicit membership
proofs for intermediate vectors. They make no claims about domains of closed extensions.

## C. Ladder operators

These operators act on arbitrary Schwartz vectors. No eigenstate or spectral assumptions
are used in their commutation relations.
### C.2. Hilbert-space commutation relations on the invariant domain

modules.title: Commutation relations
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we compute the commutators of position and momentum operators on Schwartz maps
on `Space d`, including regularized powers of the radius.

Commutator lemmas come in three flavors:
  - 1. `a_commutation_b` lemmas are of the form `⁅a, b⁆ = (⋯)`.
  - 2. `a_comp_b_commute` and `a_comp_commute` lemmas are of the form `a ∘ b = b ∘ a`.
  - 3. `a_comp_b_eq` lemmas are of the form `a ∘ b = b ∘ a + (⋯)`.

## ii. Key results

- `position_commutation_momentum` : The canonical commutation relations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. General
- B. Commutators
  - B.1. Position / position
  - B.2. Momentum / momentum
  - B.3. Position / momentum

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.leibniz_lie
declarations.statement:
lemma leibniz_lie (A B C : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⁅A ∘L B, C⁆ = A ∘L ⁅B, C⁆ + ⁅A, C⁆ ∘L B

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.lie_leibniz
declarations.statement:
lemma lie_leibniz (A B C : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⁅A, B ∘L C⁆ = B ∘L ⁅A, C⁆ + ⁅A, B⁆ ∘L C

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.comp_eq_comp_add_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_eq_comp_add_commute (A B : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    A ∘L B = B ∘L A + ⁅A, B⁆

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.id_commutation
declarations.doc: The identity commutes with everything.
declarations.statement:
lemma id_commutation (A : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⁅ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ), A⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.comp_eq_comp_sub_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma comp_eq_comp_sub_commute (A B : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    A ∘L B = B ∘L A - ⁅B, A⁆

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_position
declarations.doc: Position operators commute: `[xᵢ, xⱼ] = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma position_commutation_position : ⁅𝐱 i, 𝐱 j⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_comp_commute
declarations.statement: lemma position_comp_commute : 𝐱 i ∘L 𝐱 j = 𝐱 j ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_radiusRegPow
declarations.statement: lemma position_commutation_radiusRegPow : ⁅𝐱 i, 𝐫₀[d] ε s⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_comp_radiusRegPow_commute
declarations.statement: lemma position_comp_radiusRegPow_commute : 𝐱 i ∘L 𝐫₀ ε s = 𝐫₀ ε s ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPow_commutation_radiusRegPow
declarations.statement: lemma radiusRegPow_commutation_radiusRegPow : ⁅𝐫₀[d] ε s, 𝐫₀[d] ε t⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentum_commutation_momentum
declarations.doc: Momentum operators commute: `[pᵢ, pⱼ] = 0`.
declarations.statement: lemma momentum_commutation_momentum : ⁅𝐩 i, 𝐩 j⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentum_comp_commute
declarations.statement: lemma momentum_comp_commute : 𝐩 i ∘L 𝐩 j = 𝐩 j ∘L 𝐩 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumSqr_commutation_momentum
declarations.statement: lemma momentumSqr_commutation_momentum : ⁅𝐩[d] ⬝ᵥ 𝐩, 𝐩 i⁆ = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumSqr_comp_momentum_commute
declarations.statement: lemma momentumSqr_comp_momentum_commute : (𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩) ∘L 𝐩 i = 𝐩 i ∘L (𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_momentum
declarations.doc: The canonical commutation relations: `[xᵢ, pⱼ] = iℏ δᵢⱼ𝟙`.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_commutation_momentum : ⁅𝐱 i, 𝐩 j⁆ =
    (I * ℏ) • δ[i,j] • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_momentum_apply
declarations.doc: The canonical commutation relations, pointwise: `xᵢ (pᵢ ψ)(x) - (pᵢ (xᵢ ψ))(x) = iℏ ψ(x)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_commutation_momentum_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    ((x i : ℝ) : ℂ) * 𝐩 i ψ x - 𝐩 i (𝐱 i ψ) x = I * ℏ * ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentum_comp_position_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma momentum_comp_position_eq : 𝐩 j ∘L 𝐱 i =
    𝐱 i ∘L 𝐩 j - (I * ℏ) • δ[i,j] • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_position_commutation_momentum
declarations.statement:
lemma position_position_commutation_momentum : ⁅𝐱 i ∘L 𝐱 j, 𝐩 k⁆ =
    (I * ℏ) • (δ[i,k] • 𝐱 j + δ[j,k] • 𝐱 i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_momentum_momentum
declarations.statement:
lemma position_commutation_momentum_momentum : ⁅𝐱 i, 𝐩 j ∘L 𝐩 k⁆ =
    (I * ℏ) • (δ[i,k] • 𝐩 j + δ[i,j] • 𝐩 k)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.position_commutation_momentumSqr
declarations.statement: lemma position_commutation_momentumSqr : ⁅𝐱 i, 𝐩 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩⁆ = (2 * I * ℏ) • 𝐩 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPow_commutation_momentum
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPow_commutation_momentum :
    ⁅𝐫₀[d] ε s, 𝐩 i⁆ = (s * I * ℏ) • 𝐫₀ ε (s-2) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentum_comp_radiusRegPow_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma momentum_comp_radiusRegPow_eq :
    𝐩 i ∘L 𝐫₀ ε s = 𝐫₀ ε s ∘L 𝐩 i - (s * I * ℏ) • 𝐫₀ ε (s-2) ∘L 𝐱 i

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPow_commutation_momentumSqr
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPow_commutation_momentumSqr :
    ⁅𝐫₀[d] ε s, 𝐩[d] ⬝ᵥ 𝐩⁆ = (2 * s * I * ℏ) • 𝐫₀ ε (s-2) ∘L (𝐱 ⬝ᵥ 𝐩)
    + (s * (d + s - 2) * ℏ ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (s-2) - (ε ^ 2 * s * (s - 2) * ℏ ^ 2) • 𝐫₀ ε (s-4)

modules.title: Covariance
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the covariance of two partial linear maps `A` and `B` in a common state
`ψ` as the real part of the inner product of their centered vectors.

## ii. Key results

- `covariance` : the real part of the centered inner product.
- `covariance_comm` : covariance is symmetric in the two observables.
- `covariance_eq_re_symm_centered` : covariance as the real part of the symmetrized centered
  inner product.
- `covariance_self_eq_variance` : the covariance of an observable with itself is its variance.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Covariance

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chapter 12. [ref: hall2013quantum]

declarations.name: LinearPMap.covariance
declarations.doc: Covariance, defined as the real part of the centered inner product.
declarations.statement: def covariance : ℝ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.covariance_eq_re_inner_centered
declarations.doc: Covariance, unfolded to the real part of the centered inner product.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_eq_re_inner_centered :
    covariance A B ψ hψB =
      (⟪centered A ψ, centered B ⟨ψ, hψB⟩⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: LinearPMap.covariance_comm
declarations.doc: Swapping the two observables does not change the covariance.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_comm :
    covariance A B ψ hψB = covariance B A ⟨ψ, hψB⟩ ψ.2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.covariance_eq_re_symm_centered
declarations.doc: Covariance as the real part of the symmetrized centered inner product.
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_eq_re_symm_centered :
    covariance A B ψ hψB =
      ((⟪centered A ψ, centered B ⟨ψ, hψB⟩⟫_ℂ +
        ⟪centered B ⟨ψ, hψB⟩, centered A ψ⟫_ℂ).re) / 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.covariance_self_eq_variance
declarations.statement:
lemma covariance_self_eq_variance (A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : A.domain) :
    covariance A A ψ (by exact ψ.2) = variance A ψ
