modules.title: Momentum operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we introduce several momentum operators for quantum mechanics on `Space d`.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `momentumCLM` : (components of) the momentum vector operator acting on Schwartz maps
    `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` as `-iℏ∂ᵢ`.
- `momentumOperator` : a symmetric unbounded operator acting on the Schwartz submodule
    of the Hilbert space `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`.

Notation:
- `𝐩` for `momentumOperator`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Momentum vector operator
- B. Unbounded momentum vector operator

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumCLM
declarations.doc:
Component `i` of the momentum operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `-iℏ ∂ᵢψ`.
declarations.statement: def momentumCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumCLM_apply_fun
declarations.statement: lemma momentumCLM_apply_fun (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) : 𝐩 i ψ = (-I * ℏ) • ∂[i] ψ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumCLM_apply
declarations.statement: lemma momentumCLM_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) : 𝐩 i ψ x = -I * ℏ * ∂[i] ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator
declarations.doc: The momentum operator as a LinearPMap with domain the Schwartz submodule.
declarations.statement: def momentumOperator : SpaceDHilbertSpace d →ₗ.[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumOperator_apply (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    𝓟 i ψ = schwartzEquiv volume (𝐩 i ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ))

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_apply_ae
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumOperator_apply_ae (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) :
    𝓟 i ψ =ᵐ[volume] 𝐩 i ((schwartzEquiv volume).symm ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_range
declarations.statement: lemma momentumOperator_range (ψ : SchwartzSubmodule d) : 𝓟 i ψ ∈ SchwartzSubmodule d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_hasDenseDomain
declarations.statement: lemma momentumOperator_hasDenseDomain : (𝓟 i).HasDenseDomain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_isSymmetric
declarations.statement: lemma momentumOperator_isSymmetric : (𝓟 i).IsSymmetric

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumCLM_inner
declarations.doc: The momentum operator is symmetric on Schwartz maps, in terms of `momentumCLM`.
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumCLM_inner (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume (𝐩 i f) : SpaceDHilbertSpace d), schwartzEquiv volume g⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(schwartzEquiv volume f : SpaceDHilbertSpace d), schwartzEquiv volume (𝐩 i g)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumOperator_isUnbounded
declarations.statement: lemma momentumOperator_isUnbounded : (𝓟 i).IsUnbounded

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumSqOperator
declarations.doc: The square of the momentum operator.
declarations.statement: def momentumSqOperator : SpaceDHilbertSpace d →ₗ.[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumSqOperator_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma momentumSqOperator_eq :
    momentumSqOperator (d := d) = sum fun i ↦ (𝓟 i).comp (𝓟 i) (momentumOperator_range i)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.momentumSqOperator_domain_eq
declarations.statement: lemma momentumSqOperator_domain_eq : momentumSqOperator.domain = SchwartzSubmodule d

modules.title: Multiplication operators on `SpaceDHilbertSpace`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define and develop the properties of multiplication operators.
Given a measure `μ` on `Space d` and any function `f : Space d → ℂ`, the multiplication operator
`𝓜 μ f` is the partial linear map on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ` with domain
`{ψ : SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ | MemHS (f • ψ) μ}` and mapping `ψ` to `f • ψ`.
Prime examples of multiplication operators are the position operators which multiply by `xᵢ` and
the potential operators which multiply by the potential function `V(x)` of a quantum system.

Although the domain of `𝓜 μ f` is defined implicitly through `MemHS`, simple assumptions on `f`
allow one to nail down some of its properties. For example, when `f` is `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable
then the corresponding multiplication operator is densely defined, if `f` is `μ`-a.e. bounded then
the domain is `⊤` and if `f` has temperate growth then the domain contains the Schwartz submodule.

Multiplication operators also form the backbone for derivative operators, which are defined
through multiplication in the Fourier domain: see `Operators/Derivative.lean`.

## ii. Key results

- `mulOperator μ f` (notation `𝓜 μ f`) : The operator defined by `ψ ↦ f • ψ`
    with maximal domain `{ψ : SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ | MemHS (f • ψ) μ}`.
- `mulOperator_adjoint_eq_conj` : The adjoint of `𝓜 μ f` is the multiplication operator
    defined by the conjugate of `f`.
- `mulOperator_isSelfAdjoint` : The multiplication operator of a real function is self-adjoint.
- `mulOperator_isUnbounded` : Multiplication operators with maximal domain are unbounded
    (i.e. densely defined and closable).
- `mulOperator_isClosed` : Multiplication operators with maximal domain are closed.
- `mulOperator_eq_iff_ae_eq` : `𝓜 μ f = 𝓜 μ g ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] g` for `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable `f`
    and σ-finite `μ`.
- `mulOperator_const_smul_eq` : `𝓜 μ (c • f) = c • 𝓜 μ f` for non-zero `c`.
- `mulOperator_add_ge` / `mulOperator_sub_ge` : `𝓜 μ (f ± g)` is an extension of `𝓜 μ f ± 𝓜 μ g`.
- `mulOperator_smul_ge` : `𝓜 μ (f • g)` is an extension of `𝓜 μ f * 𝓜 μ g`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition
- B. Domain
- C. Adjoint
  - C.1. Self-adjoint
- D. Closed & unbounded
- E. Basic properties
  - E.1. Smul & neg
  - E.2. Add & sub
  - E.3. Composition
- F. Spectrum

## iv. References

* Konrad Schmüdgen, Unbounded Self-Adjoint Operators on Hilbert Space, examples 1.3 and 3.8.
  [ref: Schmudgen2012]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator which maps `ψ` to the equivalence class of `f • ψ`
with maximal domain `{ψ : SpaceDHilbertspace d μ | MemHS (f • ψ) μ}`.
declarations.statement:
def mulOperator (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f : Space d → ℂ) :
    SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ →ₗ.[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mem_mulOperator_domain_iff
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator `𝓜 μ f` has maximal domain: `ψ` is in the domain exactly
when multiplying by `f` gives an element of the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_mulOperator_domain_iff
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} {f : Space d → ℂ} {ψ : SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ} :
    ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ f).domain ↔ MemHS (f • ⇑ψ) μ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_apply_ae
declarations.doc: The defining property of a multiplication operator: `ψ` is mapped to `f • ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_apply_ae {μ : Measure (Space d)} {f : Space d → ℂ} (ψ : (𝓜 μ f).domain) :
    𝓜 μ f ψ =ᵐ[μ] f • ψ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_domain_eq_top
declarations.doc: The multiplication operator of a `μ`-a.e. bounded function has full domain.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_domain_antitone
declarations.doc: The domains of multiplication operators shrink with increasing function norm.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mem_mulOperator_domain_of_ae_eq_indicator
declarations.doc:
A state which is `μ`-a.e. equal to the indicator of a set on which `f` is `μ`-a.e. bounded
lies in the domain of `𝓜 μ f`.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_domain_eq_of_congr_norm
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operators corresponding to functions
of `μ`-a.e. equal norm have the same domain.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_conj_domain
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operators corresponding to a function
and its conjugate have the same domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_conj_domain
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ (conj ∘ f)).domain = (𝓜 μ f).domain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_hasDenseDomain
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator corresponding to a `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable function
is densely defined.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_hasDenseDomain
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ f).HasDenseDomain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_domain_ge_of_hasTemperateGrowth
declarations.doc:
The multiplication operator corresponding to a function of temperate growth
contains all Schwartz maps in its domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_domain_ge_of_hasTemperateGrowth {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : f.HasTemperateGrowth)
    (μ : Measure (Space d)) [μ.HasTemperateGrowth] [μ.IsOpenPosMeasure] :
    SchwartzSubmodule d μ ≤ (𝓜 μ f).domain

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_adjoint_eq_conj
declarations.doc: The adjoint of a multiplication operator is again a multiplication operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_adjoint_eq_conj {μ : Measure (Space d)} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
    {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ f)† = 𝓜 μ (conj ∘ f)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_isSelfAdjoint_ofReal
declarations.doc: The multiplication operator corresponding to a real function is self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_isSelfAdjoint_ofReal {μ : Measure (Space d)} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
    {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (hf' : conj ∘ f = f) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (𝓜 μ f)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_isClosable
declarations.doc: Multiplication operators of `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable functions are closable.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_isClosable {μ : Measure (Space d)} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
    {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ f).IsClosable

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_isUnbounded
declarations.doc: Multiplication operators of `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable functions are unbounded.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_isUnbounded {μ : Measure (Space d)} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
    {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ f).IsUnbounded

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_isClosed
declarations.doc: Multiplication operators of `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable functions are closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_isClosed {μ : Measure (Space d)} [IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ]
    {f : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
    (𝓜 μ f).IsClosed

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_zero
declarations.doc: The multiplication operator of the zero function is the zero operator (domain `⊤`).
declarations.statement: lemma mulOperator_zero (μ : Measure (Space d)) : 𝓜 μ 0 = 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_eq_of_congr_ae
declarations.doc: `μ`-a.e. equal functions give rise to the same multiplication operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_eq_of_congr_ae {μ : Measure (Space d)} {f g : Space d → ℂ} (h : f =ᵐ[μ] g) :
    𝓜 μ f = 𝓜 μ g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_eq_iff_ae_eq
declarations.doc:
For a `μ`-a.e. strongly measurable `f` and σ-finite `μ`, the multiplication
operator determines the function up to `μ`-a.e. equality.
No measurability of `g` is needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_eq_iff_ae_eq {μ : Measure (Space d)} [SigmaFinite μ] {f g : Space d → ℂ}
    (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) : 𝓜 μ f = 𝓜 μ g ↔ f =ᵐ[μ] g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_const_smul_ge
declarations.doc:
Scalar multiplication and `mulOperator` commute except possibly for `c = 0`
where the domains of `0 • 𝓜 μ f` and `𝓜 μ 0 = 0` may not agree.

See `mulOperator_const_smul_eq` for equality when `c ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_const_smul_ge (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f : Space d → ℂ) (c : ℂ) :
    c • 𝓜 μ f ≤ 𝓜 μ (c • f)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_const_smul_eq
declarations.doc: Scalar multiplication and `mulOperator` commute for `c ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_const_smul_eq (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f : Space d → ℂ) {c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0) :
    𝓜 μ (c • f) = c • 𝓜 μ f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_neg
declarations.doc: Negation and `mulOperator` commute.
declarations.statement: lemma mulOperator_neg (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f : Space d → ℂ) : 𝓜 μ (-f) = -𝓜 μ f

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_add_ge
declarations.doc:
`𝓜 μ (f + g)` extends `𝓜 μ f + 𝓜 μ g`.

In general the domains do not match: `ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ f + 𝓜 μ g).domain` amounts to `MemHS (f • ψ) μ`
_and_ `MemHS (g • ψ) μ` whereas `ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ (f + g)).domain` is equivalent to the weaker condition
`MemHS ((f + g) • ψ) μ`.

See `mulOperator_add_eq` and `mulOperator_add_eq'` for sufficient conditions
to ensure equality.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_add_ge (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f g : Space d → ℂ) :
    𝓜 μ f + 𝓜 μ g ≤ 𝓜 μ (f + g)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_add_eq
declarations.doc: `(𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤` is a sufficient condition to ensure equality in `mulOperator_add_ge`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_add_eq
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} (f : Space d → ℂ) {g : Space d → ℂ} (h : (𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤) :
    𝓜 μ (f + g) = 𝓜 μ f + 𝓜 μ g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_add_eq'
declarations.doc:
Having both `‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖f x + g x‖` and `‖g x‖ ≤ c' * ‖f x + g x‖` `μ`-a.e. is a sufficient
condition to ensure equality in `mulOperator_add_ge`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_add_eq' {μ : Measure (Space d)}
    {f g : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ)
    (c c' : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖f x + g x‖) (hg' : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖g x‖ ≤ c' * ‖f x + g x‖) :
    𝓜 μ (f + g) = 𝓜 μ f + 𝓜 μ g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_sub_ge
declarations.doc:
`𝓜 μ (f - g)` extends `𝓜 μ f - 𝓜 μ g`.

In general the domains do not match: `ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ f - 𝓜 μ g).domain` amounts to `MemHS (f • ψ) μ`
_and_ `MemHS (g • ψ) μ` whereas `ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ (f - g)).domain` is equivalent to the weaker condition
`MemHS ((f - g) • ψ) μ`.

See `mulOperator_sub_eq` and `mulOperator_sub_eq'` for sufficient conditions
to ensure equality.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_sub_ge (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f g : Space d → ℂ) :
    𝓜 μ f - 𝓜 μ g ≤ 𝓜 μ (f - g)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_sub_eq
declarations.doc: `(𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤` is a sufficient condition to ensure equality in `mulOperator_sub_ge`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_sub_eq
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} (f : Space d → ℂ) {g : Space d → ℂ} (h : (𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤) :
    𝓜 μ (f - g) = 𝓜 μ f - 𝓜 μ g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_sub_eq'
declarations.doc:
Having both `‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖f x - g x‖` and `‖g x‖ ≤ c' * ‖f x - g x‖` `μ`-a.e. is a sufficient
condition to ensure equality in `mulOperator_sub_ge`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_sub_eq' {μ : Measure (Space d)}
    {f g : Space d → ℂ} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (hg : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ)
    (c c' : ℝ) (hf' : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖f x - g x‖) (hg' : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ‖g x‖ ≤ c' * ‖f x - g x‖) :
    𝓜 μ (f - g) = 𝓜 μ f - 𝓜 μ g

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_smul_ge
declarations.doc:
`𝓜 μ (f • g)` extends `𝓜 μ f * 𝓜 μ g`.

In general the domains do not match: `ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ f * 𝓜 μ g).domain`
amounts to `MemHS (g • ψ) μ` _and_ `MemHS (f • g • ψ) μ` whereas
`ψ ∈ (𝓜 μ (f • g)).domain` only requires `MemHS (f • g • ψ) μ`.

See `mulOperator_smul_eq` for a sufficient condition to ensure equality.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_smul_ge (μ : Measure (Space d)) (f g : Space d → ℂ) :
    𝓜 μ f ∘ᵣ 𝓜 μ g ≤ 𝓜 μ (f • g)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDHilbertSpace.mulOperator_smul_eq
declarations.doc: `(𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤` is a sufficient condition to ensure equality in `mulOperator_smul_ge`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mulOperator_smul_eq
    {μ : Measure (Space d)} (f : Space d → ℂ) {g : Space d → ℂ} (h : (𝓜 μ g).domain = ⊤) :
    𝓜 μ f ∘ᵣ 𝓜 μ g = 𝓜 μ (f • g)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator
declarations.doc:
An unbounded operator on the one-dimensional Hilbert space,
corresponds to a subobject `ι : S →L[ℂ] HilbertSpace` of the Hilbert
space along with the operator `op : S →L[ℂ] HilbertSpace`
declarations.statement:
def UnboundedOperator {S : Type} [AddCommGroup S] [Module ℂ S]
    [TopologicalSpace S] (ι : S →L[ℂ] HilbertSpace)
    (_ : Function.Injective ι)
instance : CoeFun (UnboundedOperator ι hι) (fun _ => S → HilbertSpace)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator.ofSelfCLM
declarations.doc: An unbounded operator created from a continuous linear map ` S →L[ℂ] S`.
declarations.statement: def ofSelfCLM (Op : S →L[ℂ] S) : UnboundedOperator ι hι

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator.ofSelfCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSelfCLM_apply (Op : S →L[ℂ] S) (ψ : S) :
    ofSelfCLM (hι := hι) Op ψ = ι (Op ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator.IsGeneralizedEigenvector
declarations.doc:
A map `F : S →L[ℂ] ℂ` is a generalized eigenvector of an unbounded operator `U`
on `S` if there is an eigenvalue `c` such that for all `ψ`, `F (U ψ) = c ⬝ F ψ`
declarations.statement: def IsGeneralizedEigenvector (F : S →L[ℂ] ℂ) (c : ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator.isGeneralizedEigenvector_ofSelfCLM_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma isGeneralizedEigenvector_ofSelfCLM_iff {Op : S →L[ℂ] S}
    (F : S →L[ℂ] ℂ) (c : ℂ) :
    IsGeneralizedEigenvector (ofSelfCLM (hι := hι) Op) F c ↔
    ∀ ψ : S, F (Op ψ) = c • F ψ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.OneDimension.UnboundedOperator.IsSymmetric
declarations.doc:
The condition for an unbounded operator to be *symmetric* (equivalently, formally
self-adjoint): `⟪U ψ1, ι ψ2⟫ = ⟪ι ψ1, U ψ2⟫` for all `ψ1 ψ2`. This is the Hermitian
pairing on the underlying space `S`; on its own it does **not** imply genuine
self-adjointness (`A† = A`, including equality of domains), which for an unbounded
operator on a proper dense core is strictly stronger.
declarations.statement: def IsSymmetric : Prop

modules.title: Position operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we introduce several position operators for quantum mechanics on `Space d`.

## ii. Key results

Definitions:
- `positionCLM` : (components of) the position vector operator acting on Schwartz maps
    `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` by multiplication by `xᵢ`.
- `radiusRegPowCLM` : operator acting on Schwartz maps by multiplication by
    `(‖x‖² + ε²)^(s/2)`, a smooth regularization of `‖x‖ˢ`.
- `positionOperator` : a self-adjoint multiplication operator acting on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`.
- `readiusRegPowOperator` : a self-adjoint multiplication operator acting on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`.

Notation:
- `𝐱` for `positionCLM`
- `𝐫₀` for `radiusRegPowCLM`
- `𝐫` for `radiusPowLM`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Schwartz operators
  - A.1. Position vector
  - A.2. Radius powers (regularized)
  - A.3. Radius powers
    - A.3.1. As limit of regularized operators
- B. Unbounded operators
  - B.1. Position vector
  - B.2. Radius powers (regularized)
  - B.3. Radius powers
    - B.3.1. As limit of regularized operators

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.positionCLM
declarations.doc:
Component `i` of the position operator is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `xᵢψ`.
declarations.statement: def positionCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.positionCLM_apply_fun
declarations.statement: lemma positionCLM_apply_fun (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) : 𝐱 i ψ = (fun x : Space d ↦ x i) • ⇑ψ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.positionCLM_apply
declarations.statement: lemma positionCLM_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) : 𝐱 i ψ x = x i * ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.positionCLM_inner
declarations.doc: The position operator is symmetric on Schwartz maps, in terms of `positionCLM`.
declarations.statement:
lemma positionCLM_inner (f g : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    ⟪(SpaceDHilbertSpace.schwartzEquiv volume (𝐱 i f) : SpaceDHilbertSpace d),
      SpaceDHilbertSpace.schwartzEquiv volume g⟫_ℂ
      = ⟪(SpaceDHilbertSpace.schwartzEquiv volume f : SpaceDHilbertSpace d),
        SpaceDHilbertSpace.schwartzEquiv volume (𝐱 i g)⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPowCLM
declarations.doc:
The radius operator to power `s`, regularized by `ε ≠ 0`, is the continuous linear map
from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to itself which maps `ψ` to `(‖x‖² + ε²)^(s/2) • ψ`.
declarations.statement: def radiusRegPowCLM {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) (s : ℝ) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPowCLM_apply_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPowCLM_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) (s : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐫₀ ε s ψ = fun x ↦ (‖x‖ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPowCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPowCLM_apply {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) (s : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐫₀ ε s ψ x = (‖x‖ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2) ^ (s / 2) • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPowCLM_comp_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPowCLM_comp_eq {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) (s t : ℝ) :
    𝐫₀[d] ε s ∘L 𝐫₀ ε t = 𝐫₀ ε (s+t)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusRegPowCLM_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusRegPowCLM_zero {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) :
    𝐫₀ ε 0 = ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.positionSqCLM_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma positionSqCLM_eq {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) :
    ∑ i, 𝐱 i ∘L 𝐱 i = 𝐫₀ ε 2 - ε.1 ^ 2 • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℂ 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusPowLM
declarations.doc:
The radius operator to power `s` is the linear map from `𝓢(Space d, ℂ)` to `Space d → ℂ` that
maps `ψ` to `x ↦ ‖x‖ˢψ(x)` (which is 'nearly' Schwartz for general `s`).
declarations.statement: def radiusPowLM {d : ℕ} (s : ℝ) : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] Space d → ℂ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusPowLM_apply_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusPowLM_apply_fun {d : ℕ} (s : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    𝐫 s ψ = fun x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ s • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusPowLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusPowLM_apply {d : ℕ} (s : ℝ) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    𝐫 s ψ x = ‖x‖ ^ s • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.radiusPowLM_apply_contDiffAt
declarations.doc: `x ↦ ‖x‖ˢψ(x)` is smooth away from `x = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma radiusPowLM_apply_contDiffAt {d : ℕ} (s : ℝ) (n : ℕ∞) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) {x : Space d}
    (hx : x ≠ 0) : ContDiffAt ℝ n (𝐫 s ψ) x

QuantumMechanics.positionOperator
declarations.doc: The operator on `SpaceDHilbertSpace d` acting by multiplication by `fun x ↦ xᵢ`.
declarations.statement: def positionOperator : SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ →ₗ.[ℂ] SpaceDHilbertSpace d μ

modules.title: Spectral theory for closed operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we develop the basics for the spectral theory of closed unbounded operators.
This forms the basis for the spectral theory of self-adjoint unbounded operators,
which are of central importance in quantum mechanics.

Definitions for subsets of ℂ associated to an operator `T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H` vary by author.
Here we adopt those used in
[Konrad Schmüdgen, Unbounded Self-Adjoint Operators on Hilbert Space][Schmudgen2012]
[ref: Schmudgen2012], summarized in the following table:

| Subset of ℂ | abbrev. | `D(T - z)` | `R(T - z)` | `(T - z)⁻¹` |
| :---------- | :-----: | :--------: | :--------: | :---------: |
| Regularity domain | | `= ⊥` | | continuous |
| Resolvent set | `ρ` | `= ⊥` | `= ⊤` | continuous |
| Point spectrum | `σᵖ` | `≠ ⊥` | | |
| Residual spectrum | `σʳ` | `= ⊥` | `≠ ⊤` | continuous |
| Continuous spectrum | `σᶜ` | | not closed | |

## ii. Key results

Definitions (corresponding to an operator `T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H`)
- `LinearPMap.regularityDomain` : The set of regular points. A complex number `z` is a regular
    point if there exists `c > 0` such that `c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖T x - z • x‖` for all `x : T.domain`.
- `LinearPMap.deficiencySubspace` : Given a complex number `z`, the closed submodule which
    is orthogonal to the range of `T - z • 1`.
- `LinearPMap.defectNumber` : Given a complex number `z`, the rank of the corresponding
    deficiency subspace as a (possibly infinite) cardinal.
- `LinearPMap.numericalRange` (`Θ`) : The set of complex numbers `⟪x, T x⟫_ℂ` as `x` ranges over
    the unit sphere in `T.domain`.
- `LinearPMap.resolventSet` (`ρ`) : The set of complex numbers `z` for which `T - z • 1`
    has a continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse with domain all of `H`.
- `LinearPMap.spectrum` (`σ`) : The complement of the resolvent set.
- `LinearPMap.pointSpectrum` (`σᵖ`) : The set of complex numbers `z` for which `T - z • 1`
    fails to be invertible.
- `LinearPMap.residualSpectrum` (`σʳ`) : The set of complex numbers `z` for which `T - z • 1`
    has a continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse with domain not all of `H`.
- `LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum` (`σᶜ`) : The set of complex numbers `z` for which
    the range of `T - z • 1` is not dense in `H`.

Main results
- `regularityDomain_isOpen` : The regularity domain is an open subset of `ℂ`.
- `closure_range_sub_eq_range_closure_sub` : If `z` is a regular point for a closable operator `T`
    then the closure of `(T - z • 1).range` is `(T.closure - z • 1).range`.
- `defectNumber_const` : The defect number is constant on each connected component
    of the regularity domain.
- `compl_closure_numericalRange_subset_regularityDomain` : The regularity domain contains
    the exterior of the numerical range.
- `numericalRange_convex` : The Toeplitz-Hausdorff theorem — the numerical range is a convex set.
- `resolventSet_isOpen` and `spectrum_isClosed` : The resolvent set is an open subset of ℂ
    and its complement, the spectrum, is closed.
- `IsClosed.spectrum_eq` : For a closed operator the spectrum is the union of the point, residual
    and continuous spectra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Regularity domain
- B. Deficiency subspace & defect number
- C. Numerical range
  - C.1. The Toeplitz-Hausdorff theorem
- D. Spectrum of a closed operator
  - D.1. Resolvent set
  - D.2. Spectrum
    - D.2.1. Point spectrum
    - D.2.2. Residual spectrum
    - D.2.3. Continuous spectrum
  - D.3. Spectrum decomposition
- E. Resolvent identities

## iv. References

* Konrad Schmüdgen, Unbounded Self-Adjoint Operators on Hilbert Space. [ref: Schmudgen2012]

sections.text: ## D. Spectrum of a closed operator

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolvent
declarations.doc: The resolvent, `(T - z • 1)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: abbrev resolvent (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsLowerBound
declarations.doc: `IsLowerBound T z c` is the property that `c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖T x - z • x‖` for all `x : T.domain`.
declarations.statement: def IsLowerBound (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) (c : ℝ) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma isLowerBound_neg {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z c) :
    IsLowerBound (-T) (-z) c

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_of_right_le
declarations.statement:
lemma isLowerBound_of_right_le
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c₁ c₂ : ℝ} (hle : c₁ ≤ c₂) (h : IsLowerBound T z c₂) :
    IsLowerBound T z c₁

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_of_left_le
declarations.statement:
lemma isLowerBound_of_left_le
    {T₁ T₂ : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hle : T₁ ≤ T₂) {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T₂ z c) :
    IsLowerBound T₁ z c

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isLowerBound_closure
declarations.statement:
lemma isLowerBound_closure
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z c) : IsLowerBound T.closure z c

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain
declarations.doc:
The regular points for `T`.

`z : ℂ` is a regular point for `T` iff there exists a constant `c > 0` such that
`c * ‖x‖ ≤ ‖(T - z • 1) x‖` for all `x ∈ T.domain`.
declarations.statement: def regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_neg
declarations.statement: lemma regularityDomain_neg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : (-T).regularityDomain = -T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma regularityDomain_smul (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    (w • T).regularityDomain = w • T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_antitone
declarations.doc: `T ≤ T'` implies `T'.regularityDomain ⊆ T.regularityDomain`.
declarations.statement: lemma regularityDomain_antitone : Antitone (regularityDomain (H := H))

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_regularityDomain_iff
declarations.doc:
`z` is a regular point for `T` iff `T - z • 1` has
a continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_regularityDomain_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ T.regularityDomain ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.ball_subset_regularityDomain
declarations.doc: The regularity domain of `T` contains open balls with radii controlled by the lower bounds.
declarations.statement:
lemma ball_subset_regularityDomain
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z c) : ball z c ⊆ T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_isOpen
declarations.doc: The regularity domain is an open set.
declarations.statement: lemma regularityDomain_isOpen (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : IsOpen T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.regularityDomain_closure
declarations.doc: `T` and `T.closure` have the same regularity domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma regularityDomain_closure (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    T.closure.regularityDomain = T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.closure_range_sub_eq_range_closure_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosable.closure_range_sub_eq_range_closure_sub [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    (T - z • 1).toFun.range.closure = (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.range

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.sub_range_isClosed
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.sub_range_isClosed [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    _root_.IsClosed ((T - z • 1).toFun.range : Set H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_closure_sub_range
declarations.doc: `(T.closure - z • 1).rangeᗮ = (T† - conj z • 1).ker`
declarations.statement:
lemma IsUnbounded.orthogonal_closure_sub_range [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsUnbounded) (z : ℂ) :
    (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ
      = (T† - conj z • 1).toFun.ker.map (T† - conj z • 1).domain.subtype

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_sub_ker
declarations.doc: `(T† - conj z • 1).kerᗮ = (T.closure - z • 1).range`
declarations.statement:
lemma IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_sub_ker [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsUnbounded) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    ((T† - conj z • 1).toFun.ker.map (T† - conj z • 1).domain.subtype)ᗮ
      = (T.closure - z • 1).toFun.range

declarations.name: LinearPMap.deficiencySubspace
declarations.doc:
For a partial linear map `T` and any complex number `z`, the closed submodule which
is orthogonal to the range of `T - z • 1`.

`T.defectNumber z` is defined as the rank of this subspace.
declarations.statement: def deficiencySubspace (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) : ClosedSubmodule ℂ H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.deficiencySubspace_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma deficiencySubspace_coe (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) :
    T.deficiencySubspace z = (T - z • 1).toFun.rangeᗮ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber
declarations.doc: The rank of `T.deficiencySubspace z = (T - z • 1).rangeᗮ`.
declarations.statement: def defectNumber (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) : Cardinal

declarations.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma defectNumber_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (z : ℂ) :
    T.defectNumber z = Module.rank ℂ (T.deficiencySubspace z)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.defectNumber_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.defectNumber_eq_zero_iff [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    T.defectNumber z = 0 ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤

declarations.name: LinearPMap.defectNumber_closure
declarations.doc: `T` and `T.closure` have the same defect number at points in their regularity domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma defectNumber_closure [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ T.regularityDomain) :
    T.closure.defectNumber z = T.defectNumber z

declarations.name: Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_rank_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.Submodule.inf_ne_bot_of_rank_lt
    {E F : Submodule ℂ H} [E.HasOrthogonalProjection] (h_rank : Module.rank ℂ E < Module.rank ℂ F) :
    Eᗮ ⊓ F ≠ ⊥

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.exists_inner_eq_zero_of_defectNumber_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.exists_inner_eq_zero_of_defectNumber_lt [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} (hz₁ : z₁ ∈ T.regularityDomain) (h : T.defectNumber z₁ < T.defectNumber z₂) :
    ∃ x : T.domain, x ≠ 0 ∧ ⟪T x - z₁ • x, T x - z₂ • x⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.defectNumber_eq_of_mem_ball
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosable.defectNumber_eq_of_mem_ball [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : IsLowerBound T z₁ c) (h_ball : z₂ ∈ ball z₁ c) :
    T.defectNumber z₁ = T.defectNumber z₂

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.defectNumber_const
declarations.doc: The defect number is constant on each connected component of the regularity domain.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosable.defectNumber_const [CompleteSpace H]
    {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosable)
    {z₁ z₂ : ℂ} (hz : z₂ ∈ connectedComponentIn T.regularityDomain z₁) :
    T.defectNumber z₁ = T.defectNumber z₂

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange
declarations.doc: The set `{⟪x, T x⟫_ℂ | x ∈ T.domain ∧ ‖x‖ = 1} ⊆ ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def numericalRange (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_eq
declarations.statement: lemma numericalRange_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θ T = (fun x ↦ ⟪↑x, T x⟫_ℂ) '' {x | ‖x‖ = 1}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_numericalRange
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_numericalRange {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {x : T.domain} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    (‖x‖ ^ 2)⁻¹ * ⟪↑x, T x⟫_ℂ ∈ Θ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_nonempty
declarations.statement: lemma numericalRange_nonempty {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.domain ≠ ⊥) : (Θ T).Nonempty

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_neg
declarations.statement: lemma numericalRange_neg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Θ (-T) = -Θ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_smul
declarations.statement: lemma numericalRange_smul (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (c : ℂ) : Θ (c • T) = c • Θ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_sub_const
declarations.statement: lemma numericalRange_sub_const (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (c : ℂ) : Θ (T - c • 1) = Θ T - {c}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.compl_closure_numericalRange_subset_regularityDomain
declarations.doc: The regularity domain contains the exterior of the numerical range.
declarations.statement:
lemma compl_closure_numericalRange_subset_regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    (_root_.closure (Θ T))ᶜ ⊆ T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.numericalRange_convex
declarations.doc: The Toeplitz-Hausdorff theorem.
declarations.statement: theorem numericalRange_convex (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Convex ℝ (Θ T)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet
declarations.doc:
The resolvent set, `ρ`, of a partial linear map.

A complex number `z` is in `ρ T` iff the linear map `T - z • 1` from `T.domain` to `H`
is a bijection with continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse.
declarations.statement: def resolventSet (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma resolventSet_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    ρ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_resolventSet_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_resolventSet_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ ρ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_eq_empty
declarations.doc: If an operator is not closed then its resolvent set is empty.
declarations.statement: lemma resolventSet_eq_empty [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (h : ¬T.IsClosed) : ρ T = ∅

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_subset_regularityDomain
declarations.statement: lemma resolventSet_subset_regularityDomain (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : ρ T ⊆ T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.resolventSet_eq
declarations.doc:
For a closed operator the continuity of the resolvent is redundant
in the definition of the resolvent set.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.resolventSet_eq [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) :
    ρ T = {z : ℂ | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.resolventSet_eq'
declarations.doc:
For a closed operator the resolvent set consists of those regular points for which
the defect number is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.resolventSet_eq' [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T.IsClosed) :
    ρ T = T.regularityDomain ∩ T.defectNumber ⁻¹' {0}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolventSet_isOpen
declarations.doc: The resolvent set is an open subset of ℂ.
declarations.statement: lemma resolventSet_isOpen [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : IsOpen (ρ T)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.spectrum
declarations.doc:
The spectrum, `σ`, of a partial linear map.

`σ T` is the complement of `ρ T`. A complex number `z` is in `σ T` iff the linear map `T - z • 1`
from `T.domain` to `H` fails to be bijective or `(T - z • 1)⁻¹` is not continuous
(equivalently, is not bounded).
declarations.statement: def spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_eq
declarations.statement: lemma spectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σ T = (ρ T)ᶜ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_spectrum_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_spectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ σ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥ ∨ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∨ ¬Continuous (𝑅 T z)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_eq_univ
declarations.doc: If an operator is not closed then its spectrum is all of ℂ.
declarations.statement: lemma spectrum_eq_univ [CompleteSpace H] {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (h : ¬T.IsClosed) : σ T = univ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.spectrum_isClosed
declarations.doc: The spectrum is a closed subset of ℂ.
declarations.statement: lemma spectrum_isClosed [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : _root_.IsClosed (σ T)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The point spectrum, `σᵖ`, of a partial linear map.

A complex number `z` is in `σᵖ T` iff `T - z • 1` is not injective.
declarations.statement: def pointSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_eq
declarations.statement: lemma pointSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_pointSpectrum_iff
declarations.statement: lemma mem_pointSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} : z ∈ σᵖ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker ≠ ⊥

declarations.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_subset_spectrum
declarations.statement: lemma pointSpectrum_subset_spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T ⊆ σ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The residual spectrum, `σʳ`, of a partial linear map.

A complex number `z` is in `σʳ T` iff `T - z • 1` is injective but not surjective
and `(T - z • 1)⁻¹` is continuous (equivalently, bounded).
declarations.statement: def residualSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : Set ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma residualSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    σʳ T = {z | (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)}

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_residualSpectrum_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_residualSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :
    z ∈ σʳ T ↔ (T - z • 1).toFun.ker = ⊥ ∧ (T - z • 1).toFun.range ≠ ⊤ ∧ Continuous (𝑅 T z)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_subset_spectrum
declarations.statement: lemma residualSpectrum_subset_spectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σʳ T ⊆ σ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.residualSpectrum_subset_regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum

The continuous spectrum, `σᶜ`, of a partial linear map.

A complex number `z` is in `σᶜ T` iff the range of `T - z • 1` is not closed.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.continuousSpectrum_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma continuousSpectrum_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) :
    σᶜ T = {z | ¬_root_.IsClosed ((T - z • 1).toFun.range : Set H)}

lemma mem_continuousSpectrum_iff {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} {z : ℂ} :

declarations.name: LinearPMap.pointSpectrum_inter_residualSpectrum
declarations.statement: lemma pointSpectrum_inter_residualSpectrum (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) : σᵖ T ∩ σʳ T = ∅

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolvent_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma resolvent_sub
    {T₁ T₂ : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hT : T₂.domain ≤ T₁.domain) {z : ℂ} (hz₁ : z ∈ ρ T₁) (hz₂ : z ∈ ρ T₂) :
    𝑅 T₁ z - 𝑅 T₂ z = 𝑅 T₁ z * (T₂ - T₁) * 𝑅 T₂ z

declarations.name: LinearPMap.resolvent_sub'
declarations.statement:
lemma resolvent_sub' {T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (z₁ z₂ : ℂ) (hz₁ : z₁ ∈ ρ T) (hz₂ : z₂ ∈ ρ T) :
    𝑅 T z₁ - 𝑅 T z₂ = (z₁ - z₂) • (𝑅 T z₁ * 𝑅 T z₂)

modules.title: Spectral theory for self-adjoint operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we develop the spectral theory for self-adjoint operators.

## ii. Key results

- `resolventSet_eq_regularityDomain` : The resolvent set and regularity domain coincide. That is,
    if `T - z • 1` has a continuous (equivalently, bounded) inverse then its range is all of `H`.
- `mem_resolventSet_of_im_ne_zero` : every non-real `z` lies in the resolvent set of a
    self-adjoint operator.
- `sub_smul_surjective` : A self-adjoint `T` has `T - z • 1` surjective for every non-real `z`
    (in particular `T ± i • 1` are onto).
- `spectrum_real` : The spectrum of a self-adjoint unbounded operator is real.
- `unitaryConj_isSelfAdjoint` : Unitary conjugation preserves self-adjointness.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Resolvent set
- B. Spectrum
- C. Unitary conjugation

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.resolventSet_eq_regularityDomain
declarations.statement: lemma resolventSet_eq_regularityDomain : ρ T = T.regularityDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.mem_resolventSet_of_im_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Every non-real `z` lies in the resolvent set of a self-adjoint operator.
declarations.statement: lemma mem_resolventSet_of_im_ne_zero {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) : z ∈ ρ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.sub_smul_surjective
declarations.doc:
A self-adjoint operator has `T - z • 1` surjective for every non-real `z`: off the real
axis a self-adjoint operator has `z` in its resolvent set, so `T - z • 1` has full range.
declarations.statement: lemma sub_smul_surjective {z : ℂ} (hz : z.im ≠ 0) : Function.Surjective (T - z • 1).toFun

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.mem_resolventSet_of_range_eq_top
declarations.doc:
`(T - z • 1).range = ⊤` is a sufficient condition for `z ∈ ρ T`
(and it is a necessary condition by definition of `ρ`).
declarations.statement: lemma mem_resolventSet_of_range_eq_top {z : ℂ} (h : (T - z • 1).toFun.range = ⊤) : z ∈ ρ T

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.spectrum_real
declarations.doc: The spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is real.
declarations.statement: lemma spectrum_real : σ T ⊆ range ofReal

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsSelfAdjoint.residualSpectrum_eq_empty
declarations.doc: The residual spectrum of a self-adjoint operator is empty.
declarations.statement: lemma residualSpectrum_eq_empty : σʳ T = ∅

declarations.name: LinearPMap.unitaryConj_isSelfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
Unitary conjugation preserves self-adjointness: if `A` is a self-adjoint operator on `H` and
`u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H'` is unitary, then `u A u⁻¹` is self-adjoint on `H'`. Symmetry, dense domain, and
the two deficiency surjectivities of `A` all transfer through `u`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConj_isSelfAdjoint (u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H') {A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    IsSelfAdjoint (A.unitaryConj u)

modules.title: Spectral measures
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A spectral measure `μS` on a measurable space `α` is a σ-additive function `Set α → H →L[ℂ] H`
such that each set is mapped to a star projection on `H`, the empty set and non-measurable sets are
mapped to zero, and `univ` is mapped to the identity.
This is implemented as a structure extending `VectorMeasure α (H →L[ℂ] H)` with additional fields
constraining `μS A` to be a star projection for each set `A` and `μS univ = 1`.

For each `x : H` there is an associated measure `μₓ` given by `μₓ A = ‖μS A x‖² = ⟪x, μS A x⟫ ≤ 1`.

## ii. Key results

- `SpectralMeasure` : A star projection-valued measure.
- `comp_eq_of_inter` : For a spectral measure `μS` and measurable sets `A` and `B`,
    the composition `μS A ∘ μS B = μS (A ∩ B)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition
- B. Composition

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.statement:
instance (H : Type*) [SeminormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] :
    HasUniqueDiv (H →L[ℂ] H)

declarations.name: SpectralMeasure
declarations.doc:
A _spectral measure_ on a measurable space `α` is a σ-additive function `Set α → H →L[ℂ] H`
such that each set is mapped to a star projection on `H`, the empty set and non-measurable sets
are mapped to zero, and `univ` is mapped to the identity.
declarations.statement:
structure SpectralMeasure
    (α : Type*) [MeasurableSpace α]
    (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    extends VectorMeasure α (H →L[ℂ] H) where
  isStarProjection' : ∀ A, IsStarProjection (measureOf' A)
  univ' : measureOf' univ = 1

declarations.name: SpectralMeasure.comp_self

lemma comp_of_disjoint

modules.title: Spectral theory for symmetric operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we develop the spectral theory for symmetric operators.

The numerical range of an operator, `Θ T = {⟪x, T x⟫_ℂ | x ∈ T.domain ∧ ‖x‖ = 1}`, is a subset of ℂ.
For symmetric operators the numerical range consists only of real numbers and it is meaningful
to discuss its upper/lower bounds. To facilitate this, we define `LinearPMap.realNumericalRange`
as the projection of `LinearPMap.numericalRange` onto the real axis. For symmetric operators this
simply reinterprets the numerical range as a subset of ℝ.

## ii. Key results

- `realNumericalRange` (`Θᵣₑ`) : The projection of the numerical range onto the real axis.
- `compl_ofReal_subset_regularityDomain` : The regularity domain of a symmetric operator contains
    all complex numbers with non-zero imaginary part.
- `regularityDomain_isConnected_iff` : The regularity domain of a symmetric operator is connected
    if and only if it contains a real number.
- `IsSymmetric.isEssentiallySelfAdjoint_of_defectNumber_eq_zero` : The basic criterion for
    essential self-adjointness: symmetric + densely defined + vanishing defect numbers at `± i`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Numerical range
- B. Regularity domain
- C. Point spectrum
- D. Essential self-adjointness

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Expectation values and centered vectors
modules.doc:
For a partial linear map `T` on a complex inner product space and `ψ ∈ T.domain`, this file
defines the expectation value and the centered vector `Tψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ`.

## Main definitions

- `LinearPMap.expectedValue`: the real part of `⟪ψ, Tψ⟫_ℂ`.
- `LinearPMap.centered`: the centered vector `Tψ - ⟨T⟩ψ`.

## Main statements

- `LinearPMap.expectedValue_eq_inner`: for symmetric `T`, the complex inner product is real and
  equals the real expectation value coerced to `ℂ`.

## References

* B. C. Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chapter 12. [ref: hall2013quantum]

declarations.name: LinearPMap.expectedValue
declarations.statement: def expectedValue (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) : ℝ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.expectedValue_eq_re_inner
declarations.doc: The expectation value, unfolded as a real part.
declarations.statement:
lemma expectedValue_eq_re_inner (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    expectedValue T ψ = (⟪(ψ : H), T ψ⟫_ℂ).re

declarations.name: LinearPMap.expectedValue_eq_inner
declarations.doc: If `T` is symmetric, `⟪ψ, Tψ⟫_ℂ` is the expectation value, coerced to `ℂ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma expectedValue_eq_inner (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (ψ : T.domain) :
    ⟪(ψ : H), T ψ⟫_ℂ = (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inner_eq_expectedValue
declarations.doc: Reverse orientation of `LinearPMap.expectedValue_eq_inner`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_eq_expectedValue (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (ψ : T.domain) :
    (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) = ⟪(ψ : H), T ψ⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.centered
declarations.doc: The centered vector `Tψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ`.
declarations.statement: def centered (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) : H

declarations.name: LinearPMap.centered_eq
declarations.doc: The centered vector, unfolded to its raw expression.
declarations.statement:
lemma centered_eq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    centered T ψ = T ψ - (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) • (ψ : H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.centered_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: A centered vector vanishes exactly when `Tψ = ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma centered_eq_zero_iff (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    centered T ψ = 0 ↔ T ψ = (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) • (ψ : H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inner_state_centered_eq_zero
declarations.doc: For a unit vector and symmetric `T`, the centered vector is orthogonal to the state.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_state_centered_eq_zero (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hT : T.IsSymmetric)
    (ψ : T.domain) (hψ_norm : ‖(ψ : H)‖ = 1) :
    ⟪(ψ : H), centered T ψ⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.inner_centered_state_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The conjugate orientation of `LinearPMap.inner_state_centered_eq_zero`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_centered_state_eq_zero (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (hT : T.IsSymmetric)
    (ψ : T.domain) (hψ_norm : ‖(ψ : H)‖ = 1) :
    ⟪centered T ψ, (ψ : H)⟫_ℂ = 0

modules.doc:
## Main definitions

- `LinearPMap.IsEigenvector`: a nonzero domain vector satisfying `T ψ = μ • ψ`.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEigenvector
declarations.doc: A nonzero vector in the domain of `T` satisfying `T ψ = μ • ψ`.
declarations.statement: def IsEigenvector (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) (μ : ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEigenvector.apply_eq
declarations.doc: The eigenvalue equation for a partial-map eigenvector.

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsEigenvector.ne_zero

modules.title: Variance and standard deviation
modules.doc:
The variance of a partial linear map `T` in a state `ψ` is `‖Tψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ‖ ^ 2`. It only
requires `ψ ∈ T.domain`.

When `T` is symmetric, `‖ψ‖ = 1`, and `Tψ ∈ T.domain`, it also equals `⟨T^2⟩_ψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ^ 2`.

## Main definitions

- `LinearPMap.variance` and `LinearPMap.standardDeviation`.

## Main statements

- `LinearPMap.variance_eq_norm_sq_sub_expectedValue_sq`: for a unit vector and symmetric `T`,
  the variance is `‖Tψ‖ ^ 2 - ⟨T⟩_ψ ^ 2`.
- `LinearPMap.variance_eq_re_inner_sub_expectedValue_sq`: the second-order formula when
`Tψ ∈ T.domain`.
- `LinearPMap.variance_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector` and
  `LinearPMap.standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector`: for a unit vector, zero variance or
  standard deviation is equivalent to the eigenvector condition.

## References

* B. C. Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chapter 12. [ref: hall2013quantum]

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance
declarations.doc: Variance `‖Tψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ‖ ^ 2`; only `ψ ∈ T.domain` is required.
declarations.statement: def variance (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) : ℝ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_centered_norm_sq
declarations.doc: The variance is the squared norm of the centered vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_centered_norm_sq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    variance T ψ = ‖centered T ψ‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_norm_sub_sq
declarations.doc: `variance` with `centered` unfolded to `Tψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ • ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_norm_sub_sq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    variance T ψ =
      ‖T ψ - (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) • (ψ : H)‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_norm_sq_sub_expectedValue_sq
declarations.doc: For symmetric `T` and `‖ψ‖ = 1`, variance equals `‖Tψ‖ ^ 2 - ⟨T⟩_ψ ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_norm_sq_sub_expectedValue_sq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (hT : T.IsSymmetric) (ψ : T.domain) (hψ_norm : ‖(ψ : H)‖ = 1) :
    variance T ψ = ‖T ψ‖ ^ 2 - expectedValue T ψ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_nonneg
declarations.doc: Variance is nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_nonneg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    0 ≤ variance T ψ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_zero_iff_centered_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Zero variance is the same as a zero centered vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_zero_iff_centered_eq_zero (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    variance T ψ = 0 ↔ centered T ψ = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: Zero variance is the same as `Tψ = ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_zero_iff (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    variance T ψ = 0 ↔ T ψ = (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) • (ψ : H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector
declarations.doc: For `‖ψ‖ = 1`, zero variance iff `ψ` is an eigenvector with eigenvalue `⟨T⟩_ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (ψ : T.domain) (hψ_norm : ‖(ψ : H)‖ = 1) :
    variance T ψ = 0 ↔
      T.IsEigenvector ψ (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation
declarations.doc: Standard deviation `√(variance)` for `ψ ∈ T.domain`.
declarations.statement: def standardDeviation (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) : ℝ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_eq_sqrt_variance
declarations.doc: The standard deviation, unfolded to the square root of the variance.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_eq_sqrt_variance (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    standardDeviation T ψ = Real.sqrt (variance T ψ)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_nonneg
declarations.doc: Standard deviation is nonnegative.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_nonneg (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    0 ≤ standardDeviation T ψ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_sq (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    standardDeviation T ψ ^ 2 = variance T ψ

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff_centered_eq_zero
declarations.doc: Zero standard deviation is the same as a zero centered vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff_centered_eq_zero (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (ψ : T.domain) :
    standardDeviation T ψ = 0 ↔ centered T ψ = 0

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: Zero standard deviation is the same as `Tψ = ⟨T⟩_ψ ψ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H) (ψ : T.domain) :
    standardDeviation T ψ = 0 ↔ T ψ = (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ) • (ψ : H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector
declarations.doc: For `‖ψ‖ = 1`, zero standard deviation iff the eigenvector condition holds.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardDeviation_eq_zero_iff_isEigenvector (T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H)
    (ψ : T.domain) (hψ_norm : ‖(ψ : H)‖ = 1) :
    standardDeviation T ψ = 0 ↔
      T.IsEigenvector ψ (expectedValue T ψ : ℂ)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.re_inner_apply_sq_eq_norm_sq
declarations.doc: For symmetric `T`, `re ⟪ψ, T(Tψ)⟫` is `‖Tψ‖ ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma re_inner_apply_sq_eq_norm_sq :
    (⟪(ψ : H), T ⟨T ψ, hTψ⟩⟫_ℂ).re = ‖T ψ‖ ^ 2

declarations.name: LinearPMap.variance_eq_re_inner_sub_expectedValue_sq
declarations.doc: When `Tψ ∈ T.domain`, variance equals `⟨T^2⟩_ψ - ⟨T⟩_ψ ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma variance_eq_re_inner_sub_expectedValue_sq :
    variance T ψ =
      (⟪(ψ : H), T ⟨T ψ, hTψ⟩⟫_ℂ).re - expectedValue T ψ ^ 2

modules.title: Unbounded operators
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The appropriate mathematical objects for discussing operators in non-relativistic quantum mechanics
are partially-defined linear map (`LinearPMap`) between complex Hilbert spaces, `H →ₗ.[ℂ] H'`.
An import class of operators in NRQM are those which are both densely defined and closable,
which we refer to as _unbounded_. When `H = H'` operators may also be symmetric, self-adjoint or
essentially self-adjoint (closure is self-adjoint).

In this module we collect results on how the properties `HasDenseDomain`, `IsUnbounded`,
`IsSymmetric`, `IsSelfAdjoint` and `IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint` interact with the basic algebraic
operations, closure, adjoints, unitary conjugation and each other.

### Notes

- Naming convention : Definitions of `LinearPMap`s for quantum mechanical unbounded operators should
    have a name of the form `[…]Operator` and notation should use calligraphic capital letters,
    e.g. `mulOperator f` (`𝓜 f`) for the multiplication operator associated with the function `f`.

- Implementation : Although operators encountered in quantum mechanics are almost always unbounded,
    we opt to implement unbounded operators via the property `IsUnbounded` on `LinearPMap` rather
    than as a structure `UnboundedOperator` extending `LinearPMap`. The basic reason for this
    is that addition/subtraction and composition of unbounded operators in general does not result
    in another unbounded operator. This means, for example, that any attempt to define addition of
    `UnboundedOperator`s would inevitably require introducing junk values that spoil associativity.

## ii. Key results

Definitions
- `HasDenseDomain` : An operator `U : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H'` has dense domain if `U.domain` is dense in `H`.
- `IsUnbounded` : An operator is unbounded if it is both densely defined and closable.
- `IsSymmetric` : An operator `T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H` is symmetric if `⟪T x, y⟫_ℂ = ⟪x, T y⟫_ℂ` holds
    for all `x y : T.domain`.
- `IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint` : An operator `T : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H` is essentially self-adjoint if
    its closure is self-adjoint.

Results
- `adjoint_add_le_add_adjoint` : The inequality `U₁† + U₂† ≤ (U₁ + U₂)†` when `U₁ + U₂` has
    dense domain.
- `unitaryConj` : The conjugation `u A u⁻¹ : H' →ₗ.[ℂ] H'` of `A` by a unitary `u`, with domain
    `u (A.domain)`.
- `IsFormalAdjoint.unitaryConj` : Unitary conjugation preserves formal-adjoint pairs.
- `HasDenseDomain.unitaryConj_dense_domain` : If `A` has dense domain, then so does `u A u⁻¹`.
- `unitaryConj_sub_smul_surjective` : If `A - z` is surjective for a scalar `z : ℂ`,
    then so is `u A u⁻¹ - z`.
- `adjoint_compRestricted_le_compRestricted_adjoint` : The inequality `U† ∘ᵣ V† ≤ (V ∘ᵣ U)†`
    when `V` and `V ∘ᵣ U` have dense domain.
- `IsUnbounded.adjoint` : The adjoint of an unbounded operator is also unbounded.
- `IsUnbounded.adjoint_closure_eq_adjoint` : An unbounded operator and its closure have
    the same adjoint.
- `IsUnbounded.adjoint_adjoint_eq_closure` : An unbounded operator `U` satisfies `U†† = U.closure`.
- `IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint.unique_self_adjoint_extension` : The closure of an essentially
    self-adjoint unbounded operator is its unique self-adjoint extension.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definitions
- B. Basic properties
  - B.1. Dense domain
  - B.2. Closability
  - B.3. Adjoints
  - B.4. Continuity / boundedness
  - B.5. Unitary conjugation
- C. Classes of operators
  - C.1. Unbounded operators
  - C.2. Symmetric operators
  - C.3. Self-adjoint operators
  - C.4. Essentially self-adjoint operators

## iv. References

* Reed and Simon, Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics, Vol. I: Functional Analysis.
  [ref: Reed1972]
* Konrad Schmüdgen, Unbounded Self-Adjoint Operators on Hilbert Space. [ref: Schmudgen2012]

declarations.name: LinearMap.continuous_iff_bounded
declarations.doc:
`f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F` is continuous iff there exists `M > 0` s.t. `‖f x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖` for all `x : E`.

This is a (convenient) immediate consequence of
`IsBoundedLinearMap.isLinearMap_and_continuous_iff_isBoundedLinearMap`.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.LinearMap.continuous_iff_bounded {𝕜 E F : Type*} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
    [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
    {f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F} : Continuous f ↔ ∃ M, 0 < M ∧ ∀ x : E, ‖f x‖ ≤ M * ‖x‖

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isClosable_of_continuous
declarations.doc: Continuous operators are closable.
declarations.statement: lemma isClosable_of_continuous (h : Continuous U) : U.IsClosable

declarations.name: LinearPMap.closure_domain_eq_domain_closure_of_continuous
declarations.doc: A strengthening of `closure_domain_le_domain_closure` for continuous operators.
declarations.statement:
lemma closure_domain_eq_domain_closure_of_continuous [CompleteSpace H'] (h : Continuous U) :
    U.closure.domain = U.domain.closure

declarations.name: LinearPMap.isClosed_iff_isClosed_domain_of_continuous
declarations.doc: A continuous operator is closed iff its domain is closed.
declarations.statement:
lemma isClosed_iff_isClosed_domain_of_continuous [CompleteSpace H'] (h : Continuous U) :
    U.IsClosed ↔ _root_.IsClosed (U.domain : Set H)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.isClosed_toFun_graph
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.isClosed_toFun_graph (hU : U.IsClosed) :
    _root_.IsClosed (U.toFun.graph : Set (U.domain × H'))

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.continuous_of_isClosed_domain
declarations.doc:
The **closed graph theorem** for partial linear maps:
a closed operator with closed domain is continuous.

This follows immediately from `LinearMap.continuous_of_isClosed_graph`
and the completeness of `H` and `H'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.continuous_of_isClosed_domain [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace H']
    (hU : U.IsClosed) (h : _root_.IsClosed (U.domain : Set H)) :
    Continuous U

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.add_continuous
declarations.doc: Closability is preserved upon adding a continuous operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosable.add_continuous
    (h₁ : U₁.IsClosable) (h₂ : Continuous U₂) (h : U₁.domain ≤ U₂.domain) :
    (U₁ + U₂).IsClosable

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosable.sub_continuous
declarations.doc: Closability is preserved upon subtracting a continuous operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosable.sub_continuous
    (h₁ : U₁.IsClosable) (h₂ : Continuous U₂) (h : U₁.domain ≤ U₂.domain) : (U₁ - U₂).IsClosable

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.add_continuous
declarations.doc: Closedness is preserved upon adding a continuous operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.add_continuous [CompleteSpace H']
    (h₁ : U₁.IsClosed) (h₂ : Continuous U₂) (h : U₁.domain ≤ U₂.domain) : (U₁ + U₂).IsClosed

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsClosed.sub_continuous
declarations.doc: Closedness is preserved upon subtracting a continuous operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsClosed.sub_continuous [CompleteSpace H']
    (h₁ : U₁.IsClosed) (h₂ : Continuous U₂) (h : U₁.domain ≤ U₂.domain) : (U₁ - U₂).IsClosed

declarations.name: LinearPMap.adjoint_domain_of_continuous
declarations.statement: lemma adjoint_domain_of_continuous [CompleteSpace H] (h : Continuous U) : U†.domain = ⊤

declarations.name: LinearPMap.HasDenseDomain.adjoint_add_continuous
declarations.statement:
lemma HasDenseDomain.adjoint_add_continuous [CompleteSpace H]
    (h₁ : T₁.HasDenseDomain) (h₂ : Continuous T₂) (h : T₁.domain ≤ T₂.domain) :
    (T₁ + T₂)† = T₁† + T₂†

declarations.name: LinearPMap.HasDenseDomain.adjoint_sub_continuous
declarations.statement:
lemma HasDenseDomain.adjoint_sub_continuous [CompleteSpace H]
    (h₁ : T₁.HasDenseDomain) (h₂ : Continuous T₂) (h : T₁.domain ≤ T₂.domain) :
    (T₁ - T₂)† = T₁† - T₂†

declarations.name: LinearPMap.unitaryConj
declarations.doc:
The conjugation `u A u⁻¹` of a partially-defined operator `A : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H` by a unitary
`u : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H'`, with domain `u (A.domain) = u⁻¹ ⁻¹' (A.domain)` and action
`y ↦ u (A (u⁻¹ y))`. Since `u` and `u⁻¹` are `ℂ`-linear, the result is again `ℂ`-linear.
declarations.statement: def unitaryConj : H' →ₗ.[ℂ] H'

declarations.name: LinearPMap.mem_unitaryConj_domain_iff
declarations.doc: Membership in the conjugated domain: `x ∈ D(u A u⁻¹) ↔ u⁻¹ x ∈ D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_unitaryConj_domain_iff {x : H'} :
    x ∈ (unitaryConj u A).domain ↔ u.symm x ∈ A.domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.unitaryConj_apply
declarations.doc: The defining formula `(u A u⁻¹) x = u (A (u⁻¹ x))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConj_apply (x : (unitaryConj u A).domain) :
    unitaryConj u A x = u (A ⟨u.symm (x : H'), (mem_unitaryConj_domain_iff u A).mp x.2⟩)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.map_mem_unitaryConj_domain
declarations.doc: `u` maps `D(A)` into `D(u A u⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement: lemma map_mem_unitaryConj_domain (y : A.domain) : u (y : H) ∈ (unitaryConj u A).domain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.unitaryConj_apply_map
declarations.doc: The action on the image domain: `(u A u⁻¹)(u y) = u (A y)` for `y ∈ D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConj_apply_map (y : A.domain) :
    unitaryConj u A ⟨u (y : H), map_mem_unitaryConj_domain u A y⟩ = u (A y)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsFormalAdjoint.unitaryConj
declarations.doc:
Unitary conjugation preserves formal adjointness. If `A` is a formal adjoint of `B`, then
`u A u⁻¹` is a formal adjoint of `u B u⁻¹`. Unitary conjugation preserves symmetry when `A = B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsFormalAdjoint.unitaryConj {B : H →ₗ.[ℂ] H} (h : A.IsFormalAdjoint B) :
    (unitaryConj u A).IsFormalAdjoint (unitaryConj u B)

declarations.name: LinearPMap.HasDenseDomain.unitaryConj_dense_domain
declarations.doc:
If `A` has dense domain, then so does `u A u⁻¹`: the domain `u⁻¹ ⁻¹' (A.domain)` is the
preimage of a dense set under a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasDenseDomain.unitaryConj_dense_domain (hdense : A.HasDenseDomain) :
    (unitaryConj u A).HasDenseDomain

declarations.name: LinearPMap.unitaryConj_sub_smul_surjective
declarations.doc: If `A - z` is surjective for a scalar `z : ℂ`, then so is `u A u⁻¹ - z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryConj_sub_smul_surjective {z : ℂ} (h : Function.Surjective (A - z • 1).toFun) :
    Function.Surjective (unitaryConj u A - z • 1).toFun

lemma IsUnbounded.isClosed_iff [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace H'] (h : U.IsUnbounded) :

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_range
declarations.doc: `U†.rangeᗮ = U.closure.ker`

lemma IsUnbounded.orthogonal_adjoint_range [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace H']
    (h : U.IsUnbounded) : U†.toFun.rangeᗮ = U.closure.toFun.ker.map U.closure.domain.subtype

declarations.name: LinearPMap.IsUnbounded.orthogonal_closure_ker

modules.title: Uncertainty bounds for partial linear maps
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we prove abstract Robertson and Robertson–Schrödinger uncertainty bounds for
symmetric partial linear maps on a complex inner product space. The statements are independent of
any concrete position or momentum operator.

The centered-commutator results use only the domain assumptions needed to form the centered
vectors. The raw-commutator results add the second-order domain hypotheses required to apply `A`
to `Bψ` and `B` to `Aψ`.

## ii. Key results

- `inner_im_of_commutator_eq` : an anti-Hermitian commutator identity fixes the imaginary part of
  an inner product.
- `centeredCommutatorExpectation` : the scalar commutator of the centered vectors.
- `rawCommutatorExpectation` : the expectation of the raw commutator on a state.
- `inner_centered_commutator_of_raw_commutator` : a raw commutator expectation gives the centered
  commutator expectation.
- `state_uncertainty_squared_of_centered_commutator` : the Robertson squared bound from a centered
  commutator identity.
- `state_uncertainty_squared_with_covariance_of_centered_commutator` : the strengthened
  Robertson–Schrödinger bound.
- `state_uncertainty_of_centered_commutator` : the standard-deviation form of the bound.
- `state_uncertainty_squared_of_raw_commutator`,
  `state_uncertainty_squared_with_covariance_of_raw_commutator`, and
  `state_uncertainty_of_raw_commutator` : variants using a raw commutator expectation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Inner product lemmas
- B. Centered commutator bounds
- C. Raw commutator bounds

## iv. References

* H. P. Robertson, The Uncertainty Principle (1929). [ref: robertson1929uncertainty]
* E. Schrodinger, Zum Heisenbergschen Unscharfeprinzip (1930). [ref: schrodinger1930heisenberg]
* B. C. Hall, Quantum Theory for Mathematicians, Chapter 12. [ref: hall2013quantum]

modules.title: 1d Pöschl-Teller
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Pöschl-Teller potential, `$V(x) \propto -\mathrm{sech}^2{(\kappa x)}$`, gives rise
to a one-dimensional quantum system for which the energy eigenvalues, energy eigenstates and
scattering data can be computed exactly. Notably, the potential is _reflectionless_ when
the parameter controlling its depth is a positive integer.

## ii. Key results

- `potential` is the Pöschl-Teller potential `-(ℏ² κ² N (N + 1)) / (2 m cosh² (κ x))`, of depth
  `depth = ℏ² κ² N (N + 1) / (2 m)`; it is negative, bounded below by `-depth`, even, of temperate
  growth (`potential_hasTemperateGrowth`) and continuous.
- `toSpaceDQuantumSystem` realises the Pöschl-Teller system as a `SpaceDQuantumSystem` of
  dimension `1`; its kinetic, potential and Hamiltonian operators are the generic ones of
  `SpaceDQuantumSystem`, for which this file gives the pointwise formulas in dimension one
  (`toSpaceDQuantumSystem_kineticCLM_apply`, `toSpaceDQuantumSystem_hamiltonianCLM_apply`) and the
  self-adjointness of the potential operator
  (`toSpaceDQuantumSystem_potentialOperator_isSelfAdjoint`).
- `creationCLM_apply`, `annihilationCLM_apply` give the pointwise action of the ladder operators;
  their sum and difference are `(2 / √(2m)) 𝐩` and `(2 i ℏ κ / √(2m)) tanh (κ X)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Potential function
  - A.1. Definition and depth
  - A.2. Sign, bounds and parity
  - A.3. Regularity
- B. As a quantum system
- C. Operators
  - C.1. Kinetic energy, potential energy and Hamiltonian
  - C.2. Creation and annihilation operators
    - C.2.1. On Schwartz functions
    - C.2.2. As unbounded operators

## iv. References

* https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.14941. [ref: arxiv_2411_14941]

sections.text: ### C.1. Kinetic energy, potential energy and Hamiltonian

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller
declarations.doc:
A Pöschl-Teller system is specified by the particle mass `m`, the width parameter `κ`,
and family number `N` (all positive). -
declarations.statement:
structure PoschlTeller where
  /-- mass of the particle -/
  m : ℝ
  /-- width parameter of the potential -/
  κ : ℝ
  /-- family number, positive integer -/
  N : ℕ
  m_pos : 0 < m -- mass of the particle is positive
  κ_pos : 0 < κ -- width parameter of the potential is positive
  N_pos : 0 < N -- family number is positive

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.potential
declarations.doc: The Pöschl-Teller potential is `-(ℏ^2 * κ^2 * N * (N + 1)) / (2 * m * (cosh (κ * x)) ^ 2)`. -
declarations.statement: def potential (x : Space 1) : ℝ

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.depth
declarations.doc:
The depth `ℏ^2 * κ^2 * N * (N + 1) / (2 * m)` of the potential well, so that

declarations.statement: def depth : ℝ

declarations.statement: lemma depth_pos : 0 < Q.depth

declarations.doc: The potential in terms of the depth, `potential x = -depth / cosh (κ * x) ^ 2`.
declarations.statement: lemma potential_eq (x : Space 1) : Q.potential x = -Q.depth / Real.cosh (Q.κ * x 0) ^ 2

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.potential_eq_tanh

declarations.statement:
lemma potential_eq_tanh (x : Space 1) :
    Q.potential x = -Q.depth * (1 - Real.tanh (Q.κ * x 0) ^ 2)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.potential_neg

declarations.statement: lemma potential_neg (x : Space 1) : Q.potential x < 0

declarations.statement: lemma potential_neg_eq (x : Space 1) : Q.potential (-x) = Q.potential x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.toSpaceDQuantumSystem_kineticCLM_apply

    Q.toSpaceDQuantumSystem.kineticCLM ψ = (2 * Q.m)⁻¹ • momentumCLM 0 (momentumCLM 0 ψ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.toSpaceDQuantumSystem_hamiltonianCLM_apply
declarations.doc: The pointwise action of the Hamiltonian on a Schwartz function.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.tanhCLM
declarations.doc: Pointwise multiplication of Schwartz maps by `tanh(κx)`.
declarations.statement: def tanhCLM : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.tanhCLM_apply
declarations.doc: Multiplication by `tanh (κ * x)` acts pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma tanhCLM_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)) (x : Space 1) :
    Q.tanhCLM ψ x = Real.tanh (Q.κ * x 0) • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.creationCLM
declarations.doc: The creation operator, `1/√(2m) (P + iℏκ tanh(κX))`
declarations.statement: def creationCLM : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.annihilationCLM
declarations.doc: The annihilation operator, `1/√(2m) (P - iℏκ tanh(κX))`
declarations.statement: def annihilationCLM : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.creationCLM_apply
declarations.doc: The pointwise action of the creation operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma creationCLM_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)) (x : Space 1) :
    Q.creationCLM ψ x = (1 / √(2 * Q.m)) • momentumCLM 0 ψ x
      + (I * ℏ * Q.κ / √(2 * Q.m)) * (Real.tanh (Q.κ * x 0) • ψ x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.annihilationCLM_apply
declarations.doc: The pointwise action of the annihilation operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma annihilationCLM_apply (ψ : 𝓢(Space 1, ℂ)) (x : Space 1) :
    Q.annihilationCLM ψ x = (1 / √(2 * Q.m)) • momentumCLM 0 ψ x
      + (-I * ℏ * Q.κ / √(2 * Q.m)) * (Real.tanh (Q.κ * x 0) • ψ x)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.creationCLM_add_annihilationCLM
declarations.doc: The sum of the ladder operators is `(2 / √(2m)) 𝐩`.
declarations.statement:
lemma creationCLM_add_annihilationCLM :
    Q.creationCLM + Q.annihilationCLM = (2 / √(2 * Q.m)) • momentumCLM 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.creationCLM_sub_annihilationCLM
declarations.doc: The difference of the ladder operators is `(2 i ℏ κ / √(2m)) tanh (κ X)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma creationCLM_sub_annihilationCLM :
    Q.creationCLM - Q.annihilationCLM = (2 * I * ℏ * Q.κ / √(2 * Q.m)) • Q.tanhCLM
