modules.title: Scattering states of the 1d Pöschl-Teller system
modules.doc:
The polynomials describing the scattering states of the Pöschl-Teller system.

## i. Overview

At energy `E = ℏ² k² / (2 m)` the scattering states of the Pöschl-Teller system are of the form
`ψₖ(x) = Pₖ(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`, where the polynomial `Pₖ` is obtained by applying the
operators `-∂ₓ + n κ tanh (κ x)`, for `n = 1, …, N`, to the plane wave `e^{i k x}`. The operator
`-∂ₓ + n κ tanh (κ x)` intertwines the Hamiltonians of the Pöschl-Teller systems with family
numbers `n - 1` and `n`, so it maps solutions of the one to solutions of the other at the same
energy.

This file works with the polynomial in `tanh (κ x)` multiplying `e^{i k x}`, as an element of
`ℂ[X]`. The derivative, the raising operators and the Hamiltonian become operators on `ℂ[X]`, and
the intertwining relation becomes an identity of polynomials.

## ii. Key results

- `polyReducedHamiltonian_polyRaise` : the raising operator intertwines the Hamiltonians with family
  numbers `n` and `n + 1`.
- `polyReducedHamiltonian_polyScattering` : the scattering polynomial `Pₖ` is an eigenvector of the
  reduced Hamiltonian with eigenvalue `k²`.
- `polyScattering_eval_one`, `polyScattering_eval_neg_one` : the values `Pₖ(1) = ∏ₙ (n κ - i k)`
  and `Pₖ(-1) = ∏ₙ (-n κ - i k)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Polynomials in `tanh (κ x)`
  - A.1. Derivative, raising operator and Hamiltonian
  - A.2. The intertwining relation
  - A.3. The scattering polynomials
  - A.4. Values at `±1`

## iv. References

* https://arxiv.org/pdf/2411.14941. [ref: arxiv_2411_14941]

sections.text: ### A.1. Derivative, raising operator and Hamiltonian

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative acting on the polynomial of a wave `p(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`,
`p ↦ κ (1 - X²) p' + i k p`, so that
`∂ₓ (p(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}) = (polyDeriv k p)(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`.
declarations.statement: def polyDeriv (k : ℝ) (p : ℂ[X]) : ℂ[X]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyRaise
declarations.doc:
The raising operator `-∂ₓ + n κ tanh (κ x)` acting on the polynomial of a wave
`p(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`.
declarations.statement: def polyRaise (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) : ℂ[X]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyReducedHamiltonian
declarations.doc:
The operator `-∂ₓ² - n (n + 1) κ² / cosh² (κ x)` acting on the polynomial of a wave
`p(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`. This is `2 m / ℏ²` times the Hamiltonian of the Pöschl-Teller system
with family number `n`.
declarations.statement: def polyReducedHamiltonian (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) : ℂ[X]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyReducedHamiltonian_polyRaise
declarations.doc: The raising operator intertwines the Hamiltonians with family numbers `n` and `n + 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyReducedHamiltonian_polyRaise (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    Q.polyReducedHamiltonian k (n + 1) (Q.polyRaise k (n + 1) p) =
      Q.polyRaise k (n + 1) (Q.polyReducedHamiltonian k n p)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyDeriv_C
declarations.doc: The derivative of a constant multiple of the plane wave `c e^{i k x}` is `i k c e^{i k x}`.
declarations.statement: lemma polyDeriv_C (k : ℝ) (c : ℂ) : Q.polyDeriv k (C c) = C (k * I * c)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyRaise_C_mul
declarations.doc: The raising operator is linear with respect to constant multiples.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyRaise_C_mul (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (c : ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    Q.polyRaise k n (C c * p) = C c * Q.polyRaise k n p

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyScattering
declarations.doc:
The polynomial `Pₖ` of the scattering state `Pₖ(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}` of the Pöschl-Teller
system with family number `n`, obtained by applying the raising operators with
`1, …, n` to `1`.
declarations.statement: def polyScattering (k : ℝ) : ℕ → ℂ[X]

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyReducedHamiltonian_polyScattering
declarations.doc:
The scattering polynomial with family number `n` is an eigenvector of the reduced Hamiltonian
with eigenvalue `k²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyReducedHamiltonian_polyScattering (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    Q.polyReducedHamiltonian k n (Q.polyScattering k n) =
      C ((k : ℂ) ^ 2) * Q.polyScattering k n

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.eval_one_polyRaise
declarations.doc: At `tanh (κ x) = 1` the raising operator acts as multiplication by `n κ - i k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_one_polyRaise (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    (Q.polyRaise k n p).eval 1 = (n * Q.κ - k * I) * p.eval 1

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.eval_neg_one_polyRaise
declarations.doc: At `tanh (κ x) = -1` the raising operator acts as multiplication by `-n κ - i k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_neg_one_polyRaise (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    (Q.polyRaise k n p).eval (-1) = (-(n * Q.κ) - k * I) * p.eval (-1)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyScattering_eval_one
declarations.doc: The value at `1` of the scattering polynomial is `∏ₙ (n κ - i k)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyScattering_eval_one (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (Q.polyScattering k n).eval 1 = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range n, ((j + 1) * Q.κ - k * I)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyScattering_eval_neg_one
declarations.doc: The value at `-1` of the scattering polynomial is `∏ₙ (-n κ - i k)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyScattering_eval_neg_one (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (Q.polyScattering k n).eval (-1) = ∏ j ∈ Finset.range n, (-((j + 1) * Q.κ) - k * I)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyScattering_eval_one_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The value at `1` of the scattering polynomial is non-zero.
declarations.statement: lemma polyScattering_eval_one_ne_zero (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : (Q.polyScattering k n).eval 1 ≠ 0

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.PoschlTeller.polyScattering_eval_neg_one_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The value at `-1` of the scattering polynomial is non-zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyScattering_eval_neg_one_ne_zero (k : ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
    (Q.polyScattering k n).eval (-1) ≠ 0

modules.title: Quantum system
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In non-relativistic quantum mechanics a quantum system is characterized by a Hilbert space
(complete inner product space) and self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator; these data are collected in
the `QuantumSystem` structure.

Two quantum systems are said to be "unitary equivalent" if there is a unitary bijection between
their respective Hilbert spaces which sends one Hamiltonian to the other under conjugation.
Unitary equivalent quantum systems are physically indestinguishable, as all operators, states,
matrix elements, probabilities, eigenvalues, etc. are in 1-1 correspondence.

## ii. Key results

Definitions
- `QuantumSystem` : Structure bundling together a choice of Hilbert space
    and self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator.
- `UnitaryRelation` : The unitary equivalence relation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition
- B. Creation from an essentially self-adjoint operator
- C. Zero
- D. Unitary equivalence

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## B. Creation from an essentially self-adjoint operator

An essentially self-adjoint operator has a unique self-adjoint extension
(c.f. `IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint.unique_self_adjoint_extension`).
For this reason, a quantum system can be uniquely associated to an e.s.a. Hamiltonian operator.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem
declarations.doc: A quantum system is identified by its Hilbert space and self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator.
declarations.statement:
structure QuantumSystem where
  /-- The complex Hilbert space. -/
  HS : Type*
  /-- The Hilbert space is a normed, commutative group. -/
  [instNormed : NormedAddCommGroup HS]
  /-- The Hilbert space is a complex inner product space. -/
  [instInner : InnerProductSpace ℂ HS]
  /-- The Hilbert space is complete. -/
  [instComplete : CompleteSpace HS]
  /-- The self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator. -/
  ℋ : HS →ₗ.[ℂ] HS
  ℋ_self_adjoint : IsSelfAdjoint ℋ
instance (Q : QuantumSystem) : NormedAddCommGroup Q.HS
instance (Q : QuantumSystem) : InnerProductSpace ℂ Q.HS
instance (Q : QuantumSystem) : CompleteSpace Q.HS

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.mkESA
declarations.doc:
Create a quantum system from a Hamiltonian operator which is merely
essentially self-adjoint by taking its closure.
declarations.statement:
def mkESA {HS : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup HS] [InnerProductSpace ℂ HS] [CompleteSpace HS]
    {ℋ : HS →ₗ.[ℂ] HS} (hℋ : IsEssentiallySelfAdjoint ℋ) : QuantumSystem

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.instZero
declarations.statement: instance instZero : Zero QuantumSystem

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.UnitaryRelation
declarations.doc:
The relation on quantum systems where `Q₁` is related to `Q₂` if there exists a linear isometry
equivalence `e : Q₁.HS ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] Q₂.HS` between the respective Hilbert spaces satisfying
`e ∘ Q₁.ℋ ∘ e.symm = Q₂.ℋ`.
declarations.statement: def UnitaryRelation (Q₁ Q₂ : QuantumSystem) : Prop

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.unitaryRelation_refl
declarations.doc: The relation `UnitaryRelation` is reflexive.
declarations.statement: lemma unitaryRelation_refl (Q : QuantumSystem) : UnitaryRelation Q Q

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.unitaryRelation_symm
declarations.doc: The relation `UnitaryRelation` is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryRelation_symm {Q₁ Q₂ : QuantumSystem} (h₁₂ : UnitaryRelation Q₁ Q₂) :
    UnitaryRelation Q₂ Q₁

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.unitaryRelation_trans
declarations.doc: The relation `UnitaryRelation` is transitive.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitaryRelation_trans {Q₁ Q₂ Q₃ : QuantumSystem} (h₁₂ : UnitaryRelation Q₁ Q₂)
    (h₂₃ : UnitaryRelation Q₂ Q₃) : UnitaryRelation Q₁ Q₃

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.unitaryRelation_equiv
declarations.doc: The relation `UnitaryRelation` is an equivalence relation.
declarations.statement: lemma unitaryRelation_equiv : Equivalence UnitaryRelation

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.QuantumSystem.QuantumSystemSetoid
declarations.doc: The setoid of quantum systems with `UnitaryRelation` for equivalence relation.
declarations.statement: instance QuantumSystemSetoid : Setoid QuantumSystem

modules.title: The rectangular potential barrier
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The rectangular potential barrier in one dimension provides the simplest example of quantum
tunnelling. A particle of mass `m` is subject to a piece-wise constant potential which is `V₀`
on a closed interval and zero elsewhere.

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic properties
- B. Potential function
- C. Hilbert space
- D. Operators
  - D.1. Kinetic
  - D.2. Potential
  - D.3. Hamiltonian
- E. As a quantum system

## iv. References

* None.

A quantum particle with mass `m > 0` on `Space 1` subject to a rectangular potential barrier.

The potential is `V₀` on the interval `Icc lower upper` and zero elsewhere.

  /-- The upper bound of the barrier. -/
  upper : ℝ
  h_bounds : lower < upper
  /-- The height of the potential barrier. -/

modules.title: Single-particle quantum system on `Space d`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we introduce the general notion of a single-particle quantum system on `Space d`.

The structure `SpaceDQuantumSystem` encompasses the basic information needed to specify the system,
namely the number of spatial dimensions, the particle's mass and the potential function.

## ii. Key results

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic properties
- B. Operators
  - B.1. Kinetic energy
  - B.2. Potential energy
  - B.3. Hamiltonian

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDQuantumSystem
declarations.doc:
A single-particle quantum system with Hilbert space `SpaceDHilbertSpace d`,
characterized by the particle's mass `m > 0` and potential function `potential : Space d → ℝ`.
declarations.statement:
structure SpaceDQuantumSystem (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The mass (positive). -/
  m : ℝ
  hm : 0 < m
  /-- The potential function. -/

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDQuantumSystem.potentialCLM
declarations.doc:
The potential operator as a continuous linear map on Schwartz space,
where `Q.potential` is a function of temperate growth.
declarations.statement: def potentialCLM : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ) →L[ℂ] 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDQuantumSystem.potentialCLM_eq
declarations.statement: lemma potentialCLM_eq : Q.potentialCLM = smulLeftCLM ℂ (ofReal ∘ Q.potential)

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDQuantumSystem.potentialCLM_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialCLM_apply (h_HTG : Q.potential.HasTemperateGrowth) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) :
    Q.potentialCLM ψ = fun x ↦ Q.potential x • ψ x

declarations.name: QuantumMechanics.SpaceDQuantumSystem.potentialCLM_apply_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma potentialCLM_apply_apply
    (h_HTG : Q.potential.HasTemperateGrowth) (ψ : 𝓢(Space d, ℂ)) (x : Space d) :
    Q.potentialCLM ψ x = Q.potential x • ψ x

declarations.statement: lemma potentialOperator_eq : Q.potentialOperator = 𝓜 volume (ofReal ∘ Q.potential)
